Merge pull request #122025 from NousResearch/fix/bootstrap-no-stale-script

fix(bootstrap-installer): never use a cached install script

fix(install): don't ask the gateway install questions twice

The setup stage installs the gateway service through
ensure_gateway_service. On Windows that asks the start-now, Scheduled
Task and UAC questions. The gateway stage then ran `hermes gateway
install`, which asked them all again.

`gateway install --if-missing` does nothing when a service is already
installed. Both installers' gateway stages use it, so they ask only
when setup did not install the service.

fix(desktop-update): give Windows update steps NUL stdin, not the hand-off console

Steps inherited the hand-off console's stdin, so any step that asks a
question blocked forever. Its prompt went to the captured stdout, which
is shown only after the step exits. `gateway start --all` did exactly
this: it saw an interactive console and asked "Install it now so the
gateway starts on login?". The update stopped after `hermes update exit
code: 0` and never relaunched the app.

Steps now read NUL. Prompts see a non-interactive stdin and take their
defaults. The working-directory self-test also checks that a step's
stdin is not a console, and a new test runs it under a real console.

fix(pm): a lazily installed extra swaps into the running process

ensure_import synced the extra into a new generation and then always
raised "restart Hermes to activate", so choosing a provider whose SDK is an
opt-in extra (anthropic, bedrock, ...) failed the first message in every
fresh install or worktree even though the install had succeeded.

adopt_selected() already knows when swapping a live process onto a new
generation is safe (it was on the generation selected before the sync, and
nothing it imported changed version). Call it after the sync; raise only
when adoption was refused, naming restart_needed()'s reason.

Merge pull request #122227 from NousResearch/fix/windows-tests-after-legacy-venv

test: stop relying on the in-tree venv after #122161

feat(pm): say when this process must restart to load the selected generation

A process that could not adopt a newly published dependency generation keeps
importing the old one. restart_needed() names that case (and stays silent for
dev venvs, Nix and anything not booted from a PM generation, so no false
restart prompts); adopt_selected() lets callers move onto the selection before
loading new code. The test helpers publish real generations and make the test
process run from one.

(cherry picked from commit 978abe8ec4b852778b8c63bcefdf141db51bc703)
(cherry picked from commit 28be27334adc531db59bf37a02a64acaaf47a2ee)

feat(pm): adopt a newly selected generation inside the running process

After a plugin's runtime request is published, the process that asked should be
able to import the result without a restart, but only when nothing it already
loaded would change underneath it. Adopt when this process was on the
generation that was selected when the build started, and no loaded module's
file appears in the RECORD of a distribution whose version changed or
disappeared. Adopting swaps the site-packages entry, processes only the new
generation's new .pth files, rewrites PYTHONPATH/PATH for child processes, and
leases the new generation while keeping the old lease, since loaded packages
still resolve submodules from it.

(cherry picked from commit 478f945d9f36e94229f58b251642b7c9f3b9e781)

test: stop relying on the in-tree venv after #122161

PR #122161 stopped boot from activating the in-tree venv or .venv when
PM has committed no environment. Six Linux tests and four Windows tests
still used that tree to supply their probe modules.

- Launcher tests put the probe in a committed generation. A custom
  HERMES_HOME is its own dependency root, so it gets its own commit.
- The legacy row of test_pre_pm_base_dependencies_activate_only_at_boot
  asserted the removed behavior. test_boot_never_activates_the_pre_pm_venv
  now covers the inverse. The payload row stays.
- The mint payload fixture writes manifest.json as real payloads do, so
  boot selects the payload venv.
- The PowerShell activate test expects PYTHONPATH to be the checkout
  alone. The bootstrap .venv packages do not leak in.

fix(providers): report why a lazy SDK install did not land

_get_anthropic_sdk() swallowed every ensure_import("anthropic") failure and
_require_sdk() then told the user to "Install it with: hermes pm install
--extra anthropic". PM often HAS installed it: sync_venv succeeds into a new
dependency environment that only activates at process boot, and
ensure_import raises "installed; restart Hermes". A lazy-install guard
("this process is not running from the install's dependency environment")
was flattened the same way. Users were told to install something that was
installed, or given a command that doesn't address the actual refusal.

Keep the import as the decider, but remember the InstallError and put its
text in the ImportError. bedrock_adapter._require_boto3 had the identical
shape; azure_identity_adapter already propagates str(exc) and is the model.

Merge pull request #122161 from NousResearch/fix/never-activate-legacy-venv

PM never activates the pre-PM in-tree venv (gateway lost pydantic_core after update)

fix(update): key the early-spawn sync on currency, not on a commit

Under the updater's claim, sync whenever dependencies are not current
rather than only when nothing is committed. The tail's own children
and post-sync verification children are current and stay no-ops. A
stale generation still committed from the previous Python pin is the
same ABI trap as the pre-PM venv, and it now syncs too. If the sync
still leaves the tree out of date, raise instead of relaunching into
another sync.

fix(update): commit dependencies for processes the update spawns early

prepare_launch returned early for any process running under the
updater's own claim, so it would not re-run the completion tail. That
also covered processes the updater spawns before PM commits a
generation (a restarted gateway), which then booted with no
environment: previously on the pre-PM venv, now refused.

Under the updater's claim with nothing committed, sync the dependency
generation (carrying the legacy venv's extras, as the first sync
always has), skip the tail since that belongs to the updater, and
relaunch on the store Python. The relaunched process sees the commit
and returns early as before, so the no-recursion guard still holds.

fix(pm): never activate the pre-PM in-tree venv

With nothing committed, activate_dependencies fell back to the in-tree
venv/.venv. After an update that venv was built for the old interpreter
(uv CPython 3.11) while the process ran PM's store Python 3.14, so every
compiled module in it was unloadable: the messaging gateway's Group Chat
worker died on `No module named 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core'` until PM
committed a generation ~40 minutes later and deleted the old venv.

committed_venv() returns the committed generation or a sealed payload's
environment, never the in-tree venv. Boot activation and child
activation environments use it. With nothing committed, a venv/Nix
interpreter keeps its own packages; PM's bare store Python refuses with
the repair remedy instead of running on inherited paths. selected_venv
keeps its contract because pre-PM updaters import it after the swap.

fix(release): pass the executable path to PowerShell via the environment

powershell -Command joins trailing argv into the script text, so $args
was never populated and the path became a stray token (ParserError).
An env var needs no quoting.
fix(desktop): keep slow plugin installs from reporting false failure (#121856)

Merge pull request #122136 from NousResearch/fix/desktop-post-update-backend-start

Desktop no longer fails to start after an update (dead backend record wedged boot)

fix(desktop): stop waiting 45s on a dead backend record after an update

A hard-killed backend leaves its spawn-ledger record and its published
session token behind. Since the attach path started adopting published
tokens (f1247d2e01), such a record passed the token rung and then had its
refused port polled for the whole 45s readiness budget. The renderer's boot
timeout is the same 45s and starts first, so it gave up just before main
fell through to spawning, and every Retry/Repair killed the fresh backend
and produced another dead record: the app never started after an update.

A ledger record is written only after its backend binds, so a refused
connection on one means the process is gone. Readiness gains an opt-in
`alreadyBound` that fails at once on ECONNREFUSED; the attach probe and the
attached-backend liveness monitor set it. Remote/SSH readiness keeps
polling, since a tunnel still coming up refuses legitimately.

Merge pull request #122101 from NousResearch/fix/record-msix-executable

fix(release): Windows release builds no longer fail recording the executable version

fix(desktop): open markdown preview links inside the app

Electron denies every target=_blank window, so a web link in a previewed
.md file looked clickable and did nothing; a #fragment link rode the
HashRouter and changed the app route instead of scrolling the note; a
relative link to a sibling note never opened it.

Links now take the same doors chat links take: web links render through
ExternalLink (in-app browser, Cmd/Ctrl for native), file links are wrapped
in the existing #preview/ hash before Streamdown's hardener sees them and
resolved against the note's directory by normalizeOrLocalPreviewTarget,
and headings get GitHub-style ids from a rehype plugin so a TOC click
scrolls within the pane. Slugs and lookups are NFC-normalized so a TOC
written on another editor still finds its heading.

Fixes #81055
Co-authored-by: xxxigm <tuancanhnguyen706@gmail.com>

fix(desktop): collapse ../ in the renderer preview path fallback

A note linking ../other.md resolved to /notes/../other.md when the Electron
normalizer is unavailable, a path the fs bridge then rejects.

docs(pm): note why tool.uv.package = true makes a member buildable

Review suggestion from #122098: spell out on the condition line that
uv package mode produces real build metadata, so such members keep
their declared name.

Merge pull request #122095 from NousResearch/fix/desktop-ismain-eval

fix(desktop): isMain returns false when there is no entry script

fix(release): read the Windows executable name from the MSIX manifest

record() looked up stamp['identity']['windowsExecutableName'], a key no
stamp writer emits, so every Windows record on a runner resolved no
executable and failed. The built package's Application/@Executable
names the exe; match it in the unpacked dir only, which also skips
before-pack's .bak rollback copy.

fix(pm): name virtual workspace members by their unique key

uv identifies a workspace member by its declared project name, so the
same plugin enabled in two profiles declares one name twice and the
dependency sync fails with 'Two workspace members are both named ...'.
Metadata-only members (no build backend) now carry the unique member
key in their name, exactly like manifest-only members already do. A
buildable member keeps the name it declares, since uv verifies it
against the package metadata its backend produces.

fix(desktop): treat a missing plugin-decision door as bot mode on

Other plugin tests mock host without that door. A missing read is the
default, not a crash.

fix(desktop): read bot-mode state through the plugin SDK

Plugins cannot import the contrib store. host.pluginDecisions is the
read-only door, and absence still means the plugin default.

fix(desktop): do not dial the bot relay drain with nothing to deliver

The 30s drain opened a throwaway gateway socket even when Bot Mode was off or the route had no outbox work. With the push door, only a route that signaled bot_relay.outbox.pending is drained. Older shells without that door still poll. The background-scope reset from #119836 is unchanged.

fix(desktop): isMain returns false when there is no entry script

Importing a script from `node -e` leaves process.argv[1] undefined, and
pathToFileURL(undefined) throws on import. The bootstrap installer's
signing step imports batch-sign-binaries.mjs this way, and it crashed
when that pulled in sanitize-pe-signatures.mjs.

fix(desktop): publish pending clarify before transcript hydration

An authoritative still-pending clarify was answerable only after
getLatestSessionMessages returned. Publish the snapshot tool-call row
in the same needsInput view update, and keep provenance checks from
hiding that row.

fix(pm): make the staged agent-browser binary executable

The npm tarball ships every bin/agent-browser-* as 0644; agent-browser's
own postinstall sets the exec bit, and pm runs no postinstall. The first
browser_navigate auto-installs agent-browser and then fails with
PermissionError.
fix(desktop): decode fetched link metadata by charset

fix(desktop): route omitted-profile messaging approvals to the list server

A Telegram row that omits profile is owned by the backend that served
the messaging list. Keep a non-primary connection id, send a primary-pool
list through that profile door, and do not guess primary or ambient when
the list server was never recorded.

fix(desktop): settle a silent live turn and offer retry

A dead or interrupted turn left the thinking spinner up, including after
a partial assistant payload. When that session stops producing events,
force-settle it and stamp the existing retryable error card instead of
leaving the spinner spinning.

fix(desktop): Enter on a focused clarify choice reaches activateActive

Clicking a single-select choice leaves focus on the option button, and the
window keydown handler bailed for every button, so Enter never submitted the
staged answer. Exempt button[data-choice] and let activateActive handle Enter:
a staged single-select answer submits, a multi-select row toggles, and Continue
still confirms the set. Choice buttons do not call submitAnswer.

Fixes #92816

Co-authored-by: echohn <echohn@gmail.com>

fix(desktop): scope the config-record cache to the active gateway

The shared ['hermes-config-record'] slot survived a gateway switch, so a
settings save painted the previous machine's record and PUT it onto the
other config.yaml. Key that existing slot by $activeConnectionId.

Fixes #101640

fix(desktop): defer tray hide and log main-process stalls

Hiding inside the minimize handler wedges the Windows minimized flag, and
showInactive() restores a painted window that never takes input. Defer hide
until after that dispatch, skip a stale hide if the user already restored,
and activate with show()+focus() on Windows. Log main-process event-loop
stalls in desktop.log; renderer unresponsive handlers cannot see AppHangB1.

Reported in #119252.

Co-authored-by: finn763 <165816600+finn763@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: KoNit-K <konit.block@protonmail.com>

fix(desktop): speak each assistant turn once across id rewrite

Auto-speak keyed already-spoken on the assistant row id and ordinal.
Hydration rewrites the live id and tool-row folds move that ordinal, so
the same turn looked unspoken and was played again. A second
playSpeechText stopped the first clip. markSpoken also ran before a play
that never started, so the turn stayed silent.

Key the anchor on the user turn, which survives both. A later turn that
says the same thing is still spoken. Release the anchor when playback
never starts, and do not let a second start of the same turn stop the first.

fix(desktop): refuse remote-only profile spawns when the connection id is missing

An empty connection id is no longer rewritten to registry.primary, which dialed
another SSH host. A concrete remote-only profile, including default, is refused
on the forced-local branch instead of spawned. A profile open without an owner
route no longer stamps mode local when the live connection is remote.

fix(desktop): refresh peer windows and refuse a stale multi-window submit (#65047)

A second Desktop window on the same stored session never saw the first
window's completed turn, and submitting from that stale transcript could
fork the session. Notify other windows to re-pull on turn completion, and
refuse composer and session-tile submit when the local transcript is behind
the authoritative latest page.

Co-authored-by: stantheman0128 <stanshih888@gmail.com>

fix(proxy): send a real error event when a /v1/messages stream fails (#41826)

* fix(proxy): send a real error event when a /v1/messages stream fails

When a stream failed halfway through, the proxy wrote the error as a plain
`data: {"error": ...}` line with no `event:` in front of it. Anthropic clients
pick stream events by that name, so they skip the line and the request looks
like it simply stopped with nothing in it.

Write the failure as an `event: error` frame with Anthropic's own payload, and
take the error type from the status code

* fix(proxy): use the shared Anthropic error mapping for the stream error frame

The first pass added a third copy of the status to error-type table, and it
disagreed with the documented one: 529 came out as `api_error` rather than
`overloaded_error`, and 413 as `invalid_request_error` rather than
`request_too_large`, which hides the two failures a client can actually act on.

Drop that copy and put the frame builder next to the table litellm already
keeps in anthropic_interface/exceptions. The bridged adapter path was building
the same frame inline, so it uses the shared one now too

* fix(proxy): seal a torn SSE frame before the /v1/messages error event

An upstream that drops mid-frame leaves the client inside an open event,
so the error frame that follows is glued onto the torn data line and the
Anthropic SDK raises a JSON decode error instead of an APIStatusError.
Close the open frame with a ping event the SDK skips before writing the
error event, and add the e2e stream-cut edge with Bedrock, Anthropic
boundary, and Anthropic mid-frame legs.

* fix(proxy): keep the SSE tail unchanged on a chunk that is not text

A serializer that hands a dict or model object through as-is has no bytes
the frame tail can learn from, so advance_sse_tail leaves it alone instead
of slicing it.

* fix(proxy): answer a /v1/messages stream that fails before its first byte as a JSON error carrying its status

* test: move the Anthropic error frame tests into tests/unit

* test(e2e): cut the upstream stream only after content has been relayed

* test(e2e): carry split SSE lines across chunks and always tear a data line mid-frame

* test(e2e): find the next data line across a chunk boundary before tearing it

fix(router): count provider budget spend on every API surface (#38172)

* fix(router): count provider budget spend on every API surface

RouterBudgetLimiting read custom_llm_provider from litellm_params, which only
chat completions populates. Responses, anthropic_messages, embedding and rerank
calls raised inside the success callback before any spend was recorded, so those
budgets never moved and a ceiling made up mostly of that traffic was never hit.

Read the provider from the standard logging payload, which every surface fills
in. Dropping the raise also stops one missing field from taking the deployment
and tag budgets down with it.

Move miniapp back-navigation state into the Miniapp SDK

The bundled miniapps imported a useHistoryState hook from miniapps/shared by

earlier history.go() is still landing waits for it. Previously, closing a
dialog and changing another value in the same tick pushed the new entry
before the pop landed, and the pop removed it instead of the dialog.

commits.message:
fix(ci): select runtime suites from PR changes only (#7843)

A documentation-only update to #7809 selected desktop builds and E2E
tests because path detection compared an old PR base SHA with GitHub's
newer synthetic merge commit. The [failing run's path-detection
log](https://github.com/block/buzz/actions/runs/35789957773/job/106955810630)
includes four unrelated desktop files from `main`; `VISION_MOBILE.md`
did not match a runtime filter.

Use GitHub's PR file list for pull requests so unrelated changes in the
synthetic merge commit cannot select runtime suites. The existing
directory filters are unchanged: root and docs/ Markdown do not select
runtime suites, while Markdown under runtime directories still selects
its affected suites. Mixed code/documentation changes retain normal
coverage. Always-on security, policy, and source-contract checks and
full push-to-main coverage are unchanged.

Added regression coverage runs the pinned paths-filter action against
real fixture repositories, including a synthetic merge containing
unrelated upstream desktop code. All 35 selection scenarios and 26
required-check scenarios pass; the new regressions failed before the
fix. Existing required-context isolation, file-size policy, and
security-review contract checks pass, as do script lint and workflow
syntax validation. Full workflow lint reports the same two pre-existing
shell-quoting findings in the untouched dead-token guard. A desktop E2E
build was run to diagnose the unrelated required smoke failure.

Related: #7809 (incident, unchanged) and #5756 (shared-input path
coverage, separate scope). No matching issue found.

PRs with at least 3,000 changed files now select every runtime suite,
avoiding GitHub's PR-file-list ceiling. Boundary tests cover 2,999,
3,000, and 3,001 files, including a runtime file omitted beyond the API
cap; disabling the safeguard makes the latter two regressions fail.

Required checks now run and fail when path selection fails, is
cancelled, or is skipped. Regression coverage exercises the workflow
conditions and shell checks for all 13 required wrappers, plus an
API-denial case against the pinned action. Mutating either the
scheduling guard or the result check makes all 13 failure regressions
fail.

The required mention-settings smoke test expected a pin after explicitly
disabling automatic mentions. Waiting for its old avatar to exit
reproduced the CI failure 3/3; the test now checks that subsequent
mentions remain manual and retains outgoing recipient-tag assertions.
Corrected browser regression: 20/20 repeated runs; related picker unit
tests: 18/18. No desktop production behavior changed. The always()
requirement is now pinned in required-wrapper regression tests; deleting
it fails all 26 gate cases.

---------

Signed-off-by: Tom Brow <tomb@block.xyz>

test(desktop): synchronize upload edit smoke test (#7903)

## Summary
Fix the upload/edit smoke-test race observed on main at
`6410e685a80d42db0645fadc9bbe710559ef911e`.

- Hold the mock upload at the Tauri IPC boundary and release it
explicitly after checking edit rejection, rather than assuming menu
interaction finishes within one second.
- Wait for the Radix menu to unmount: edit dispatch happens in
`onCloseAutoFocus`, after the click. Without that wait, the negative
assertion can pass before the edit callback actually runs.
- Keep the existing attachment-preservation and subsequent
successful-edit assertions. No production code or CI coverage is
changed.

## Evidence and scope
- [Main
failure](https://github.com/block/buzz/actions/runs/36189213149/job/108250341388):
`opening edit during an immediate photo upload preserves the draft`,
including an upload-progress timeout on retry.
- Investigated from #7791, which changes only `docs/nips/NIP-AR.md`. Its
PostgreSQL failures and video-menu timeout are separate; PostgreSQL
passed on this main run, and the video spec passed locally. This PR does
not claim to fix those failures or the separate pointer-interception
failure seen in the main job.
- #7843 already addresses unrelated runtime suites being selected for
docs-only PRs.

## Validation
- Full desktop `pnpm test`: 6,676 Node tests + 92 jsdom tests passed.
- Upload/edit regression repeated 5 times: passed. Holding the upload
without waiting for menu teardown failed all 5 runs, demonstrating the
second race.
- Complete file-attachment and video-attachment Playwright specs: 30
passed.
- Pre-push desktop lint, typecheck, full desktop tests, and file-size
gate passed at `46e3d4392e5b56dcb74ea864aa19aa10287f27d3`.
- `just ci` attempted: initial formatting issue corrected; second run
exceeded the 5-minute local limit during Tauri clippy. Not claiming full
repository CI green.

## Review / human verification
Self-reviewed the diff against the test contract; no production behavior
changes. Draft pending human verification and CI.

To verify: activate Hermit, then `cd desktop && pnpm test:e2e:smoke
file-attachment.spec.ts --grep "opening edit during" --repeat-each=5`.
Expect all five runs to pass, retaining the upload in the draft and
allowing edit only after upload release.

feat(relay): enforce NIP-FI assertion+NIP-98 pairing on HTTP ingress (#7264)

Implements NIP-FI HTTP ingress enforcement per the merged spec (PR
#7254). Every protected HTTP surface in enforce mode requires a valid
`Nostr-Federated-Identity: Bearer <JWS>` assertion alongside its NIP-98
authorization, bound to the same key. The NIP-98 pubkey (proven actor)
must equal the assertion's `nostr_pubkey`; absent, mismatched, or
unverifiable assertions are denied fail-closed with byte-exact
text/plain responses per the spec's rejection table.

This is S5 of the `buzz-enterprise-identity` program. WS enforcement
(S3) is separate.

## What changed

**New `nip_fi_http` module:** `admit_nip_fi_http()` covers the full
admission sequence — `Nostr-Federated-Identity` extraction, offline JWKS
verification, NIP-98 key pairing [FI-INV-05], issuer-qualified deny-map
check via `(iss, pubkey, now)` [FI-INV-14], and byte-exact denial for
all four `DenialClass` variants. `admit_nip_fi_http_on_state()` is the
single call-site wrapper for all surfaces [FI-TRACE-AUTHORITY-UNIFORM].

**Protected surfaces** (all gated via the uniform authority):
- HTTP bridge: `POST /events`, `/query`, `/count`
- GIF proxy: `POST /gifs/search`, `/gifs/share`
- Workflow reads: `GET /workflows/{id}/runs`, `GET
/workflows/{id}/runs/{id}/approvals`
- Moderation reads: `GET /moderation/reports`, `/moderation/audit`,
`/moderation/restricted`
- Media/Blossom: `PUT /upload`, `/media/upload`
- Git smart-HTTP: `info/refs`, `upload-pack`, `receive-pack`
- Git settings control plane: `GET`/`POST
/git/:owner/:repo/default-branch` (now routed through
`admit_nip_fi_http_on_state` for full assertion key-pairing)
- Invites: `POST /api/invites` (mint only; claim exempt as
pre-membership enrollment door)

**NIP-98 strictness in NIP-FI mode:**
- When NIP-FI is not Off, bridge POST handlers force `require_auth_token
= true` — the `X-Pubkey` dev-mode fallback cannot satisfy the pairing
requirement [NIP-FI.md:547-567]
- POST bodies on `/events`, `/query`, `/count` require a matching
`payload` tag in enforce mode [NIP-FI.md:579-597]
- A payload tag present with no content (one-element `["payload"]` or
empty string) is rejected as a structurally invalid claim — NIP-98
requires the content to be a valid 64-char lowercase hex SHA-256 digest.
Malformed payload diagnostics use a static error message (no
attacker-controlled content in logs).
- Off mode preserves pre-NIP-FI behavior per [FI-INV-15]

**Off-mode compatibility changes:** Admission now runs before request
validation on every protected surface, so Off mode differs from
pre-NIP-FI behavior in these ways:
- **GIF routes:** NIP-98 authentication happens before the upstream
provider lookup. An unauthenticated request on a tenant with no GIF
provider now returns 401 instead of 404. The 401 goes through the legacy
`api_error()` path, so the body is JSON `{"error":"..."}` with no
`WWW-Authenticate` header.
- **Workflow runs** (`GET /workflows/{id}/runs`): the query string is
parsed after admission. A request with a missing credential and a
malformed query (for example `?limit=abc`) now returns 401 instead of
400.
- **Authorized malformed query:** once admitted, a malformed query
returns a JSON 400 `{"error":"invalid query: ..."}` from
`parse_query_or_400` instead of axum's `text/plain` `Query` rejection.
- **Moderation reads** (`/moderation/reports`, `/moderation/audit`):
same extraction change as workflow runs. Admission comes first, then a
JSON 400 for a malformed query.
- **Malformed `payload` tag:** shared NIP-98 verification now rejects a
malformed `payload` tag in every mode, including on bodyless requests.
That means a one-element `["payload"]`, an empty digest, or anything
other than 64 lowercase hex characters. Before this change, a bodyless
request ignored the tag.

**Auth header cardinality:** Enforce mode rejects requests with more
than one `Authorization` header with 403 `evidence rejected\n`.
DenyProtected returns 503 `authorization unavailable\n` before this
check (and before NIP-98 or assertion verification) runs. The
cardinality gate is enforced at the NIP-FI admission boundary
(`admit_nip_fi_http`), not via legacy auth boolean flags, so it applies
uniformly to all Enforce-mode surfaces including Git. Off mode passes
through the first header value unchanged, preserving pre-NIP-FI behavior
[FI-INV-15].

**Denial-class remapping:** In Enforce mode, NIP-98
extraction/verification failures from the closure are mapped to the
appropriate `DenialClass`: `MissingEvidence` when no `Authorization`
header is present, `EvidenceRejected` when the header is present but
invalid. Off mode propagates legacy responses unchanged [FI-INV-15]; for
example, the Git missing-Authorization and wrong-scheme 401s keep their
legacy bytes with no `content-type` header.

**JWKS refresh scheduling:** The refresh timer's `*last` checkpoint is
set after the fetch completes, not from the pre-fetch timestamp,
preventing interval drift under network latency. The loop is extracted
to `nip_fi_jwks_refresh_loop` for unit-testability.

**Log hygiene [NIP-FI.md:777-779]:** Issuer identity is never written to
logs or error messages. All startup/refresh diagnostics use an ordinal
index (`issuer_index = N`). Config parse errors for malformed issuers
use classify()/line/column codes rather than raw config values.

**Admin SPA document routes:** `/reports`, `/reports/{id}`, and
`/feedback` are exempt from the NIP-FI assertion guard only on the admin
host (host-qualified via `is_admin_host`). These paths are not added to
the broad `NIP_FI_EXEMPT_PREFIXES` list — tenant hosts remain fully
protected.

**Deny-map seam (`HttpDenyMap` trait):** signature is `(issuer, pubkey,
now)` matching `NipFiDenyMap::is_denied` from S4 (PR #7265) so
integration is a one-liner. Stub is `AlwaysAdmitStubDenyMap` — named to
accurately describe stub-phase semantics (fail-open intentionally
pending S4).

**Route inventory:** every authenticated HTTP route is classified as
Protected or Exempt with justification. Documented in the F4 seam-test
comment in `bridge.rs`.

**Outer-guard tests:** `#[ignore = "requires Postgres"]` tests in
`bridge.rs` drive the full router (`build_router`) in Enforce mode with
valid NIP-98 but no `Nostr-Federated-Identity` header. These exercise
the **outer `nip_fi_assertion_guard` middleware** in `router.rs` — the
layer that fires before any handler runs. They prove the guard's exact
response bytes (401 `authentication required\n`, `text/plain;
charset=utf-8`, `WWW-Authenticate: Nostr`) for each protected route.
Per-handler `admit_nip_fi_http_on_state` wiring is proven separately by
the cardinality test and the media/settings/git handler-level suites.

## Seams

**S3 seam:** `nip_fi_config.rs` is duplicated (S3 not landed;
session-deadline parts stripped). Removed when S5 rebases onto S3.

**S4 seam:** `AlwaysAdmitStubDenyMap` until S4 provides the real map.
Integration is one line at the `admit_nip_fi_http_on_state` wrapper.

🤖 docs: add pre-PR checklist and review guidance to AGENTS.md (#7897)

Adds a "Before opening a PR" checklist and "Reviewing" guidance to
`AGENTS.md`, and makes the Review-Proven Rules the shared reviewer
checklist.

PRs stay in draft until an agent review has run, an agent has exercised
the change on the affected surface, and a human has tested it. The
review-completed passphrase goes in the description only once that
checklist holds for the current change, and comes out if later edits
change behavior. Docs-only changes use the light path: content, link,
and diff checks plus human confirmation.

Reviews read `VISION.md` and the surface's `VISION_*.md` first, check
the change against the Review-Proven Rules, recommend blocking only for
concrete correctness, security, or contract defects with a realistic
failure, label everything else optional, and put all findings in the
first pass. Agents comment and never use Request Changes; humans decide
which findings must be fixed.

docs: specify durable data backfills (#7326)

## Why

Data backfills need a durable contract outside schema migrations. The
contract must survive crashes and support automatic or manual operation
without adding version-selection machinery.

## What

- Define one PostgreSQL-backed lifecycle for finite data repair
- Treat the stable backfill ID as the only durable execution and
readiness identity
- Use eventually consistent, idempotent registration; compatible workers
compete for one exclusive claim
- Require bounded batches, atomic mutation and checkpoint commits,
generation fencing, and validation before completion
- Define all four migration and automatic-backfill configurations
- Define the authorized admin API and honest client projection

## How

A backfill captures one immutable upper bound, processes finite batches,
and commits each target mutation with its checkpoint. PostgreSQL owns
lifecycle state, claims, progress, and completion.

Registration order and build metadata do not choose a definition.
Compatible processes are interchangeable. A material behavior change
requires a new stable ID. The orchestrator does not resolve different
behavior registered under one active ID. Diagnostic validation on
completed rows records only its bounded outcome and audit; it does not
create an execution claim.

The spec now starts with a six-step mental model and follows the
operator flow. It removes repeated requirements and cuts the document
from 614 lines and 4,835 words to 474 lines and 3,656 words.

## Risk

Low. This PR changes documentation only. It commits Buzz to a design
contract, but it does not add runtime, schema, configuration, or
protocol behavior.

## Testing

No manual runtime testing. A fresh full-spec review checked the
lifecycle, safety rules, four configuration cells, admin contract, and
production-seam conformance requirements. `git diff --check` and the
repository file-size policy pass at
`13681664674d4667b181a6211f012090fa40a2cf`.

## Bigger picture

The design keeps the relay as orchestrator, a focused backfill crate as
domain owner, and `buzz-db` as narrow transaction infrastructure. It
removes deployment generations and definition precedence from the
implementation plan.

test: share one settings lock across unit tests (#13644)

Unit tests in the `mise` crate that replace the process-wide settings
each had their own lock (`TEST_SETTINGS_LOCK` in node, ruby, swift and
task_script_parser, plus `IMPORT_TESTS` in daemons). About 50 more tests
called `Settings::reset` with no lock at all. With a lock per module, a
reset in one module could undo another module's override partway through
a test. Most of those tests also restored settings only on the happy
path, so a failed assertion leaked its override into later tests. This
is internal to the test suite; nothing changes for mise users.

This PR follows the pattern `mise-util` adopted in #13633 and adds one
crate-wide lock in `src/test.rs`:

- `test::SETTINGS_LOCK` is the one lock every settings-mutating test
takes.
- `test::SettingsGuard::lock()` holds it and runs
`Settings::reset(None)` on drop, before the lock is released and even
when the test panics.
- The per-module statics and their local guard structs are gone.
`task_script_parser`'s `tera_v1()` helper now returns the shared guard.
- The daemons `IMPORT_TESTS` lock is merged into it, since that lock was
really protecting the `paranoid` setting. `paranoid_on(&guard)` now
requires the caller to hold the guard.
- Tests in `install_before`, `backend`, `config`, `config::settings`,
`env_directive::file`, `shorthands` and `git` that called
`Settings::reset`/`override_with` without a lock now take the guard.
Their trailing `Settings::reset(None)` and git's manual backup/restore
are dropped because the guard does that on drop.
- Lock order: the settings guard is taken before any environment lock
(`env_directive::file`'s `ENV_MUTEX`). No other test takes both, so
there is no ordering cycle.

## Validation

- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D
warnings` and `mise run lint` pass.
- `mise run test:unit` fails the same tests with and without this
change. After merging current `main`: 4189 passed, 22 failed. On `main`
alone in this checkout, the failures are the same set. They all come
after an earlier test leaves the process in a deleted working directory
(`getcwd: cannot access parent directories`), which is unrelated to
settings.
- The suite normally runs one test at a time (`RUST_TEST_THREADS=1`,
nextest `test-threads = 1`), so the race needs parallel threads to show
up. Before merging `main`, I ran the settings-touching modules
(install_before, config::settings, node/ruby/swift, tera,
task_script_parser, daemons, shorthands, backend, env_directive::file,
git) 5 times each with `--test-threads=8`:
  - `main`: 10–13 failures per run
  - this PR: 2–4 failures per run

The remaining parallel failures come from a separate race that this lock
cannot close. `Settings::try_get` loads settings lazily and stores the
result. A test that only reads settings can store a snapshot taken
before a concurrent guarded test applied its override. Fixing that
belongs in `mise-settings`, not the test lock.

chore(release): refuse release prep when a workspace manifest is already dirty (#13632)

Release prep in `xtasks/release-plz` now runs `git add
crates/*/Cargo.toml`. That staging has to be broad, because bumping one
subcrate rewrites the version requirement in every workspace crate that
path-depends on it. The downside is that an edit already sitting in any
workspace manifest would be committed into `chore: release …` along with
the bump. Before this change, the per-crate `has_uncommitted_changes`
check only looked at the four subcrates it bumps, and `git status` only
printed the state, so nothing stopped that.

Release prep now checks `Cargo.toml` and `crates/*/Cargo.toml` before it
touches anything, and exits if either has uncommitted changes:

```
Workspace manifests have uncommitted changes before release prep:
 M crates/mise-util/Cargo.toml
```

The release workflow runs on a fresh checkout, so a normal release is
unaffected. Nothing between checkout and this point edits a manifest;
the publish branch exits before reaching it.

The original content of this PR (updating every workspace path
dependency on a subcrate bump, and staging every subcrate manifest)
already reached `main` through #13631. After merging `main`, this check
is all that is left in the diff.

**Validation:** `bash -n` passes. I ran the check against a clean tree,
a dirty `crates/mise-util/Cargo.toml` (blocked), and a dirty
non-manifest file under `crates/` (allowed).

feat(pypi): support #subdirectory= and .git-less URLs in git sources (#13607)

Python CLIs that live in a monorepo document installs like `pipx install
"git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui"`. The pypi
backend couldn't install that form. Now it can:

```toml
[tools]
"pypi:git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui" = "main"
"pypi:runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=jtui" = "main"   # GitHub shorthand works too
```

Discussed in #4595.

## Before / after

| Tool name | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui` | No
`.git`, so it was read as GitHub shorthand and failed with a 404 from
`api.github.com/repos/git+https://…/releases` | Installs
`git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui@main#subdirectory=ltui` |
| `git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui.git#subdirectory=ltui` |
Everything after `.git` dropped; installed the repository root |
Installs
`git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui.git@main#subdirectory=ltui` |
| `runpantheon/ltui@main#subdirectory=ltui` (fragment in the version,
the workaround from #4595) | Installs, but the version directory
contains `#`. uv writes that path into launcher shebangs, and macOS then
fails with `bad interpreter` | Unchanged. The docs now point to the
tool-name form |

## Behavior

- `git+<scheme>://…` is recognized with or without a trailing `.git`,
and the remote is used as written (so `git+file:///path/to/repo` works).
GitHub shorthand still gets `.git` added, as before.
- The `#…` fragment is kept and passed to uv/pipx. `subdirectory`,
`egg`, and any other keys pass through verbatim. The requested ref goes
before the fragment (`git+<remote>@<ref>#subdirectory=…`), as pip and uv
require. `[...]` in a tool name is still parsed as mise tool options, so
extras go in the `extras` option, not `#egg=pkg[extra]`.
- The fragment is part of the tool name, so sibling packages from one
repository are separate tools with separate install directories. mise's
tool directory name already strips `#`
(`pipx-runpantheon-ltui-subdirectory-jtui/main`), so launchers work.
- Version discovery uses only the repository. GitHub releases, `git
ls-remote` tags, and default-branch HEAD work as they do without a
fragment. `mise ls-remote` returns the same list for the fragment form
and for `pypi:runpantheon/ltui`.
- The venv's Python link is rewritten to the minor-version path (so
Python patch upgrades don't break the tool) by finding the venv under
the install path. Before, it guessed the venv name from the tool name,
which misses fragment tools and repos whose name differs from the
distribution name (ltui's `ltui/` builds `ltui-linear`).
- Extras: on the pipx path, `egg=<pkg>[extras]` is merged into the
existing fragment (one `#`). Without `package_name`, the distribution
name is now guessed from `egg`, then from the last segment of
`subdirectory`, and only then from the repository name.

Tool names that parsed before (all of which had `.git` or were
shorthand) produce the same install requests; regression tests pin the
existing strings.

## Limitation

`latest` still means the newest GitHub release of the whole repository.
If a repository's releases predate the subdirectory, as ltui's `v0.12.0`
does, `latest` fails with uv's error (``has no subdirectory `ltui` ``).
Pin a branch or commit instead. The docs describe this.

## Docs correction

`pypi.md` said GitHub `latest` installs from the default branch and does
not select the latest release. `ToolVersion::resolve_version` only falls
back to the default branch when the release list is empty. A dry run of
`pypi:psf/black` resolves to `26.5.1`. The paragraph now says that.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover parsing (with and without `.git`, shorthand,
`git+ssh`, `git+file`, multi-key fragments), request building on both
the uv and pipx paths (SHA, branch, and unresolved `latest`), extras
merging, package-name precedence, and keeping the fragment out of
version discovery.
- New e2e test `e2e/backend/test_pipx_git_subdirectory` installs ltui
and jtui from one repository at a pinned commit through uv. It asserts
neither install path contains `#` and the paths differ, runs `ltui` and
`jtui` through `mise x` and the shim, and checks the ltui venv's Python
link uses `/installs/python/3.12/`. `test_pipx_venv_symlink` and
`test_pipx_uvx` still pass. The test depends on
github.com/runpantheon/ltui staying available at that commit.
- `mise run lint`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features
--all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `mise run docs:build` pass. Tested on
macOS only. The pipx path without uv is covered by unit tests only.

fix(dotfiles): anchor include/exclude patterns with a leading slash to the entry root (#13621)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/205
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Per-entry `include` and `exclude` lists on `[dotfiles]` entries (`mode =
"track"`, and directory-walking `symlink-each` / `copy` entries)
silently ignored any pattern starting with `/`. The patterns are matched
against paths relative to the entry, which never start with `/`, so:

```toml
[dotfiles]
# captured ~/.codex/cache into history anyway
"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", exclude = ["/cache"] }
# selected nothing at all
"~/.claude" = { mode = "track", include = ["/rules/*.md"] }
```

A leading `/` now anchors a pattern to the entry root, as in
`.gitignore`:

- `exclude = ["/cache"]` skips only the top-level `cache` directory, not
`app/cache` deeper down (a bare `cache` still matches at any depth).
- `include = ["/rules/*.md"]` selects the same files as `rules/*.md`.
- `*` stops at `/` in a rooted pattern, in both lists, as it does in
include lists since #13618. So `/rules/*.md` doesn't reach into
`rules/sub/`. Rooted patterns never matched anything before, so unlike
an unrooted exclusion, a rooted exclusion has no older `*`-crosses-`/`
behaviour to deprecate.
- `/` on its own names the entry itself and still matches nothing.

For a `symlink-each` entry, a file that a fixed `/…` exclude now covers
has its recorded link removed on the next apply, the same as any newly
excluded file. Note that in the global `[history] exclude` list a
leading `/` still means an absolute path. The docs now say so.

### Rollback compatibility

Checkpoints record the matcher version used to read these lists. A
rooted `include` that now selects files an older mise never captured
could make a rollback to an older checkpoint treat those files as
covered but absent, and delete them. The matcher version is bumped to 2.
Checkpoints written by version 1 are still read normally unless the
owning entry's `include` list has a rooted pattern. In that case the
affected paths are reported as unevaluable and kept. A rooted `exclude`
that now matches only moves paths out of coverage, which never deletes
anything.

### Implementation

`rooted_pattern` in `src/system/files.rs` is the only place that decides
whether a pattern starts at the root. `is_selected` / `is_excluded` and
the capture walk's pruner (`reaches_into`) all use it, so pruning and
selection agree. Patterns are still stored and shared exactly as
written, so none of the compile sites needed to change.

Tests: new unit tests cover the matcher, pruner/selection agreement, and
replay of version 1 checkpoints. I also checked a `symlink-each` apply
with `exclude = ["/cache"]` by hand. `cargo clippy --workspace
--all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint-fix` are
clean.

fix(dotfiles): stop `*` crossing `/` in tracked include patterns (#13618)

A tracked directory's `include` list now uses `.gitignore` rules for
patterns that contain a `/`: `*` stops at a `/` and only `**` crosses
directories. This fixes a rollback that could delete a live file.
Per-entry `exclude` lists keep matching what they matched before, but
mise now warns when an exclusion relies on `*` crossing `/`.

## The bug

Take a tracked directory with an include list:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", include = ["rules/*.md"] }
```

Before this change, two parts of mise read `rules/*.md` differently:

- **Capture** skipped `rules/deep/` because no part of `rules/*.md`
matches `deep`. So `rules/deep/two.md` was never saved.
- **Selection** (used by rollback and by the "include list leaves out"
notice) let `*` cross `/`. It treated `rules/deep/two.md` as selected.

The combination was destructive. Suppose you later widened the list to
`rules/**/*.md`, saved, and then ran `mise dot rollback ~/.codex --to
<the earlier checkpoint>`. Rollback saw a file the old checkpoint
"selected" but didn't hold, and called it absent. That is the one answer
that allows removing a live file, so the rollback **deleted
`~/.codex/rules/deep/two.md`**.

Now both parts read `rules/*.md` as "markdown files directly in
`rules`", and the rollback leaves the nested file alone. To select
nested files as well, write `rules/**/*.md`. These are the same rules
the global `[history] exclude` list already uses.

## Exclude lists: deprecation, not a silent change

`exclude` lists go through the same matcher on tracked directories and
on `symlink-each` and directory `copy` entries. They keep their old
meaning for now, because narrowing an exclusion would quietly start
saving files you asked to leave out. For example, with `exclude =
["secrets/*.json"]`, the file `secrets/prod/settings.json` would start
going into history as plaintext.

Such a path is still excluded, and mise now prints a deprecation
warning:

```
mise WARN  deprecated [dotfiles-exclude-star-crosses-separator]: [dotfiles] exclude pattern 'rules/*.md' matches 'rules/deep/two.md' only because `*` crosses `/`; use `**` where a pattern should match across directories, as in include lists. This will be removed in mise 2027.9.13.
```

`rules/**/*.md` keeps the same meaning and produces no warning. Patterns
without a `/` and patterns without wildcards are unaffected.

| Pattern | Path | `include` before | `include` now | `exclude`
(unchanged) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rules/*.md` | `rules/one.md` | matches | matches | matches |
| `rules/*.md` | `rules/deep/two.md` | matches | **no match** | matches,
with a warning |
| `rules/**/*.md` | `rules/deep/two.md` | matches | matches | matches |
| `rules/*` | `rules/deep/two.md` | matches | matches (a matched
directory takes its subtree) | matches |

Rollback safety for older checkpoints is unchanged. The include change
only makes a checkpoint cover less, which rollback treats as "leave the
file alone". So the history matcher version stays at 1. It has to be
bumped when the legacy exclude match is removed.

## Tests

- New e2e test `e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_pattern_separator` covers:
  - what an include list captures;
- the rollback scenario above, which fails on `main` by deleting the
file;
- legacy exclude matches still excluding, with the warning, on a tracked
directory and on a `symlink-each` entry.
- Unit tests in `files.rs` for both matchers. A table in `tracked.rs`
checks that walk pruning and selection agree for `rules/*.md`,
`rules/*/two.md`, `rules/**/*.md`, and `*/two.md`.

Docs: `docs/dotfiles.md` ("Excluding files", with a deprecation notice,
and "Select files within a tracked directory") and the per-entry
exclusions list in `docs/history.md`.

refactor(env): move environment and directory statics into a mise-util crate (#13620)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/204
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. Stacked on #13616, the
second step in splitting mise into crates so that edits recompile less
code.

## Why

Almost every module in mise starts from `env.rs` and `dirs.rs`: `HOME`,
the XDG and `MISE_*_DIR` directories, `PATH_KEY`, the `var_*` helpers.
`env.rs` also mixed in code that reads `.miserc.toml`, detects the shell
type, parses CLI args and reverses activation diffs, so it depended on
`config`, `cli` and `shell`. As a result, no low-level module (`file`,
`path`, `hash`, `lock_file`, progress reporting) could move below
`config`.

## What changes

- **New `crates/mise-util` crate** holding the half of `env.rs` that
only reads the process environment:
- the env-var helpers (`var_path`, `var_is_true`, `set_var`,
`vars_safe`, `args_safe`, …)
  - `HOME` and the XDG / `MISE_*_DIR` statics
  - `PATH_KEY` and its helpers
  - tokens, color and terminal-width flags
  - shim and self-replace name checks
  - Windows launcher argument recovery

It also takes the directory statics from `dirs.rs` and the `~` expander
`replace_path` from `file.rs`.
- **The rest stays in mise.** Anything that needs miserc, `Settings`,
`EnvDiff`, `ShellType` or CLI parsing is unchanged, e.g. `MISE_ENV`,
override filenames, `PRISTINE_ENV`/`PATH`, `prefer_offline` and
`shared_install_dirs`. mise's `env`, `dirs` and `file` modules re-export
the moved items, so every `crate::env::…` / `crate::dirs::…` call site
is untouched.
- **`#[cfg(test)]` became a runtime switch.** `cfg(test)` doesn't reach
dependencies, so the four statics that behaved differently under unit
tests now check `mise_util::testing::active()`: `HOME`,
`IS_RUNNING_AS_SHIM`, `TERM_WIDTH` and `TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE`. mise's
test constructor calls `mise_util::testing::enable(<repo>/test)` before
anything reads the environment, the same place it already set up the
test `HOME`. Release builds never call it.
- **Dependencies:** `homedir`, `terminal_size` and `mise-agent-env` move
from `mise` to `mise-util`.
- **Release:** `xtasks/release-plz` publishes `mise-util` before `mise`.
`mise-agent-env` bumps now update `mise-util`'s manifest.

Tests of the helpers that became private to `mise-util` moved with them:
launcher argument parsing, `PATH` key casing, token precedence, and
`argv[0]` basenames.

## Follow-ups

Next is moving `file.rs`, `path.rs`, `hash.rs`, `lock_file.rs` and
progress reporting into `mise-util`, which needs `mise-settings` as a
dependency. After that, large areas like `src/system` can start moving
out of the main crate.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
passes.
- Unit tests: `mise-util` and `mise-settings` pass (26 tests). mise
passes 4843 of 4844; the one timeout,
`git::tests::update_resolves_short_branches_and_tags`, runs in 0.97s
against nextest's 1s limit on this machine and fails the same way on
#13616.
- A debug build reports the same `mise dr` directories as before, and
`mise x node@22 -- node -v` works.
- Windows-only moved code (`LOCAL_APPDATA`,
`invoked_as_self_replace_helper`) moved verbatim. It isn't compiled
locally, so Windows CI is the check.

refactor(config): move generated settings types into a mise-settings crate (#13616)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/201
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the first step
toward splitting mise into several crates so that edits recompile less
code.

## Why

The `mise` crate is about 410k lines of Rust. Measured on an M-series
Mac with a unique one-string edit to `src/duration.rs`:

- With a warm incremental cache, the rebuild takes about 11s, nearly all
of it in the `mise` unit.
- When that cache is cold (a fresh worktree, a switched branch, or
artifacts restored from a shared build cache), the whole crate
recompiles in 75–90s. Content-addressed caches can't skip any of that,
because it's one unit.

Splitting helps that cold case and full builds, but only once large
parts of the code live in their own crates. Low-level modules like
`file`, `dirs`, `http`, `cmd` and `platform` all call `Settings::get()`,
and `Settings` has been defined inside the config system at the top of
the dependency graph. Nothing can move below `config` until `Settings`
does.

## What changes

- **New `crates/mise-settings` crate.** It generates the `Settings` /
`SettingsPartial` / `MisercSettings` types and `SETTINGS_META` from the
root `settings.toml`, which moves that codegen out of mise's `build.rs`.
The crate also holds the setting value enums (including `TaskOutput`),
the env-var parsers, the accessors that only read fields, and the
process-wide settings cache.
- **Loading stays in mise, behind a registered loader.** Loading
settings needs config discovery, trust checks, templating and CLI flags.
mise calls `mise_settings::set_loader(load)` at the start of `main` and
in the test harness constructor. `Settings::try_get()` returns the
cached value or runs that loader, so callers keep using
`Settings::get()` as before.
- **Methods that need the rest of mise live on extension traits.**
Rust's orphan rule stops mise from adding inherent methods to a type
defined in another crate. Methods like `offline()`, `http_timeout()` and
`reset()` therefore live on `SettingsExt` in `src/config/settings.rs`,
and similar traits cover `SettingsNode` and `TaskOutput`. Call sites are
unchanged apart from importing the trait. That import is most of the
~100-file diff.
- **The `python.uv_venv_auto = true` deprecation warning moved.** It now
fires from the loader once the setting resolves to the legacy value,
instead of inside the value's deserializer, which can't reach mise's
`deprecated_at!`. The message and ID are unchanged. One difference: a
`true` that a higher-precedence source overrides no longer warns.
- **Release.** `xtasks/release-plz` publishes `mise-settings` before
`mise`. It copies `settings.toml` into the crate for packaging, the same
way `mise-interactive-config` handles `mise.json`, and treats edits to
`settings.toml` as changes to the crate.

`settings.toml` stays at the repository root, where the docs and schema
tooling already read it.

## Follow-ups

This PR does not speed up builds by itself; warm rebuilds are unchanged
at about 11s. The next steps move the low-level helpers (`file`, `dirs`,
`env`, `hash`, `cmd`, `http`, …) into a crate below `config`, then split
off large, rarely-shared areas such as `src/system` (about 105k lines).

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
passes.
- Unit tests pass for `mise` (`cargo nextest run --all-features`) and
`mise-settings`. The parser tests for the moved helpers now live in the
new crate.
- Windows-only code isn't compiled locally. A scan for extension-trait
method calls in files without the matching import found one miss, in
`ruby_windows.rs`, which is fixed.

chore(release): build Windows tarballs with thin LTO (#13614)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/199
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Windows release builds were timing out, which blocked the 2026.9.14
release PR. This switches the Windows tarballs from fat LTO to thin LTO
so they finish reliably. Linux and macOS builds are unchanged.

## Why

On the `windows-latest` runner (4 vCPU / 16 GB), the fat-LTO compile and
link of the `mise` crate is single-threaded and memory-bound:

- v2026.9.13 tag build: `Compiling mise` → `Finished` took about 65
minutes (74m56s total cargo time)
- 2026.9.14 release PR ([run
36133236032](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/36133236032)): the
same stage was still running after 2h22m, and
`build-tarball-windows-x64` hit the 150-minute job timeout

Larger Windows runners aren't available yet: the Namespace plan doesn't
include Windows, and Buildkite's Windows hosted agents have to be
enabled by their support team. Once one of those is in place, Windows
can go back to fat LTO.

## Change

`scripts/build-tarball.ps1` sets `CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_LTO=thin`, next
to the existing `CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_PANIC=unwind` Windows override.
This applies to both x64 and arm64. Thin LTO keeps most of the
cross-crate inlining but optimizes in parallel and uses much less
memory. The Windows binary may be slightly slower or larger than a
fat-LTO build.

## Validation

Not run locally. The Windows jobs only run in the release workflow, so
the next armed release PR is the real test.

fix(system): follow HTTP mirror redirects for checksum-pinned brew sources (#13611)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/198
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Building a GNU formula from source with the brew system package manager
failed because GNU's mirror redirector is currently sending requests to
a plain-HTTP mirror:

```
$ curl -sI https://ftpmirror.gnu.org/hello/hello-2.12.3.tar.gz | grep -i location
Location: http://mirror.team-cymru.com/gnu//hello/hello-2.12.3.tar.gz
```

Since #13292, mise refuses HTTPS→HTTP redirects on downloads, so `mise
bootstrap packages apply` stopped with:

```
mise brew:hello      download hello-2.12.3.tar.gz
mise brew:hello    ✗ failed
Error:
   0: error following redirect
   1: refusing to redirect a download from HTTPS to HTTP
```

Homebrew follows these redirects. Every formula source tarball is pinned
by sha256, so downgrading the transport doesn't weaken the result. With
this change, brew source downloads follow the redirect, the build
completes, and a tarball that doesn't match the checksum is still
rejected.

This failure is also what broke
`cli/test_system_install_brew_source_slow` on the 2026.9.14 release PR
(jdx/mise#13590).

## Implementation

- New `http::download_file_checksum_pinned(url, path, sha256, pr)`. It
uses a private client whose redirect policy allows the downgrade, and it
removes the file if the checksum doesn't match. That private client is
the only one that allows the downgrade, and it can only be reached
through this helper. Every other client keeps refusing it.
- `brew::source::fetch_source` now calls this helper instead of
`HTTP.download_file` followed by `ensure_checksum`.

## Validation

- `TEST_ALL=1 mise run test:e2e
cli/test_system_install_brew_source_slow` passes locally. At the time of
the run, ftpmirror.gnu.org was redirecting to HTTP, so the test
exercised the downgrade path.
- New unit test: a matching file is kept and a mismatched file is
removed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
is clean.

ci: defer release PR merges overnight with a release-now override (#13606)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/195
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Releases should be able to be kicked off in the evening and actually go
out the next morning, so nothing ships while nobody is around to watch
it. Two recent releases landed in the middle of the night Central time
(`v2026.9.9` at 00:08 CDT, `v2026.9.3` at 01:51 CDT).

This adds a `release-window` commit status on the release PR. Once it is
a required check on main:

- **Defer:** enable auto-merge on the release PR at, say, 8pm. Between
18:00 and 03:00 America/Chicago the status is `pending` ("Waiting for
03:00 Central; label release-now to release immediately"), so the PR
waits instead of merging. The scheduled run shortly after 03:00 flips it
to `success` and auto-merge completes on its own.
- **Override:** add the `release-now` label to the release PR. The
status turns `success` immediately and the release proceeds (removing
the label restores the hold).
- **Daytime:** the status is `success`, so releases behave as today.
- **Every other PR:** always `success`; normal PRs are unaffected.

Note that enabling auto-merge still starts the release dry-run build
right away (the existing `auto_merge_enabled` gate in `release.yml`);
only the merge, and therefore publishing, waits.

## Details

- The gate sits on the merge because merging the release PR is what
makes `xtasks/release-plz` publish crates and push the tag. Gating
`release.yml` instead would leave a published crate with no GitHub
release.
- Six scheduled runs a day (UTC times chosen to cover both CDT and CST)
flip the status at the edges: around 17:07 Central it turns `pending`
(anything within an hour of 18:00 counts as quiet), and around 03:07
Central it turns `success`. Each edge has follow-up runs an hour or two
later in case GitHub delays or drops one.
- Only the release PR's own events and the schedule write the status of
this repository's `release` branch commit, all in one serialized
concurrency group; other PRs (including forks with a `release` branch)
never write it, so they cannot clear the hold or revive a removed
override. A failed branch lookup fails the job without posting a status,
keeping the PR blocked.
- `pull_request_target` lets the workflow post statuses on fork PRs; it
reads only PR metadata and checks out no code, like
`conventional-commits.yml`.

## After merging

1. Create the `release-now` label.
2. Add `release-window` to the required status checks in the main
ruleset (after merge, since `pull_request_target` runs from main; PRs
already open need a new push or reopen to receive the status).

## Validation

- `actionlint`, `zizmor`, and `prettier` pass; quiet-hour boundaries
checked locally for every scheduled run time (16:07 success, 17:07
pending, 02:07 pending, 03:07 success).
- Not yet exercised on a live release PR.

fix(backend): don't reuse versions-host version lists when MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0 (#13605)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/194
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #13604.

For a registry tool, mise gets the remote version list from the versions
host (mise-versions.jdx.dev). The host picks up new GitHub releases
after a delay, and mise then caches its list for
`fetch_remote_versions_cache` (1h by default).
`MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0` should skip the host and fetch from the
source directly. Instead it used the same cache entry, so it returned
the host's older list until that entry expired.

Before, right after `jdx/tak` v0.0.11 was published:

```sh
mise ls-remote tak                           # host list cached: up to 0.0.10
MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0 mise ls-remote tak  # same cache entry: still up to 0.0.10
```

After, `MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0` has its own remote-versions cache
entry, so it lists versions from the backend and shows 0.0.11. Turning
the host off adds a cache key, but turning it on doesn't, so caches that
already exist for the default setting stay valid. The extra key is only
added for backends the versions host can serve (github, aqua, core,
asdf, vfox, and similar). Backends like npm and cargo always list from
their own source, so they keep a single cache entry.

The hosted `latest` release cache that the issue also mentions already
uses separate hosted and direct keys (`release_cache_key` in
`src/github.rs`), so it needed no change. This PR doesn't change `mise
cache clear <tool>`. That command still doesn't clear the tool's
`github/` release cache.

### Validation

- New e2e test `e2e/cli/test_ls_remote_versions_host_cache`. A local
stand-in, set up with `url_replacements`, serves both the versions host
(only 0.0.10) and the GitHub API (0.0.10 and 0.0.11) for the registry
tool `tak`. After the host list is cached, `MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0
mise ls-remote tak` must list 0.0.11, and the host-on cache entry must
stay as it was. Without the fix, the host-off run returns only 0.0.10.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
passes.

fix(bootstrap): point config_roots deprecation warning at conf.d folders (#13598)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/190
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap].config_roots` was deprecated in 2026.9.3 (#13010). Its
warning said to "move bootstrap declarations into global or system
configuration". That doesn't tell users how to keep a setup split into
self-contained bundles, which is why they used `config_roots`.

#13603 added `conf.d` folders: a folder inside `conf.d` is a config
fragment and the config root for its own files. That is a direct
migration path, so the warning now says to use it:

```
mise WARN  deprecated [bootstrap.config_roots]: `[bootstrap].config_roots` in ~/dotfiles/mise.toml is deprecated. Move each selected root into a conf.d folder instead (or symlink it): bundles/git becomes mise/conf.d/git in the same project, or ~/.config/mise/conf.d/git when config_roots is set in global config. A conf.d folder reads only mise.toml, mise.local.toml, mise.<env>.toml, and mise.<env>.local.toml (rename other config filenames) and is their config root, so relative paths and `{{ config_root }}` still resolve inside it. See https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html#conf-d-folders for details. This will be removed in mise 2027.3.3.
```

For example, this setup:

```toml
# ~/dotfiles/mise.toml
[bootstrap]
config_roots = ["*/*"]   # dev/git/mise.toml, shell/zsh/mise.macos.toml, ...
```

becomes `~/dotfiles/mise/conf.d/dev-git/` and
`~/dotfiles/mise/conf.d/shell-zsh/`, moved or symlinked, with the root
`config_roots` removed. A project's `mise/conf.d` loads exactly when its
`mise.toml` does. If `config_roots` was set in global config, the
bundles go to `~/.config/mise/conf.d/` so they still apply from any
directory. The warning prints the real global `conf.d` path, so it
follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. Relative dotfile
sources keep resolving inside each folder. Unlike `config_roots`, every
section in a folder participates (tools, tasks, packages, hooks,
`[env]`).

The `config_roots` schema description points to the same docs. Behavior
and the removal date are unchanged.

commits.message: fix(config-releases): serve a former archive from the store when a repository replacement outruns the mirror (CFG-7) (#7701) ## Summary Staging release-gate run 36188978457 (attempt 2, `deployed api shard (2)`) failed `CFG-7` with `the project's own stored archive: 404` (`tests/src/flows/config-releases.flow.ts:1000`), on staging SHA `b6872877` with `CONFIG_RELEASES_ENABLED=true` (#7691). **Verdict: product bug**, not a test bug. ### Root cause `apps/api/src/config-releases/serve-archive.ts` (`serveConfigArchive`) gated every archive request on `isTreeObject(mirror, treeId)` *before* ever consulting the S3 store. `PUT /v1/projects/:id/git/repository` (the route CFG-7 exercises by writing the same columns it writes) can replace a project's origin with a second, genuinely unrelated repository. The OLD config tree is not reachable from the NEW origin's history — no `git fetch` of the current origin will ever reproduce it. The bare git mirror lives on **per-ECS-task ephemeral disk** (`apps/api/src/projects/git/mirror.ts`, `repoCachePath` keyed only by `projectId`, root `/tmp/kortix/git-cache`), not shared across API replicas. A replica whose local mirror never warmed *before* the replacement clones straight from the CURRENT (already-replaced) origin and can **never** contain the old tree — the mirror-gate returns 404 there forever, even though the archive is durably stored in S3 under the project's own key (`projects//trees/.tar.gz`, written by `storeConfigArchive` when the pre-replacement descriptor was first built). This explains why `CFG-1/2/3/4/6/8/9/10` passed in the same run: none of them replace the repository with unrelated history, so every replica's mirror still contains the tree the archive route needs, regardless of which replica serves the request. `CFG-7` is the only flow that swaps to a genuinely unrelated repository, so it is the only one exposed to a cold replica. Confirmed NOT an S3 IAM permission gap (the learnings entry on HeadObject-403-vs-404 does not apply here): the 404 response is returned directly from the mirror-gate, before the code ever calls `store.head()` / `store.downloadUrl()`. ### Fix When the tree is absent from both the warm and the forced-refresh mirror, try the store directly by its project-scoped key before answering 404. The key alone proves the archive is this project's own former config (the caller already passed repository-access / `PROJECT_FILE_READ` to reach the route), so no mirror confirmation is required. Only 404 when **neither** the mirror **nor** the store has it. ## Test plan - [x] `bun test --isolate --env-file=scripts/test.env --timeout=15000` over every `apps/api/src/config-releases/**/*.test.ts` file: **108 pass, 0 fail** (includes 2 new regression tests — store-hit/mirror-miss now serves 200 from the store, mirror-miss/store-miss still 404). - [x] `tsc --noEmit` on `apps/api`: clean. - [x] `pnpm test -- --domain config-releases` (local stack): **10/10 flows pass**, `CFG-7` included (2.3s). The local profile runs one API process, so it cannot reproduce the multi-replica cache split itself — the new unit tests are the deterministic reproduction of that exact condition. - [ ] `test` label on this PR for the six CI lanes (not run yet — requesting the label on open). --- Need help on this PR? test(api): seed IAM HTTP suites with a local git upstream (#7669) ## Problem The four slowest DB suites in the `core` lane seed the project `repoUrl` with an `https://example.com/...git` URL. Each request that reads the repository runs `git clone --bare` or `git ls-remote` against that host. It then waits on DNS, TLS, and an HTTP failure. The mirror retries each failed clone 3 times, with a 500 ms delay between attempts. CI `core` lane, db-suites stage (6 workers, 99 files), on `main` runs 36150452403 and 36156278100: | Suite | Tests | Duration | | --- | --- | --- | | `integration-project-read-leaf-gates-http` | 90 | 36.8 s / 38.6 s | | `integration-project-write-leaf-gates-http` | 90 | 21.8 s / 23.3 s | | `integration-detail-capability-http` | 3 | 12.4 s / 12.8 s | | `integration-members-manage-gates-http` | 42 | 11.6 s / 11.7 s | | db-suites stage total | 1063 | 47.8 s / 50.8 s | A local `GIT_TRACE` run found these outbound git commands: - The read suite ran 72 `git clone --bare https://example.com/...` and 2 `git ls-remote`. - The write suite ran 48 `git clone --bare`. Email installation DELETE alone spent 9.4 s and 11.4 s per request. - The detail-capability suite ran 27 `git-remote-https` execs. - The members-manage suite ran 18 `git-remote-https` execs. ## Change - New `apps/api/src/__tests__/helpers/local-git-upstream.ts`, with `createLocalGitUpstream(label)`: - It creates a bare repository with one commit (`README.md`) on `main` in a `mkdtemp` directory. - It points `KORTIX_GIT_CACHE_DIR` into the same directory, so mirror clones no longer write under the shared `/tmp/kortix/git-cache`. - `remove()` deletes the directory and restores the environment variable. - The file does not import `shared/db`. The write suite sets `LLM_GATEWAY_ENABLED` before it loads config, so this import order must not change. - All 4 suites seed `repoUrl: upstream.repoUrl` in `beforeAll` and call `upstream.remove()` in `afterAll`. - Production code does not change. The API mirror already accepts a local path as `repoUrl`, and `integration-project-snapshot` and `change-request-governance.integration` already use one. No validator rejects the path. ## Assertions - **Read and write leaf-gate suites.** Every assertion is unchanged. A denied request still returns 403 and names the leaf. An allowed request still returns a status other than 403, or passes `iamDenied() === false`. The git call on the allowed path now succeeds instead of failing, and 4 read routes change status: - `GET /commits`: 400 → 200 - `GET /files/archive`: 400 → 200 - `GET /files/content`: 503 → 200 - `GET /files/history`: 400 → 200 In the write suite, 0 statuses changed. I compared the status sequences of the local runs before and after. - **Detail-capability suite (stronger).** The member file-list test ran its assertions only inside `if (res.status === 200)`. With the unreachable upstream, the mirror always returned an empty file list, so `files toEqual []` could not fail. Now: - The member test asserts `status === 200`, then `files === []` and `file_count === 0`, with no condition. - The manager test also asserts `files === ['README.md']` and `file_count === 1`. This proves that the member's empty list comes from the filter and not from an empty repository. - Red run: the new assertions against the old `https://example.com` seed give `2 pass, 1 fail` (the MANAGER case). Green run with the local upstream: `3 pass`. - **Members-manage suite.** Only the fixture changes. ## Verification - **Offline.** Both leaf-gate suites pass inside a macOS `sandbox-exec` profile that denies every outbound connection except loopback and Unix sockets. The profile does block traffic: `curl https://example.com` fails with `(7) Couldn't connect to server`. Results: - read: 90 pass, 0 fail - write: 90 pass, 0 fail - `GIT_TRACE`: 0 `git-remote-https` execs - **Git calls after the change.** Every git command in the trace targets the temporary bare repository: `clone --bare `, `upload-pack `, `ls-remote --heads origin`, `ls-tree`, `show`. - **Other outbound calls.** The app makes 2 other outbound attempts at import time: the LLM-gateway catalog refresh and the model-pricing fetch. Both run in the background, run once per process, and handle their own failure. They do not block any request. - **Local timings.** The machine load average was 70–218 during these runs, so treat the numbers as approximate. Run with `bun test` on one freshly cloned database: - read: 98–105 s → 35 s - write: 94 s → 26 s The time left is about 28 Postgres queries per request on Docker for macOS (`Server-Timing: db;desc="n=28"`), not git. - **Other suites.** All 4 suites pass in `bun tests/bin/db-suites.ts leaf-gates-http detail-capability-http members-manage-gates-http --workers 1`. - **CI.** The `core` lane durations after this change are posted as a comment when the `test` run finishes. ## Follow-ups: other `example.com/*.git` seeds `git grep -n "example.com/.*\.git" apps/api/src`. I traced each integration suite with `GIT_TRACE` and counted `git-remote-https` execs. - **No outbound git (left unchanged):** - `integration-feature-flag-toggle-http` - `integration-iam-engine` - `integration-iam-resource-scope` - `integration-iam-service-account` - `integration-iam-sso-sync` - `integration-iam-token-scope-expiry` - `integration-member-model-gates-http` - `integration-personal-tokens` - `integration-resource-grants` - `integration-token-revocation` - **In open PR #7663 (not touched here), all with 0 outbound git today:** - `integration-member-session-prompt-gates-http` - `integration-preview-agent-authz` - `integration-session-activity` - `integration-session-title-claim` - `integration-warm-session-adopt` - `integration-warm-sessions-exclude` - **Unit tests** (`unit-git-backends`, `marketplace/catalog`, `fast-boot-git-hint`) use the URL as a string only. - **`helpers/integration-fixtures.ts` `seedProject()`** seeds `https://example.test/

feat(session): group consecutive show calls into one tabbed carousel card (#7685) ## Summary When the agent presents several outputs in a row (for example two screenshots), the session thread rendered one full `show` card per call.
