This change renders consecutive `show` calls as one carousel card. **SDK (`@kortix/sdk`, additive only)** - `groupShowSegments(segments, opts?)`: a post-pass over `segmentTurn`. It merges a run of standalone `show` / `show_user` segments into one `{ kind: 'show-group', parts }` segment. Text, a burst, another standalone tool, or a call with a pending permission breaks the run. A single `show` stays `standalone`. - `showGroupItems(parts)`: flattens the calls into carousel items. A multi-item (`items`) call contributes each of its items. A streaming call gets a `pending` slot. A failed call keeps an `error` slot with its message. A settled call with an empty payload is dropped. - New exports: `groupShowSegments`, `showGroupItems`, `ShowGroupSegment`, `ShowGroupedSegment`, `ShowGroupItem`. `Segment` is unchanged, so existing consumers (mobile) compile and behave as before. **Web** - `session-chat.tsx` and the debug session fixture render a `show-group` through the new `ShowGroupRenderer`. It merges the calls into one `items` part and renders it through the existing `ToolPartRenderer` → `ShowTool` carousel. N single calls and one N-item call produce the same markup. - The merged part keeps the first call's `id` and `callID`. The card keeps its key when the next call joins, so it does not re-mount. - `ShowTool`: the carousel header shows the active item's title (fallback: filename, then call title, then item count). - `ShowCarousel`: renders a pending slot while a call streams its payload, and clamps the active index when the item count drops. Inline, ←/→ page only the focused card; previously a window-level listener paged every carousel in the thread at once. The footer strip with chevrons, text pills and a count is removed inline. Arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs; the call's title labels the tablist. - Refresh and Full screen / Open in browser fold into one more-actions menu. Preview is the only visible button. - The viewer's file-name row is dropped when the header tab already names the file. - A running localhost port uses the app-window icon instead of a globe. - A port slide takes the same 420px slot as image and PDF slides: no gap under the frame, no height change between tabs. - Single show cards and the panel surface are unchanged. **Agent** - The `show` tool description tells the agent to make one `items` call when it has 2+ outputs to present. The embedded starter snapshot is regenerated. **Not in this PR yet** - The expanded / full-screen view still opens one file. refactor(oauth): one hashing scheme for OAuth tokens (#7666)

## Summary

OAuth access and refresh tokens (`kortix_oat_` / `kortix_ort_`) now have
one stored hash: the peppered scrypt `scrypt:v1:<hex>` that every other
Kortix credential uses. The bare-sha256 dual-read is removed.

```diff
 apps/api/src/oauth/
-├── token-hash.ts          # hashOauthToken, legacyHashOauthToken, oauthTokenHashCandidates(Async)
-├── token-hash.test.ts
 ├── index.ts               # mint: hashSecretKey · lookup: hashSecretKeyAsync
 └── access-token.ts        # lookup: hashSecretKeyAsync
```

Lookup, at all 5 sites:

```diff
-const candidates = await oauthTokenHashCandidatesAsync(token)   // [scrypt, sha256]
-.where(and(inArray(oauthAccessTokens.tokenHash, candidates), isNull(oauthAccessTokens.revokedAt)))
+const tokenHash = await hashSecretKeyAsync(token)               // scrypt, off the event loop, cached
+.where(and(eq(oauthAccessTokens.tokenHash, tokenHash), isNull(oauthAccessTokens.revokedAt)))
```

1. Lookup sites (`hashSecretKeyAsync` from `shared/token-hash`):
   - `oauth/index.ts` `oauthTokenAuth` (`/oauth/userinfo`)
   - `oauth/index.ts` `handleRefreshTokenGrant`
- `oauth/index.ts` `/oauth/revoke`: the refresh-token branch and the
access-token branch
- `oauth/access-token.ts` `validateOAuthAccessToken` (every auth
middleware)
2. Mint sites (`hashSecretKey` from `shared/crypto`): `oauth/index.ts`
`issueTokenPair` (access + refresh) and `apps/viewer.ts`
`mintAppViewerToken`.
3. `oauth/token-hash.ts` is deleted. Its two remaining exports were
pass-throughs to the shared functions. OAuth now calls them directly, as
`llm-gateway/gateway-keys.ts`, `repositories/api-keys.ts`, and
`repositories/account-tokens.ts` do. `shared/token-hash.test.ts` already
asserts `hashSecretKeyAsync(t) === hashSecretKey(t)`.
4. `OAU-7` gets one more step: revoking a live access token →
`/accounts/me` answers 401 and its refresh token answers 400
`invalid_grant`. This covers the `/oauth/revoke` access-token branch,
which had no flow step.
5. Four unit-test `mock.module('../shared/crypto')` comments named the
deleted module. They now state the general reason for the spread.

## Why the sha256 read can go: the retirement window closed

- #4344 made new tokens scrypt (merged to `main` 2026-07-08).
- It reached staging through promote #4363 and prod through release
#4364 (v0.9.101, merged 2026-07-09 14:52 UTC). Checked:
`apps/api/src/oauth/token-hash.ts` in the #4364 merge tree mints with
`hashSecretKey`; the v0.9.100 tree (#4343) has no scrypt mint.
- `REFRESH_TOKEN_TTL_MS` is 30 d (`apps/api/src/oauth/index.ts:292`).
Access tokens live 1 h (`OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_S = 3600`).
- A refresh grant after 2026-07-09 mints a new scrypt pair. The last
sha256-stored token on Kortix-hosted environments therefore expired no
later than 2026-08-08.

Exported names are unchanged: no export is renamed or removed. Both public-surface snapshots are green. **1. Route-contract tripwire.** `packages/sdk/src/route-contract.test.ts` parses the SDK with the TypeScript parser. It resolves the path of every `backendApi.*` call and every backend-URL template, then fails on any path that `tests/spec/routes.generated.json` does not serve. The resolver follows literals, same-file helpers, scoped constants and thin wrappers (`iamGet(path)`, `platformFetch(path)`). It finds 400+ call sites and 0 unresolved expressions. The allowlist has two entries: the sandbox proxy `/p/...` and the self-host `/setup/...` router. **2. Endpoints the API no longer serves are retired.** Each one is `@deprecated`. It fails at once with `ApiError { code: 'ENDPOINT_RETIRED' }` and sends no request. Before, it sent a request that returned 404. ```text REST (19) referrals ×6, Google Slides ×2, templates ×2, updateTemplateWarmPool, getInvite/acceptInvite/declineInvite, deleteInstance, claimComputer, getSandboxProvisionStreamUrl (throws) markInstanceError → resolves undefined, getSandboxProvisionStatus → resolves null (neither threw before; both keep that contract) react (53) use-admin-analytics ×28, use-admin-feedback ×8, use-system-status ×4, use-admin-billing ×4, per-sandbox admin ×7 + fetchAdminSandboxProxyToken, useAdminAccountSandboxes (no retry, no polling) web referral modal (no opener left) + its hooks/components/store: deleted presentation viewer: "Google Slides" export item removed (PDF/PPTX stay) billing/admin barrels: no longer re-export the 4 retired billing hooks ``` `platformFetch` lost its last caller, so it is deleted. It was never exported. **3. One transport module.** `send()` in `core/http/transport.ts` owns the token, the header policy (bearer, `X-Kortix-Client`, admin bypass, act-as), the default deadline, the configured `fetch`, and the one 401 replay. The replay is sent from a copy taken before the first send, which is the #7610 logic. ```text backendApi.get/post/... (makeRequest: retries, deadline, body → ApiError) ─┐ backendApi.postStream ├─► send() authenticatedFetch (fetch semantics, synthetic 401) ─┘ ``` `send()` is the only place that resolves the token. It asks `getToken()` on every attempt, so a `backendApi` read retry after a 401 replay carries the fresh token. `SendOptions` has no `token` option: the 401 replay asks `getToken()` again, so a caller-resolved token would be swapped for the host's identity on the replay. A caller that sets its own `Authorization` header gets no 401 replay. `makeRequest` answers `AuthError` from `send()` (no token) with `{ error: AuthError, success: false }` and does not retry. `BillingError` (402) and `RequestTooLargeError` (431) now extend `ApiError`. A 402 keeps the backend `code`, `details` and `response`. These are behaviour changes. Each one follows from sharing one policy: - `authenticatedFetch` (runtime, files, PTY) now sends the act-as and admin-bypass headers. `backendApi` always sent them. - `backendApi` replays a `401` once with a fresh token. - `postStream` honours `configureKortix({ fetch })`. Without a token it resolves a 401 and sends nothing. Deleted: `buildAuthHeaders`, `fetchWithAuth`, the admin-bypass state and header assembly in `api-client.ts`, and `postStream`'s own token and header code. **Follow-ups (not in this PR):** these callers still build their own fetch: - `platform-client/auth.ts` `call` (headless auth, no token); - `auth/app-viewer.ts`; - `platform-client/updates.ts` (public version reads); - `platform-client/host-boundary.ts`; - the explicit-token server helpers (`serverTokenGet`, `fetchAccountStateWithToken`, `files.ts`, `session-costs.ts`, `projects.ts` provision). They need an anonymous or explicit-token mode on `send()`. An explicit-token mode must disable the 401 replay, or replay only with that caller's own refresh source. `send()` takes no token option today. **4. `createAuthUser` resolves the user after a 504** (`47499d9829`). A 504 from the Supabase auth admin endpoint is the proxy giving up while GoTrue can still commit the insert. `tests/e2e/helpers/session-auth.ts` resent the create and then failed on `422 email_exists` or `500 23505` for the user its own first request made. After a 504, those two replies now resolve that user through a password sign-in. An `email_exists` without an earlier 504 still fails. Test: `tests/unit/create-auth-user-replay.test.ts`. **5. Local invalid-index repair checks its own database only** (`55cc11914a`). `pg_stat_progress_create_index` lists index builds in every database of the cluster. The db-suites lane clones a database per test file on the local cluster and builds indexes there, so the product-flow lane's local migration aborted with `Cannot repair local invalid indexes while an index build is active`. `packages/db/scripts/local-invalid-index-repair.ts` now filters on `datname = current_database()`. ## Root cause

Real-PostgreSQL keepers (`integration-*` db-suites) already owned most
lifecycle contracts. Around them, mocked replays had built up:

produce;

- source greps of route wiring;

db-suite (`integration-session-env-grants`) borrowed an existing account
and returned early, so its 12 tests asserted nothing in CI.

fix(slack,sandbox): stop killing live runs as idle (#7670)

## Summary

A prod Slack run posted "This run was closed after 30 minutes of silence
— it may have stalled or run out of credits". The run was healthy. Two
defects combined to kill it.

### 1. The Slack stale-turn sweep reads silence as death

The run sent 1 `slack step`. Then 2 `explore` subagents made model calls
every minute, with 0 gateway failures and a 148 s generation still
streaming. At 30m22s after the last relay, the sweep closed the thread
and called `abortRuntimeTurn`. That aborted both subagents
(`ToolExecutionError`) and the root turn (`MessageAbortedError`) within
300 ms. The box then idled and stopped at `deadline_expired` 17.5 min
later. Nothing else stopped it.

The sweep's only liveness signal was `chat_turn_streams.updated_at`,
which only `slack step` and `slack send` write. The Teams sweep got a
liveness check on 2026-09-23 (`50671bc79e`); Slack did not. The abort
reached prod in v0.13.31 (2026-09-24 23:14 UTC).

```diff
 sweepStaleSlackTurns   (every 5 min, rows silent > 30 min)
   for row in stale
+    if sessionHoldsLiveTurn(session)        # lifecycle authority: activeTurns on a running box
+      touch updated_at; continue
     claimFinalize
-    finalize "closed after 30 minutes of silence … run out of credits" ("Run timed out")
+    finalize "This run ended without a reply." ("Run failed")
     deleteTurn
     abortRuntimeTurn
```

### 2. Every session's first turn loses its turn authority at boot

Fix 1 relies on the lifecycle authority. On prod, 1,580 of 1,604
session-creating first turns in 7 days ended `abandoned` and none was
accepted. The same holds every day since the ledger began (2026-08-19).
The median abandon came 12.6 s into the turn, and 125 of these turns
demonstrably kept running afterwards, 75 for more than 10 min. So every
reader of "is this session working?" saw a running first turn as idle:
the stale-turn sweeps, the inbox, and `GET .../turn`. A first Slack
message creates its session, so fix 1 alone would not protect that turn.

```diff
 boot
   prompt_async(first prompt)            # answers 204 before OpenCode writes the message
   reconcileInitialTurnAcceptance
     observeOpencodeDelivery             # +11 ms: message absent / root not busy yet
-    -> turn_abandoned                   # authority erased; turn_begin later sees a "known_message"
+    -> unknown while THIS boot awaits pickup (≤ 15 min), retry on tick
 on busy frame
+  promote the pending first-turn token first    # never turn_begin a second token for it
   turn_begin
```

A prompt that an earlier boot delivered keeps the immediate verdict: on
a reused root, absence is proof.

### Also

- `kortix-slack` skill: removed the "~5-minute idle timeout" and
heartbeat-loop guidance. The plan block is an edited message, so a live
run has no idle timeout. `embedded.generated.json` is regenerated.
- `learnings`: 2 rules. A reaper asks the lifecycle authority before it
closes or aborts a run. After an async submit, "not visible yet" is
`unknown`, never terminal.

## Evidence

- **Sweep, before:** `unit-slack-turn-sweep.test.ts` →
`sweepStaleSlackTurns is not a function`, 0/4.
**After:** 4/4. Live run → untouched, not aborted, `updated_at` touched.
Dead run → closed "This run ended without a reply" and aborted.
Unreadable authority → closed. Teams row → ignored.
- **Sweep on local Postgres,** 2 synthetic rows silent for 31 min: the
live row is kept (age reset to 0.47 s), the dead row is reaped.
- **First turn on real OpenCode 1.18.23,** cold instance, real daemon
functions, reconcile right after `prompt_async` as boot does:
  ```
  before: +12ms inactive ["turn_abandoned"]   (3/3 runs)
after: +10ms unknown [] → +2015ms accepted ["turn_accepted"] (3/3 runs)
  ```
- `initial-turn-lifecycle.test.ts` 14/14. It covers absent/unanswered →
unknown, then accepted on busy; abandoned after the grace; reused root
still abandoned at once; delivery time recorded; busy frame promotes
before `turn_begin`.
- `apps/api`: `tsc --noEmit` exits 0; Slack and Teams unit tests
791/791. Daemon: `tsc --noEmit` exits 0; full suite 1313/1314. The 1
failure is a 5 s timing e2e test (`verified-reload-process.e2e`) that
passes 3/3 alone; each full run fails a different such test.
`packages/starter` 78/78.
- CI `Tests` on the first commit: `packages` and `browser-4` failed.
Both also failed on `main` in the last 2 finished runs (`cd6b6ab7af`,
`a6e219fdda`).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** turn lifecycle

- First turns now hold authority while they run, as every later turn
already did. The inbox now queues a follow-up prompt sent during a first
turn instead of forwarding it into the turn. `GET .../turn` reports the
first turn as running. Boxes keep their turn deadline grant during the
first turn.
- A prompt that is really dropped keeps a `delivering` record for up to
15 min (the control plane's own delivery grace) instead of about 0.3 s.
- A live Slack or Teams run that goes silent keeps its thread open until
it ends. A wedged turn waits for the 24 h `turnAbsoluteMaxMs` ceiling.
- The daemon change reaches boxes through runtime convergence against
the API they talk to.

## Summary

A customer set two secrets (via the agent's intake link, then the
Secrets page, then reloaded the session). The session still saw neither
value: the session's agent was not granted them. Every surface reported
this as silence or `missing`, so the agent said "not set" and the person
re-entered values that were already saved.

One signal, **"not granted to agent X"**, now appears on every surface
where the agent or the person used to see nothing:

```diff
 agent: request_secret / kortix secrets request --scope runtime
+  → withheld: [{name, reason: agent_grant}], withheld_fix   (warning printed)
 person: fills /secret-intake/<token>
-  → "Saved securely"
+  → "Saved, but <agent> can't read it yet — Customize → Agents → <agent> → Secrets"
 session follow-up message
+  → names the withheld keys + the exact fix; "do not report these as unset"
 agent: kortix secrets ls
-  ○ KEY   missing
+  ○ KEY   not granted     + "Listed: only the secrets agent X is granted"
 person: enables it in Customize (PUT /agents/:name/scope or POST /secrets/:id/grant)
-  → arrives on the session's next prompt
+  → pushed to running sessions immediately (propagateProjectSecretsToActiveSandboxes)
```

The agent's enumeration ceiling is unchanged. The verdict comes from the
caller's own grant, checked against names it supplied or declared. `GET
/secrets` adds `agent_scope`, which is the caller's own grant, not a
list of existing secrets.

This PR also corrects advice that did not work. Agents were told to run
`kortix secrets sync`, which returns `403` for every session principal.
They were also told to confirm via `KORTIX_PROJECT_SECRET_NAMES`, which
is fixed at session start.

```text
apps/api/src/projects/lib/session-secret-reach.ts   # grant ∩ allowlist verdict + fix text (new)
apps/api/src/projects/routes/setup-links.ts          # mint: withheld
apps/api/src/setup-links/public-app.ts               # submit: withheld + session prompt
apps/api/src/projects/routes/secrets.ts              # GET agent_scope; sync 403 code
apps/api/src/projects/routes/agent-scope.ts          # push grant edits to live sessions
packages/sdk  apps/web  apps/cli  docs + agent skill
```

## Evidence

Live on a worktree stack. Setup: a real managed project; agent `analyst`
granted `[VERIFY_GRANTED_KEY, VERIFY_UNSET_KEY]`; `VERIFY_WITHHELD_KEY`
set but not granted. The session used a production-minted session PAT,
and every command below ran the real CLI.

- **Before (real Platinum sandbox, session bound to `analyst`):**
`VERIFY_GRANTED_KEY present · VERIFY_WITHHELD_KEY absent` (the reported
state).
`kortix secrets sync` as agent → `exit 1`, hint "add the action to
agents.analyst.kortix_permissions" (wrong).
  **After:**
  ```
  ● VERIFY_GRANTED_KEY    set          environment  required
  ○ VERIFY_WITHHELD_KEY   not granted  environment  required
  ○ VERIFY_UNSET_KEY      missing      environment  required
! … not granted to agent analyst … a value may be set, but this session
never receives it.
  ```
`secrets request … --scope runtime` → `withheld:[{VERIFY_WITHHELD_KEY,
agent_grant}]` + fix; connector scope → no `withheld`.
Public `POST /v1/setup-links/secret/:token` → `200
{"saved":[…],"agent":"analyst","withheld":[{"name":"VERIFY_WITHHELD_KEY","reason":"agent_grant"}]}`.
The queued `system:secret-submitted` message contains the Customize fix.
Person `PUT /agents/analyst/scope` adding the key, **no prompt**, then
re-read the sandbox env → `VERIFY_WITHHELD_KEY present` (log: `propagate
… synced: 1`).
`secrets sync` as agent → "the action is reserved for people — a human
must do this".

**Blast Radius:** secrets-delivery

- Grant edits now call `propagateProjectSecretsToActiveSandboxes`. This
is the same push that already runs on every secret write, and it is
behind the same cooldown. An agent session's own scope edit does not

- `secretSubmittedPrompt` text changed (the test assertion was

**Agent scope policy (owner decision 2026-09-25):** an agent may edit
agent scopes only when it holds `project.agent.write`. That is today's
gate on `PUT /agents/:name/scope`. Note: the starter `kortix` agent
(`kortix_permissions: all`) holds it, so it can widen its own secrets
grant. Verified live: `200`. `POST /secrets/:id/grant` stays strict
(refuses all agent sessions). Its `agent_session_forbidden` 403 now
renders in the CLI as "a person with project access must do this"
instead of a `kortix_permissions` edit that cannot work.

Sessions always run the base branch's current config, behind the config_releases flag (#7403)

A session used to run whatever config its sandbox held on the day it was created. `kortix sessions reload` was meant to fix that and refused on nearly every session, because the platform itself modifies `.kortix/opencode` (the plugin pin, the managed-skill overlay) and the sync read that as the user's own edits.

## What changes

- The API builds a **config release** from the base branch's current commit: the config dir as a content-addressed archive plus the compiled agent settings, stored through the repo's existing S3 layer (`object-store/s3.ts`, extracted from the snapshot store, behaviour unchanged) — AWS on dev and prod, the Supabase S3 endpoint locally, in previews and self-host.
- The box verifies every file against its git blob id, unpacks it to `/opt/kortix/config/<release>` and seals it read-only. OpenCode boots from there, never from `/workspace`.
- **One linear boot path** replaces nine functions across two files: resolve → make present and verified → point the boot link → start → prove it serves → record. The decision surface drops from 595 lines to 409, the writers of the running state from 19 to 1. Readiness is computed from the proof, so a box cannot be ready on an unproven config. Five AST tripwires fail if a second config source, a second readiness writer or a timer near the decision is added.
- It converges at boot, restart, wake, a base-branch write, and at **turn start**: a prompt on a box that is behind converges first, then runs.
- `/workspace` stays an ordinary clone: it never decides what boots, and the platform never writes it.
- A previous-repository session is no longer frozen — six policy refusals deleted. A session whose agent the manifest no longer declares is re-pointed once to the project's declared default, audited and IAM-guarded; the rule that an undeclared name receives nothing is untouched.
- Failure is loud: a config that does not load falls back to the last proven release, else the image default, naming file, line and column in health, `GET /config`, the CLI and the web header. A release that broke two sessions is held back for that project.

## The bug this replaces

`boot.ts` raced release extraction against a 3 s timer and wrote the feature-enabled flag inside that same race. Two of eight measured boots lost it — by 282 ms and 156 ms — and those boxes silently booted `/workspace` while reporting `proven: true`. The 15 s boot tail was the same bug: the workspace path skipped the dependency pin, so OpenCode reinstalled its whole tree through a symlink.

## Two switches, both OFF

`CONFIG_RELEASES_ENABLED` (operator, per environment) and `config_releases` (per project, in Settings). An environment must be enabled, then a project must opt in. `deploy-dev` turns the operator switch on; staging and prod stay off. Merging changes behaviour nowhere.

## Verified on real Platinum sandboxes

- 10 fresh boots, 134 health samples: zero ever ready on the workspace config, zero unproven. Ready median 5,392 ms; the 15 s tail is gone.
- A push converges a running session in 6–11 s with no restart; three rounds of push-then-prompt answered with the new config every time, including through the OpenCode port.
- Broken config: the box still becomes ready, names `ConfigJsonError … line 10, column 3`, and heals after the fix without another push.
- Missing, empty and foreign clones all boot the current release. A real model turn answered a marker that exists only in the release copy.
- Suites: API 10,826 · daemon 1,444 · web 10,158 · CLI 1,418 · tests 582 · flows 473/473 in CI.

## Also fixed here

A prompt sent twice with the same text inside 10 minutes was answered `200 {"deduplicated": true}` and never ran — a content hash was treated as a submission identity. Clients without an idempotency key or wire message id (the SDK's `send()`, so `kortix sessions chat` and the TUI) lost the second prompt. The claim now requires a key that identifies one submission. Pre-existing on `main`, proven by an A/B on a real box.

## What

Deletes `apps/web` source that no module imports. Pure deletion: no
route, component, or API behavior changes.

- **162 source files deleted, 20,815 lines**, plus the 3 tests whose
only subject was a deleted module:
`features/layout/account-switcher.test.ts` (13 lines, read the deleted
component from disk), `customize/sections/view/changes-timeline.test.ts`
(180) and `components/ui/agent-avatar.test.tsx` (17).
- **Whole diff:** `git diff --shortstat origin/main 0822b589d6`
(`origin/main` = `b9c2bb59fa`) reports `197 files changed, 99
insertions(+), 21698 deletions(-)`: 165 files deleted, 32 modified. This
includes the 99-line lockfile drop, the 82 lines of `stack` data in
`landing/content.ts`, and comment updates.
- **2 dependencies dropped** from `apps/web/package.json`:
`react-hook-form` (`^7.62.0`) and `@hookform/resolvers` (`^5.2.1`).
`components/ui/form.tsx` was their only user. `pnpm-lock.yaml`
regenerated with `pnpm install`.

## Method

1. A scan resolves every import specifier (static, dynamic `import()`,
`mock.module`) in `apps/`, `packages/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `docs/` to
a file. `@/` resolves to `apps/web/src` only for importers inside
`apps/web`.
2. A file is deleted only when 0 non-test files import it. A test file
(`*.test.*`, `*.spec.*`) is not a consumer: a module whose only importer
is its own test is dead, and the test goes with its subject. Next.js
entry files (`page`, `layout`, `route`, …) are never candidates. Files
in "Kept on purpose" are roots, so modules they import stay.
3. The scan repeats after each deletion round until no new orphan
appears (fixed point: 6 rounds by filename stem, then 4 rounds by
resolved path, then 1 round by resolved path with test importers
excluded, `13a2a23199`).
4. A second, stem-based scan (any specifier ending in `/<stem>`) also
reports 0 orphans outside the keep list.

The resolved-path scan found orphans the stem scan hid behind name
collisions (for example `features/layout/account-switcher.tsx` versus

Callers pass a `providerId`, never a key name: the module derives the name the gateway reads. ```diff secrets/account-resource.ts + queryUsableGatewaySecrets({ grantUserId, providerId?, name?, ids? }) # the one pooled-key SQL; checks keys, no principal listUsableGatewaySecrets({ userId: string, ... }) # member gate (project read + account_members join), then the same SQL + ids? # only these keys (SQL) + name? # only keys stored under this key name (SQL) secrets/provider-key-selection.ts + providerEnvVarOf(providerId) # codex -> CODEX_AUTH_SECRET_NAME, else the catalog key name providerKeyOf(model) # now calls providerEnvVarOf + mayUseProviderKeys({ grantUserId, providerId, ids }) -> boolean # queryUsableGatewaySecrets; no userId usableProviderKeys({ userId, grantUserId, model }) # listUsableGatewaySecrets; name filtered in SQL projects/routes/provider-secret-pools.ts - providerEnvVar() # copy of the codex/catalog mapping - poolKeyRows() # second copy of the pooled-key query - .max(10) / ids.length > 10 + .max(MAX_KEYS_PER_PROVIDER) / ids.length > MAX_KEYS_PER_PROVIDER validateProviderSecretPool -> mayUseProviderKeys(grantUserId: caller) PUT handler -> memberMayReadProject(owner) once, then mayUseProviderKeys(grantUserId: personal user) projects/lib/session-model-keys.ts - checkSessionModelChange(..., hasSelection) + admitSessionModelChange(...) # checks for a selection, selects the keys, stores them projects/routes/session-scope.ts - hasSelection: raw DB query built in the route - insert ... onConflictDoNothing # the fill write now lives in the lib ``` The two grant scopes stay separate: - **Caller check** (`validateProviderSecretPool`): keys shared with the project, plus keys granted to the caller. The route has already authorized the caller, so this check reads keys only (`queryUsableGatewaySecrets`). A service account holds no grant (`account_secret_grants` has a foreign key to `account_memberships`), so it selects keys shared with the whole project only. - **Session check** (`PUT` handler): keys shared with the project, plus keys granted to the session's personal user. A shared session has no personal user, so it gets project keys only. The owner's project-read gate runs once, with the named `SESSION_OWNER_NO_PROJECT_ACCESS` refusal, then the key query runs. - **Member listing** (`usableProviderKeys`: session create, model change, chat channels): `listUsableGatewaySecrets` with a non-null `userId`. No nullable parameter skips its gate. Intentional changes: 1. The **session check** requires the session owner to read the project. The old `poolKeyRows` query did not check this. The gateway (`resolveSessionProviderSecrets`) applies the same gate when it serves keys. A selection that the gateway would not serve now gets `403 SESSION_OWNER_NO_PROJECT_ACCESS` instead of being stored. The **caller check** is unchanged from `main`: keys only, with the caller's grants. 2. Key names are compared exactly, in SQL. `usableProviderKeys` compared them case-insensitively before. Both writers store uppercase names (`/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/` and `CODEX_AUTH_JSON`), so no stored key changes verdict. 3. `PUT /sessions/:id/model`: when another request stores a selection for the provider between the check and the write, that selection stays and the model is judged with it. Before, the route ignored the conflict and answered with the verdict for its own unsaved selection. ## Evidence - **Real DB** (`bun --no-env-file tests/bin/db-suites.ts usable-gateway-secrets`): new `apps/api/src/__tests__/integration-usable-gateway-secrets.test.ts`, 12 tests, PASS. It asserts exact key-name match (a `_OLD` suffix and a lower-case name are other keys), the ids filter (never a key out of scope), member vs project-only scope (`grantUserId: null`), that a grant counts only for `grantUserId`, and the member gate (no project read → `[]`, no `account_members` row → `[]`). Mutation check: with the grant join on any user and a prefix name match, 8 of 12 fail. - **Unit** (`bun test --env-file=scripts/test.env --isolate`): the route test mocks `memberMayReadProject`, `queryUsableGatewaySecrets` and `listUsableGatewaySecrets` at their seam; it no longer parses drizzle SQL params. It asserts one project-read gate per `PUT` (for the owner) and the `grantUserId` of each key check: `[caller, personal user]`, or `[caller, null]` for a shared session. - Full `apps/api` unit suite after merging `main`: 10,612 pass, 0 fail. - **Flows:** `pnpm test -- --domain secrets`: 13/13 pass (SEC-1..8, SEC-POOL-1..5). SEC-POOL-2 runs a real service-account bearer with a project `manager` assignment on a human-owned, project-shared git-trigger session: pool `PUT` with a project key → 200, with a member-granted key → 403 `Secret unavailable or not granted`, model change → 200 with the project key stored. - `apps/api` `tsc --noEmit`: 0 errors. - **Real I/O** against the worktree API (local Supabase, synthetic account and keys), recorded on the first commit of this PR. The verdicts did not change since: ```text PUT .../provider-secret-pools/anthropic [k1,k2] -> 200 {configured:true, secret_ids:[k1,k2]} GET .../provider-secret-pools/anthropic -> 200 secret_ids == [k1,k2] PUT .../anthropic [member-only key, not granted] -> 403 Secret unavailable or not granted PUT .../anthropic [11 ids] -> 400 Array must contain at most 10 element(s) PUT .../anthropic [k1,k1] -> 400 Invalid or duplicate secret id PUT .../nobody [k1] -> 400 Unknown provider PUT .../codex [anthropic key] -> 403 Secret unavailable or not granted PUT shared session .../anthropic [k1,k2] -> 200 GET after the refused writes -> secret_ids == [k1,k2] ``` Acceptance: - `git grep "'CODEX_AUTH_JSON'" apps/api/src/projects/routes apps/api/src/secrets/provider-key-selection.ts` (non-test files) returns nothing. - No `.max(10)` or `> 10` key limit remains. - `session-scope.ts` does not reference `sessionProviderSecretPools`. - The only pooled-key selection SQL is `gatewaySecretRows` in `account-resource.ts`, behind `queryUsableGatewaySecrets` (keys only) and `listUsableGatewaySecrets` (member-gated). - No exported function takes `userId: string | null`; `isAccountMember` is not re-exported from `secrets/`. `resolveSessionProviderSecrets` is the gateway's use-time read of values and cooldowns, and this PR does not change it. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. There is no schema change. Before, the selection was stored, but the gateway could not serve it. - Service-account callers keep the `main` verdict: a service account that may change a human-owned session can select keys shared with the whole project and switch to a model only they reach. fix(channel-cli): downloads and teams conversations surface the API's denial message (#7643)

## Summary

This PR completes #7634. #7634 fixed the error message only in
`lib/api.ts` `parseResponse`. Three channel CLI commands still used
their own fetch calls and parsed the error themselves. On the API's
structured denial `{ error: true, message, code, action }`
(`apps/api/src/iam/denial-message.ts`), they reported:

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `slack download` | `"error": "true"` | `Download failed: HTTP 403:
<message>` |
| `teams download` | `"error": "true"` | `Download failed: HTTP 403:
<message>` |
| `teams conversations` | `Could not list conversations: HTTP 403` |
`HTTP 403: <message>` |

The PR removes the three hand-rolled fetch calls. `lib/api.ts` now holds
the only error-message logic:

```diff
 lib/api.ts
+  apiErrorMessage(status, statusText, text)   # message → string error → raw body → statusText → HTTP <status>
+  apiError(res, text, prefix)                 # CliError 'API_ERROR' + { status }
   parseResponse                               # uses apiError; output byte-identical
+  kortixDownload(path, params)                # binary GET, 60 s timeout, 'Download failed: ' prefix
 channels/slack.ts   download()      -27 lines → kortixDownload
 channels/teams.ts   downloadFile()  -24 lines → kortixDownload (resolveDownloadOutput + chmod 0o600 kept)
 channels/teams.ts   conversations   -8 lines  → kortixGet
```

Decisions:
- `{ error: true }` with no `message` resolves to the raw body, not to
`statusText`. The raw body keeps `parseResponse` byte-identical. It also
keeps the detail of a body whose `error` is an object, such as a
validation body. The result is never the bare string `true`. A unit test
covers this.
- A download failure now has `code: "API_ERROR"` and `status`, the same
envelope as every other API call. Before, it had `code: "CLI_ERROR"` and
no `status`.
- Missing `KORTIX_API_URL` or `KORTIX_TOKEN` now gives the shared
`MISSING_ENV` messages from `lib/api.ts`. A missing `KORTIX_PROJECT_ID`
still says `cannot download`.
- Query encoding: `?url=` is now built with `URLSearchParams` instead of
`encodeURIComponent`. The server decodes both to the same value. The e2e
test asserts the value the proxy receives.
- The connector-call path (`kortixConnectorCall`) is unchanged. It
already falls back to stdout/stderr, not to a boolean `error`. The
existing test `surfaces structured Connector auth errors…` covers it.

## Evidence

**Tests.** The new cases run in
`apps/api/src/__tests__/e2e-slack-cli.test.ts` (the real `bun` CLI
process against a fake API) and in
`unit-channel-cli-api-error-message.test.ts`.

- **Before** (tests on `origin/main` code): `8 pass, 3 fail, 1 error`
  ```
SyntaxError: Export named 'apiErrorMessage' not found in module
'.../slack-cli/lib/api.ts'
(fail) surfaces a structured download denial instead of the boolean
error field
  -   "code": "API_ERROR",
- "error": "Download failed: HTTP 403: This agent session is not granted
\"project.connector.read\". …",
  +   "code": "CLI_ERROR",
  +   "error": "true",
(fail) teams conversations lists targets and surfaces a structured
denial
  +   "error": "Could not list conversations: HTTP 403",
  ```
`teams download writes the file owner-only at the resolved path` passes
on both sides. It is a characterization test: it checks the resolved
path, the size, and mode `0o600`.
- **After:** `bun test e2e-slack-cli e2e-teams-cli-history
unit-channel-cli-api-error-message unit-teams-messages-strip` → `31
pass, 0 fail, 213 expect() calls`

**Real process check.** A standalone stub server answers every request
with the structured 403. Bash runs `bun
apps/sandbox/slack-cli/channels/<cli>.ts …`:

```
===== BEFORE origin/main
$ slack download --url https://files.example.com/F1 --out …/slack.bin
exit=1 stderr_bytes=0
{ "ok": false, "error": "true", "code": "CLI_ERROR"}
$ teams download --url https://files.example.com/T1 --out …/teams.bin
exit=1 stderr_bytes=0
{ "ok": false, "error": "true", "code": "CLI_ERROR"}
$ teams conversations
exit=1 stderr_bytes=0
{ "ok": false, "error": "Could not list conversations: HTTP 403", "code": "CLI_ERROR"}
===== AFTER branch
$ slack download …
exit=1 stderr_bytes=0
{ "ok": false, "error": "Download failed: HTTP 403: This agent session is not granted \"project.connector.read\". Add it to the agent's kortix_permissions in kortix.yaml and merge the change.", "code": "API_ERROR", "status": 403}
$ teams download …
exit=1 stderr_bytes=0
{ "ok": false, "error": "Download failed: HTTP 403: This agent session is not granted …", "code": "API_ERROR", "status": 403}
$ teams conversations
exit=1 stderr_bytes=0
{ "ok": false, "error": "HTTP 403: This agent session is not granted …", "code": "API_ERROR", "status": 403}
```
The CLI writes its error envelope to stdout (`handleError` → `out`), so
stderr stays empty. No output file is written on a denial.

**Static checks**
- `tsc --noEmit` over all 7 `apps/sandbox/slack-cli` sources with a
scratch tsconfig (`types: bun`, strict): exit 0 on this branch and exit
0 on `origin/main`. No CI program typechecks `channels/*.ts`. `apps/api`
`tsc --noEmit` exit 0; it now also includes `lib/api.ts` through the
unit test.
- `biome lint` on the touched paths: the same 5 errors as `origin/main`,
all in the untouched `lib/cli.ts`. `biome format` shows no new diffs on
lines this PR adds.

**Suites**
- CI (`test` label) at `38101b2c31`: `core`, `browser-1` through
`browser-4`, `packages`, API typecheck, and CodeQL all pass.
- Local `pnpm test -- --packages-only`: `kortix-api` 10483 pass, 3 fail;
`kortixd` 1279 pass, 1 fail. All 4 failures are timeouts under local
load: 3 in `unit-daytona-snapshot-context` and 1 in `kortixd`
`verified-reload-process.e2e`. Run alone, each file passes (11/11 and
3/3). The CI `packages` lane runs the same suite and passes.

## How the fix reaches a session

`apps/sandbox/slack-cli` has no in-place runtime-asset convergence. It
ships only through images:
1. **Base sandbox image:** `apps/sandbox/Dockerfile` copies it to
`/opt/kortix/apps/sandbox/slack-cli/`, and `install-shims.sh` creates
`/usr/local/bin/slack` and `/usr/local/bin/teams`.
2. **Project template runtime layer:** the API image copies
`apps/sandbox/slack-cli` (`apps/api/Dockerfile`).
`snapshots/build-context.ts` stages it as `kortix-slack-cli/`, and the
layer copies it to the same `/opt/kortix/...` path. `kortix-slack-cli`
is in `NON_AGENT_RUNTIME_ARTIFACTS` (`snapshots/templates.ts`), so this
change moves the non-agent runtime fingerprint. After the API deploys,
the next template build for a project is a full rebuild, not an
agent-swap.

The fix is live in a session that boots from a template built after the
API deploy. To check it in a sandbox, run `grep -c kortixDownload
/opt/kortix/apps/sandbox/slack-cli/channels/teams.ts`. The result is `2`
when the fix is present and `0` when it is not.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. Revert the commit to restore the old behavior. No
data, schema, or API route changes.

**Blast Radius:** sandbox-CLI

Only the `slack download`, `teams download`, and `teams conversations`
commands inside sandboxes change. On success, they return the same
output. On failure, they return a different error text and `code`. No
agent skill or doc matches on the old strings (`git grep` for `Download
failed` and `Could not list conversations` finds no other references).
Merging moves the non-agent runtime fingerprint, so the next template
build for each project is a full rebuild instead of an agent-swap.

refactor(api): one helper per request primitive, with a tripwire (#7650)

## Summary

Four request primitives in `apps/api` have one module and one import
path each. A tripwire test fails on a new copy of any of them.

```text
apps/api/src/shared/
├── client-ip.ts   # requestClientIp (stored address) + requestClientKey (rate-limit bucket key)
├── validate.ts    # NEW: isUuid, the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form a PostgreSQL uuid column accepts
├── http-body.ts   # NEW: readJsonObject(c) → Record<string, unknown>, never null
└── html.ts        # NEW: escapeHtml, moved out of the email template module
apps/api/src/__tests__/unit-request-primitives-tripwire.test.ts   # NEW
```

### 1. Client address: `shared/client-ip.ts`

Audit, session-activity, and IAM request-context rows store the
X-Forwarded-For entry that `KORTIX_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS` selects, counted
from the right (default 2). Rate limiting uses the same rule.

```ts
requestClientIp(c): string | null          // stored in rows; null when no header is set
requestClientKey(c): string                // rate-limit bucket key; 'unknown' when no header is set
clientKeyFromHeaders(header): string       // the same key for a raw Headers object (index.ts WebSocket upgrade)
```

- Converted row writers: `admin/index.ts` (12 audit rows),
`accounts/audit.ts` (3), `accounts/iam/helpers.ts` `auditIam`,
`shared/auth-audit.ts`, `projects/lib/serializers.ts`
`requestAuditContext`, `shared/audit-scope.ts`, `iam/session-gate.ts`
(2), `iam/cache.ts`, `iam/actor.ts`, and the rate-limit audit row in
`shared/rate-limit.ts`.
- Bucket keys: `requestClientKey` replaces the inline `?? 'unknown'` at
7 sites (`index.ts`, `token-attempt-budget.ts`, `middleware/auth.ts` log
line, `setup-links/public-app.ts`, `shared/rate-limit.ts`,
`tunnel/routes/device-auth.ts`, `auth/headless.ts`). Bucket keys do not
change.
- Deleted wrappers: `auth/headless.ts` `clientIp`,
`tunnel/routes/device-auth.ts` `clientRateLimitKey`,
`shared/rate-limit.ts` `clientIp`, `setup-links/public-app.ts`
pass-through, `shared/auth-audit.ts` `clientIp`, `serializers.ts`
`clientIp`, `audit-scope.ts` `firstForwardedFor`, `iam/actor.ts`
`firstForwardedIp`.
- The 12 `admin/index.ts` sites now also fall back to `x-real-ip`, the
same as every other site.
- **The IP is not used for authorization.** The only reads of `ctx.ip`
are the two audit writes in `iam/assignments.ts`. `iam/session-gate.ts`
passes `ip` only to `markRevoked` and `touchActivity`. `iam/cache.ts`
folds it into the authorize() cache key; no policy condition reads it.

### 2. UUID shape: `shared/validate.ts`

```ts
export type Uuid = string & { readonly __brand: 'Uuid' };
export function isUuid(value: unknown): value is Uuid;   // the regex is module-private
```

- It accepts any version, any variant, any case: what a `uuid` column
stores. A malformed id at a `::uuid` cast is SQLSTATE 22P02 (a 500), so
guards call `isUuid` first.
- **Why the brand:** with `value is string`, a `string` that fails the
check narrows to `never` in the false branch. A `Uuid` is assignable to
`string` everywhere.
- No dual paths: the `projects/lib/serializers.ts` `UUID_V4_REGEX` alias
and the `projects/lib/access.ts` `isUuid` re-export are deleted. 38
`UUID_V4_REGEX` uses in 18 files call `isUuid`. The 2 zod params in
`gateway.ts` (`budgetId`, `keyId`) use `z.string().uuid()`. zod
3.25.76's uuid regex is the same 8-4-4-4-12 any-version form as
`isUuid`, and the OpenAPI document keeps the `uuid` format. 4 importers
read `isUuid` from `shared/validate`.
- 17 loose private copies and 6 strict RFC copies are replaced, plus the
`channel-teams.ts` tenant and app id check now that #7633 is on main.
The 6 strict sites now accept a well-formed id of any version:
`shared/audit-query.ts` (2 cursor parsers), `connectors/attachments.ts`,
`projects/trigger-session-access-policy.ts`,
`projects/session-lifecycle/prompt-parts.ts`,

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

A plain revert restores the old code. There are no migrations and no
data rewrites. Rows written before the merge keep their stored address.
Rows written after it store the hop-selected address.

**Blast Radius:** audit-rows, request-bodies

`KORTIX_TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS`. A wrong value for a deployment stores a
proxy address (too low) or a client-supplied entry (too high). Rate
limiting has used the same setting since the client-ip change.

as `{}`. Each route then applies its normal "field is required"
validation (400) instead of a 500.

database lookup and gets its not-found result instead of an early 400.

identical.

`billing/services/webhooks.ts`, `projects/lib/access.ts`,
`middleware/auth.ts`) change by a few import and call-site lines each.

fix(sandbox): one Stop can no longer break every later turn in a session (#7655) ## Summary One Stop during the first turn of a fresh session broke every later turn on the box. Each later turn ended in 15–66 ms as `MessageAbortedError`, with no output and no cancel request. The web showed "This turn stopped before it finished. No reason was reported." Changing the model did not help. In prod over 7 days, 17 sessions on 15 accounts matched and never recovered. That is an upper bound. **Cause.** OpenCode builds each per-directory service on first use, in the caller's fiber, and caches the result forever. That includes an interrupted build (`InstanceState` → Effect `ScopedCache`). Verified on effect `4.0.0-beta.83` and `4.0.0-rc.117`, and on OpenCode 1.18.23 through upstream `dev`. No released version fixes it. The first prompt is that first caller. Kortix projects ship custom tools in `.kortix/opencode/tools/`, so the tool-registry build takes about 1 s. A Stop inside that window poisons the instance. ```text daemon (instance-guard.ts) on event-stream connect / instance dispose warm: GET /experimental/tool/ids, /agent, /skill, /config/providers, /mcp # nobody cancels these proxy.forward POST /session/:id/abort -> noteOpencodeStopRequested(id) POST /session/:id/prompt_async|… -> await warm-up (≤ 20 s) # a prompt only joins the daemon's build on session.idle / session.error inspectEndedTurn abort + stop requested -> heal if poisoned (probe 503 ×2 -> POST /instance/dispose -> warm) abort + nobody asked + no output (victim) -> dispose + warm -> turn-auto-resume (runtime-fault), once -> else relay cause RuntimeAbortedTurn ``` Every daemon abort path records the stop request first: the proxy, `/kortix/abort`, the quick-queue interrupt, the memory guard, the orphaned-turn finalize, and the runaway guard. **Second bug: the user's own Stop read "No reason was reported".** The hold route's background settle re-aborted the turn through its own `POST /session/:id/abort`, bypassing the proxy that stamps `UserStop`. It reached OpenCode before the browser's own abort. ```diff POST .../prompts/hold {held:true} + markTurnStopRequested(sessionId, 'UserStop') # before anything can abort holdInboxPrompts settleInboxHoldAfterStopInBackground - fetch(POST /session/:id/abort) # unstamped + abortRuntimeTurn(sessionId, {requestedStop:true}) # stamps, then aborts ``` ## Evidence **Real OpenCode 1.18.23 binary**, with a project custom tool whose import takes 1.5 s and a Stop at 800 ms into turn 1. The script is in the scratchpad, not in the repo: | scenario | before | after | |---|---|---| | turn 2 after the Stop | `MessageAbortedError` in 28 ms, no parts | warm-up: `OK` in 172–208 ms (2 of 2 runs) | | heal after a requested Stop | poisoned until the process restarts | `{kind:'requested', poisoned:true, disposed:true, poisonedPaths:['/experimental/tool/ids']}`, then turn 2 `OK` | | victim turn | `MessageAbortedError` in 69 ms | `{kind:'unrequested', resumed:true}`, then the transcript ends with `[auto-recovery] …` and `OK` | **Prod unblock with the same mechanism:** before `POST /instance/dispose`, a test prompt aborted in 37 ms. After it, the same prompt answered `OK` in 3.8 s. **Tests** - `instance-guard.test.ts`: 24 pass. The mock OpenCode reproduces the poison without the guard, then covers warm, gate, heal, victim resume (1 resume for 2 observers), child sessions, and the busy guard. - `turn-auto-resume.test.ts`: 19 pass, including the new runtime-fault cause. - `apps/kortix-sandbox-agent-server`: `bun test` gives 1306 pass, 0 fail. `bun tsc --noEmit` is clean. - API: `session-prompts.test.ts`, `session-lifecycle/`, `sandbox-proxy/` give 886 pass, 0 fail. `integration-sandbox-turn-lifecycle.test.ts` covers the prod order. `tsc --noEmit` is clean. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way. No schema change, no data migration. The daemon self-updates on the next idle swap, so a revert rolls back the same way. **Blast Radius:** sessions - The first prompt after boot or after a dispose waits for the warm-up, 20 s at most. The work is the same init the prompt ran before, so it moves rather than grows. A hung warm-up request is abandoned after 120 s. - A forced dispose happens only for a victim turn with no output, and never while another session is busy. - A stop sent directly to OpenCode on port 4096, for example from a TUI inside the box, is not recorded. An empty turn it aborts would be resumed once. - The hold route now stamps `UserStop` on the open turn. A turn that completes drops the stamp, as before. --- Need help on this PR? fix(sandbox): keep Kortix tools on PATH and load secrets in terminal login shells (#7654) ## Problem In the web terminal of a session sandbox built from a Debian-based custom template (for example `FROM debian:bookworm-slim`), `opencode`, `pnpm`, `node`, `python`, and `bun` return `command not found`. The agent's own shell tools work in the same sandbox. The default Ubuntu template is not affected. ## Cause 1. `apps/kortix-sandbox-agent-server/src/routes/pty.ts` spawns the terminal as `/bin/bash -l` with the daemon env. The daemon PATH starts with `KORTIX_USER_PATH_DIRS` (`/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin:/home/kortix/.bun/bin`). 2. A login shell sources `/etc/profile`. Debian's `/etc/profile` resets PATH for non-root users to `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games`. `~/.profile` adds back only `~/.local/bin`. The pnpm and bun dirs are lost. 3. Ubuntu's `/etc/profile` does not set PATH. That is why the default template works. 4. The agent's tools run non-login `bash -c`, so they keep the daemon PATH. 5. Adjacent gap, confirmed: the `/etc/profile.d` + `/etc/bash.bashrc` hooks that source `/dev/shm/kortix/agent-env.sh` exist only in `apps/sandbox/Dockerfile`. The cloud image layer (`packages/shared/src/sandbox/dockerfile-layer.ts`) had none. The layer builds every cloud template, including the Ubuntu platform default (`PLATFORM_DEFAULT_USER_DOCKERFILE`). So no cloud terminal loaded project secrets. The Docker repro below shows `missing` on Ubuntu without the hook. ## Fix - `kortixShellProfileScript()` renders `/etc/profile.d/zz-kortix.sh` (POSIX sh). It prepends only the `KORTIX_USER_PATH_DIRS` entries that are missing, and keeps every other entry in its position (root keeps Debian's sbin dirs). Sourcing it again changes nothing. It never adds an empty PATH entry. Then it sources `/dev/shm/kortix/agent-env.sh` if the file is readable. - `kortixShellProfileRun()` writes that file with one `echo ''` per line. It uses no heredoc (buildah) and no `printf '\n'` (E2B strips the backslash). It then appends one `/etc/bash.bashrc` line that sources the hook, and a `grep -qxF` guard stops a second copy. With the bashrc line, non-login interactive shells also load secrets. - The dir list comes from `KORTIX_USER_PATH_DIRS`, the same constant the layer's `ENV PATH` and the entrypoint test use. There is no second copy. - `kortixArtifactLayer` runs the step as root after `USER root`, before the final `USER kortix`. It goes in the artifact tail on purpose: it sits below the Chromium layer and does not change Chromium's build-cache key. - The meta image (`FROM debian:bookworm-slim`, same bug class) runs the same step before its entrypoint. - `RUNTIME_LAYER_VERSION` goes from `v44` to `v45`. - Docs: `/docs/work/runtime` "What the runtime layer adds" describes the hook. ## Rollout: how existing templates pick it up - **Existing sandboxes do not self-heal.** The hook is baked into the image rootfs. Nothing at runtime writes `/etc/profile.d`, and the daemon's runtime-asset convergence (`runtime-assets.ts`) does not touch it. A session whose sandbox exists today keeps the old rootfs. A new session gets the fix after its template image is rebuilt. - **Platform default and meta images:** rebuilt by the API startup pre-build (`kickStartupPreBuild` → `ensurePlatformDefaultImage` / `ensureMetaSandboxImage`, `source: 'startup'`). The default rebuilds because `RUNTIME_LAYER_VERSION` feeds `runtimeVersionKey`. The meta image rebuilds because its fingerprint hashes `packages/shared/src`. - **Custom templates:** there is no pre-build. The v45 bump changes every template's identity. It also changes the non-agent fingerprint in `swapKey`, so the agent-swap fast path does not apply and the image gets a full rebuild. The first session start after deploy boots the last ready image (still without the hook, for at most 7 days: `LAST_READY_IMAGE_MAX_AGE_MS`) and starts a background rebuild (`kickBackgroundRebuild`). Sessions started after that build is ready get the hook. A manual rebuild from the template settings also works. ## Verification Unit tests, run locally: ``` $ cd packages/shared && bun test 467 pass 0 fail Ran 467 tests across 34 files. $ cd packages/shared && npx tsc --noEmit -p . ; echo $? 0 $ cd apps/api && bun test --isolate --env-file=scripts/test.env --timeout=15000 src/snapshots/ src/__tests__/unit-dockerfile-layer.test.ts src/__tests__/unit-runtime-versions.test.ts 317 pass 0 fail Ran 317 tests across 39 files. $ cd apps/cli && bun test src/__tests__/sandboxes-local*.test.ts 29 pass 0 fail ``` `packages/shared/src/sandbox/__tests__/shell-profile.test.ts` (16 tests) runs the hook in a real `/bin/sh`. It checks: the Debian non-root and root resets, an unchanged Ubuntu PATH, idempotency, a partial PATH, empty and unset PATH, secret loading, no leaked helper variables, and the env-file path against the daemon's `AGENT_ENV_DIR`. It also runs the RUN step twice against a scratch root: the file matches the renderer byte for byte, and bashrc gets exactly one line. The test also checks where the step sits in both Dockerfiles. The layer golden (`layer-render.test.ts.snap`) diff adds only this RUN step, once in each case. Docker test. The images were built from the real `kortixShellProfileRun()` output on a minimal base (useradd, a fake `opencode` in the pnpm bin dir, `ENV PATH=KORTIX_USER_PATH_DIRS:$PATH`, `USER kortix`). Each ran `docker run -t -e PATH= bash -lic 'echo PATH=$PATH; command -v opencode'`: ``` == debian:bookworm-slim, no hook (reproduces the bug) PATH=/home/kortix/.local/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games opencode: command not found == debian:bookworm-slim, with hook PATH=/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin:/home/kortix/.bun/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/games:/usr/games /home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin/opencode == ubuntu:24.04, no hook PATH=/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin:/home/kortix/.bun/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin /home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin/opencode == ubuntu:24.04, with hook (PATH unchanged) PATH=/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin:/home/kortix/.bun/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin /home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin/opencode ``` (The duplicate `~/.local/bin` comes from the distro's `~/.profile`. It is there with or without the hook.) Secrets (`/dev/shm/kortix/agent-env.sh`, 0600, written as kortix): ``` debian no hook: login-interactive:missing nonlogin-interactive:missing debian with hook: login-interactive:loaded nonlogin-interactive:loaded ubuntu no hook: login-interactive:missing nonlogin-interactive:missing ubuntu with hook: login-interactive:loaded nonlogin-interactive:loaded ``` Root login shell on Debian with the hook: `PATH=/home/kortix/.local/bin:/home/kortix/.local/share/pnpm/bin:/home/kortix/.bun/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`. A dash login shell (`sh -lc`) also resolves `opencode`. `/etc/bash.bashrc` has exactly 1 hook line. The file is `-rw-r--r-- root root`. The same Dockerfile also builds with the classic builder (`DOCKER_BUILDKIT=0`). ## Not verified - A full layered image build on Daytona, Platinum, or E2B. The step uses only constructs the layer already uses (`echo`, `{ }`, `grep`, no heredoc, no backslash escapes). The first provider build after merge proves it. - A live web-terminal session on a Debian custom template. After the rebuild, check it: open the terminal and run `command -v opencode`, then `echo $`. - Existing sandboxes keep the bug until a new session boots from the rebuilt image (see Rollout). --- Need help on this PR? refactor(channels): one chat-channel core for Slack, Teams and email (#7633)

## Summary

Slack, Teams and email now share one chat-channel core in
`apps/api/src/channels/core/`. The Slack and Teams modules keep
transport, parsing and rendering. The rules live in the core, stated
once:

| Module | Owns |
|---|---|
| `core/identity.ts` | The chat identity link (lookup, link, revoke,
access request) and the one actor check (`resolveChatActor`) for Slack
and Teams |
| `core/settings.ts` | Every channel-setting write (agent, policy,
switch, unbind) and the one permission check. The model setters from
#7593 (`slack/model-choice.ts`, `teams/model-choice.ts`) call the same
check |
| `core/threads.ts` | Thread-to-session binding (find, bind, touch,
drop) and the follow-up rule, for Slack, Teams and email |
| `core/sessions.ts` | The recent-sessions list, filtered to sessions
the linked caller may open |
| `core/signed-state.ts` | One signer for login links and OAuth install
state, with a per-purpose key derived from `API_KEY_SECRET` |
| `core/install-completion.ts` | The OAuth install hand-off shared by
Slack and Teams |

`slack/commands.ts` goes from 1,236 to 430 lines. It now routes
subcommands and owns the account, bot-link and session commands.
Settings rendering moves to `slack/settings-commands.ts` (503 lines),
and the agent picker moves to `slack/agent-picker.ts`, the twin of
`teams/agent-picker.ts`. `slack/interactivity.ts` goes from 1,025 to 943
lines.

## What changes for users

- **Channel settings** (Slack `/kortix
model|agent|policy|switch|unbind`, the picker and switch buttons, Teams
`/model|/agent|/policy|/use`, and the Teams picker cards):
- In a shared channel, a change needs a linked Kortix account with
`project.connector.write` on the channel's project. That is the
capability the web binding editor (`PATCH /channels/bindings`) already
requires: project managers, account owners and admins.
- In a one-to-one conversation with the bot (a Slack DM, a Teams
personal chat), the change affects only that person. It needs
`project.write`, the same bar as sending a message there. This keeps
#7593's own-key and ChatGPT model choice working for ordinary members in
their own DM.
- Model choice keeps #7593's checks: per-conversation keys, agent secret
grants, and the Teams live-session owner rule. The permission check runs
before them.
- Moving a bound channel to another project needs the capability on both
projects.
  - Binding an unbound channel for the first time works as before.
- The Slack policy check changes from "account owner or admin" to this
rule, so project managers can now set the policy. Teams `/policy` had no
check before; it now has this one.
- **`/kortix sessions`**: lists only sessions the caller's linked
account may open. It uses the project read check plus the same
session-visibility rule the session routes use. An unlinked caller is
asked to connect first. A per-project app lists only its own project's
sessions.
- **Slack and Teams OAuth install**:
- The provider callback no longer installs. It checks the signed state,
then sends the browser to `/slack/install` or `/teams/install` on the
web.
- That page posts `{code, state}` to `POST
/projects/:id/channels/{slack,teams}/oauth/complete` with the signed-in
user's bearer. That route has the same gate as a manual connect (manage
+ `project.connector.write`).
- The install completes only when the state names that user and that
project.
- The state is checked before the provider configuration. A malformed or
foreign state answers `400` or `403` on every deployment; only a valid
one learns `503` (not configured).
- The installer's Slack identity is linked only when no live link
exists, or when the existing link already points at the same user.
- **Teams OAuth state**: the state is now signed with a key derived from
`API_KEY_SECRET`. It no longer falls back to an empty key when
`MICROSOFT_APP_PASSWORD` is unset.

### 1. `sandbox_compute_sessions` lookup by `sandbox_id`

`getLatestComputeSession` runs `WHERE sandbox_id = $1 ORDER BY
created_at DESC LIMIT 1` over open and closed rows. The only
`sandbox_id` indexes are partial on `ended_at IS NULL`, so each call
scanned the table.

Prod `pg_stat_statements` (read-only, 2026-09-25):

| Query text | Calls | Mean |
|---|---|---|
| current (with `workload_type`) | 26,961 | 77.2 ms |
| older text (with `provider`) | 122,632 | 16.2 ms |
| older text | 204,414 | 7.2 ms |

The table shows 359,639 seq scans and 27.1 B seq-scanned tuples, the
largest seq-scan cost on prod. One sandbox holds 14,175 rows.

The index is ascending `(sandbox_id, created_at)`. A backward scan
returns `created_at DESC NULLS FIRST`, the order the query asks for.
Drizzle's `.desc()` renders `DESC NULLS LAST`, which leaves a sort in
the plan.

Rewrite checked, not possible: the only caller is
`reopenComputeForSandbox`. It runs when no window is open, and it needs
the last closed window's spec. The open-row partial indexes cannot serve
it. The current reconcile tick query itself runs at 4.8 ms mean; the
74.6 ms variant in `pg_stat_statements` is an older query text.

### 2. Free-tier grant rotation

`getFreeAccountsDueForRotation`: `tier = 'free' AND (next_credit_grant
IS NULL OR next_credit_grant <= now())`. Prod: 3,868 calls × 915 ms, a
parallel seq scan over 234k rows that returns ~96 rows per call. `tier =
'free'` matches 99.7% of rows, so `tier` alone cannot help.

The index is a plain composite `(tier, next_credit_grant)`, not a
partial index on `tier = 'free'`: the query binds `tier` as `$1`, and a
generic plan cannot prove a partial predicate. The columns change only
on a grant, so balance updates stay HOT.

### 3. `unique_active_deletion_request`

It is keyed on `is_cancelled` / `is_deleted`. The application writes
`status` only (`apps/api/src/billing/repositories/account-deletion.ts`
is the only reader and writer). So on dev and staging a request after a
cancel failed with `23505` → `500`. Prod never had the index, and 8 prod
accounts hold more than one row.

Replaced with `uniq_account_deletion_requests_pending` on `(account_id)
WHERE status = 'pending'`. Preconditions (read-only, 2026-09-25): 0
accounts with more than one pending row on prod, staging and dev. The
new index is built before the old one is dropped.

`requestAccountDeletion` checks for a pending row, then inserts. Two
concurrent requests both pass the check; the second insert now fails on
the unique index. It returns the same `400` as the pre-check instead of
a `500`.

### 4. `db-drift.yml` has not run on schedule since 2026-08-04

- The workflow is `active` (`updated_at` 2026-06-21, never disabled).
The cron syntax is valid.
- Not the 60-day inactivity rule: the repository has commits every day.
`gh workflow enable` is not needed and was not run.
- Cause: GitHub dispatches a `schedule` as the user who last changed the
cron line. For `db-drift.yml` and `security-scan.yml` that user is no
longer an org member or collaborator (`GET
/orgs/kortix-ai/members/<login>` → 404). Every scheduled run of both
workflows carries that actor. Their last scheduled runs are 2026-08-04
and 2026-08-03. The five other scheduled workflows run as a current
member and still fire.
- Fix: change both cron lines (`07:17` daily, `06:23` Mondays). The
schedule re-registers under the merging user. Off the top of the hour,
where GitHub delays scheduled runs.

It called node-pg-migrate 8.0.4 `runner({ dryRun: true })`. That dry run: - creates `kortix_migrations` and its ledger table when they are absent; - sends `BEGIN` and `COMMIT` (not gated on `dryRun`); - calls every pending migration's `up()`. Only SQL collected through `pgm.sql()` is skipped. A URL `options=` parameter overrides the startup parameter in `pg`, so a session `SET` is tried once; if the setting is still off, `status` exits 1 before any read; - applies the same `checkOrder` refusal and message as `up`; - an absent ledger reads as empty and is not created. test(ci): run the PostgreSQL-backed suites in the core lane, one fresh database per file (#7636)

## Summary

The real-PostgreSQL suites now run in CI. Before this change, no CI lane
ran them:

- `apps/api/src/__tests__/integration-*.test.ts`: 61 files. They ran
only through `bash scripts/test.sh integration` (`dotenvx run`, against
the shared developer database).
- 13 `TEST_DATABASE_URL`-gated files (`*.integration.test.ts`, 2
`e2e-*`). They sat in the apps/api unit run and skipped. The packages
lane reported 113 skipped tests on `main`.
- 4 `packages/db` suites gated on `AUDIT_V2_DATABASE_URL`,
`CONNECTOR_CUTOVER_DATABASE_URL`, or `MIGRATION_REPAIR_ADMIN_URL`. They
skipped in CI.
- `tests/migration`: all files ran in one process, so file order decided
which `mock.module()` a file saw.

This PR adds a `db-suites` lane to the root runner. `pnpm test` (core),
`--full`, and the new `pnpm test -- --db-only [path-filter]` run it. The
`core` CI lane therefore runs it, with no workflow change.

## How the lane works (`tests/bin/db-suites.ts`,
`tests/src/core/db-suites.ts`)

1. **Discovery by name.** One rule covers 3 locations:
   - apps/api: `integration-*.test.ts`, `*.integration.test.ts`
   - packages/db: `scripts/*.integration.test.ts`
   - `tests/migration/*.test.ts`

   Each package's unit discovery excludes exactly these names:
   - `apps/api/scripts/test.sh` excludes both apps/api patterns.
   - `packages/db` `test` uses `--path-ignore-patterns`.
   - `package-quality` no longer runs `tests/migration`.
2. **Hermetic database per file.** The lane builds one template database
per content hash on the local Supabase cluster. The hash covers the
migrations, the `packages/db` scripts, and the Supabase `auth` schema.
Building the template takes about 1 s:
   - Wait for GoTrue.
- Copy the `auth` schema with `pg_dump` inside the Supabase container,
so the dump version matches the server.
   - Apply `test-prereqs.sql`.
   - Run `migrate.ts local-up`.

For each file, the lane clones a fresh database (`CREATE DATABASE …
TEMPLATE`, about 150 ms), runs one `bun test <file>` process, and drops
the database. A file never sees another file's rows or developer data.
Each file gets these variables:
- `TEST_DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_URL`: role `postgres`, the API's
role.
   - `TEST_DATABASE_SUPERUSER_URL`: for fixture setup only.
   - `TEST_DATABASE_ADMIN_URL`
   - `KORTIX_TEST_DB_CONFIRM`

apps/api files also load `scripts/test.env`. The lane never reads the
encrypted `.env`.
3. **Fail on vacuous passes.** A file fails the lane if a test fails, if
it skips any test, or if it runs no test. Quarantined files are printed
with their reason on every run.
4. **Log line and timing.** The lane prints one line per file, the 5
slowest files, and a total, for example `[db-suites] PASS 96/96 suites,
1047 tests, 2 quarantined, 51.1s`.
5. **Guard.** `tests/unit/db-suites.test.ts` fails when a test file
reads `process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL` (or another lane variable) but is
not named as a DB suite. This stops a new suite from skipping inside a
unit lane. On first run, it caught 2 misnamed files.
6. `pnpm --filter kortix-api test:integration [filter]` now calls the
lane.

The runner starts local Supabase before the stage when the plan contains
the lane. `ke2e local` reuses it, and the runner stops it at the end.
Old per-file databases from dead runs, and templates unused for 3 days,
are dropped.

refactor(db): private wallet schema, idempotency-key uniqueness, kortix.ts schema contract (#7631)

## Summary

Two changes on one branch: the wallet's SQL functions move to a private
schema, and `kortix.ts` is made to describe the database the migrations
build, with a CI check that keeps it that way.

### 1. Wallet storage

```diff
 apps/api/src/billing/wallet/index.ts
-  public.atomic_add_credits(...)              (+ a CASE EXISTS whole-ledger key check in TS)
-  public.atomic_use_credits(...)              ADMISSION
-  public.atomic_settle_credits(...)           SETTLEMENT (same body, no floor)
-  public.atomic_reset_expiring_credits(...)
+  kortix_wallet.grant_credits(...)            whole-ledger key check now in SQL
+  kortix_wallet.debit_credits(..., p_enforce_floor => true | false)   NULL enforces the floor
+  kortix_wallet.reset_expiring_credits(...)
```

- `kortix_wallet` is not exposed by PostgREST, and no client role has
`USAGE` or `EXECUTE` on it. The migration fails if any client role can
reach a wallet function.
- The new functions are `SECURITY INVOKER`. Only the API role can
execute them, and that role already writes both tables directly.
- `public.atomic_add_credits` / `atomic_use_credits` /
`atomic_settle_credits` / `atomic_reset_expiring_credits` stay for one
release as thin wrappers. Their signatures, defaults, security mode and
grants do not change, so an API image built before this PR writes
identical rows. **Follow-up:** drop them. The migration is parked in
`packages/db/migrations-pending/drop_public_wallet_wrappers.sql.pending`,
with its preconditions.
- `atomic_daily_credit_refresh` and `atomic_grant_renewal_credits` have
no caller, so they are dropped. An apply-time guard refuses the drop if
a function body or pg_cron job still calls them.
- `uniq_credit_ledger_idempotency_key` is a partial unique index on
`credit_ledger(idempotency_key)`, built in a `.concurrent.ts` migration.
A read-only check before this PR found 0 duplicate keys on dev, staging
and prod. When two concurrent grants use the same key, the second one's
insert now fails with 23505, and the wallet reports a replay.

### 2. Schema contract

```text
db-migrations.yml / shadow-db
  migrate (empty PostgreSQL)
  migrate:status
+ bun scripts/schema-contract.ts   kortix.ts <-> catalog: relations (table|view), columns,
+                                  indexes (name, relation, uniqueness, validity), unique constraints
```

- Both directions are checked. The exceptions are listed with reasons in
`scripts/schema-contract-sql-only.ts`: 1 legacy table, 3 compatibility
views, 21 legacy columns and 62 non-unique indexes. The list only
shrinks, and a unique index is never allowed on it.
- Drift fixed in `kortix.ts`, with no DB change:
- `account_members`, `project_members`, `project_group_grants`,
`iam_policies` and `iam_resource_grants` are now declared as
`.existing()` views. They were declared as tables.
- `iamRoles`, `iamRoleActions` and `accountGroupMembers` are now
declared on the physical `roles`, `role_permissions` and `group_members`
tables. The views they replaced were plain pass-through views, so reads
and writes do not change.
- Unique indexes and constraints that only SQL knew about are now
declared.
- Two phantom index declarations are removed:
`idx_account_members_user_id` and
`kortix_credit_accounts_account_id_idx`.
- `idx_account_members_account_id` is now built with `CONCURRENTLY` on
`account_memberships`. Prod already has it under this name, so the build
is a no-op there. Dev, staging and fresh databases did not have it, and
account-only membership reads seq-scanned.
- Test fixtures that wrote through the five compatibility views now go
through `apps/api/src/__tests__/helpers/compat-views.ts`. It writes
through the same INSTEAD OF triggers. No product code writes those
views.
- The drizzle snapshot is regenerated on top of main's tail. drizzle-kit
proposed SQL for objects that already exist, and that SQL is discarded.
`schema-sync` shows `No schema changes, nothing to migrate`.
- `MIGRATIONS.md` documents the contract and the
declare-and-build-CONCURRENTLY workflow for a new index.

## Evidence

- **Characterization:** `tests/migration/wallet-ledger.test.ts` is
unchanged (`git diff` is empty). It passes 29/29 in both of these runs:
- with the previous wallet module, which calls the `public.*` wrappers
against the new SQL (the mixed-version case);
  - with the new module, which calls `kortix_wallet.*`.
- **Concurrent same-key grant**, two transactions interleaved on real
PostgreSQL:
**Before (no unique index):**
`{"secondError":null,"ledgerRows":2,"balance":"10"}`, a double grant.
**After:** `{"secondError":"23505","ledgerRows":1,"balance":"5"}`. This
is pinned in `tests/migration/credit-rpc-overloads.test.ts`.
- **Duplicate-key marker:** the `duplicate-error.test.ts` case
"recognizes the unique idempotency-key index" failed before the marker
was added (1 fail), and passes after it.
- **Schema contract**, run against a freshly migrated PostgreSQL 16:
**Before (main's kortix.ts):** 49 drift lines, for example
`account_members: declared as a table, but it is a view`,
`idx_iam_policies_scope: declared index on iam_policies was never
built`, and `uq_role_assignments_identity: the database has this unique
index on role_assignments, but kortix.ts does not declare it`.
  **After:** `OK — kortix.ts describes the migrated schema.`
- **Local gates:**
  - `packages/db` `bun test`: 285 pass, 0 fail.
  - `bun test tests/migration`: 60 pass, 0 fail.
  - `apps/api` unit suite: 10,369 pass, 0 fail.
  - `tsc --noEmit` is clean for `packages/db`, `apps/api` and `tests`.
  - `lint-migrations` and squawk report 0 issues.
- **Integration suites edited for the view fixtures** (run against a
migrated PostgreSQL):
- iam-engine, token-scope-expiry, service-account, resource-scope, apps
access, approvals, connection-authorization, detail-capability,
feature-flag, members-manage, member-session-prompt, project-read-leaf,
personal-tokens, trigger-session-access and tunnel-ownership all pass.
- iam-sso-sync, preview-agent-authz, member-model and project-write-leaf
show the same failure counts on unmodified main in the same environment,
so these failures are environmental and existed before this PR.
- **PostgREST (v14.15, anon role) against the migrated database:**
- Schema not exposed: `POST /rpc/debit_credits` with `Content-Profile:
kortix_wallet` returns `406 PGRST106`.
- Schema exposed: all three functions, called with full argument sets,
return `401 42501 permission denied for schema kortix_wallet`.
  - `public.atomic_use_credits` returns `401 42501`.
  - The dropped `atomic_daily_credit_refresh` returns `404 PGRST202`.

SEC-K asserts the same responses. It runs in the core lane of this PR,
not locally.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way for code. One-way for the migration: it creates a
schema and an index, and drops two dead functions.

Rolling the API back to an older image is safe, because the `public.*`
wrappers delegate to the new functions. Do not merge the parked
wrapper-drop migration until every environment runs an image from this
PR or later.

**Blast Radius:** billing

Every credit movement goes through the moved functions. The
mixed-version run above covers both API generations. The unique index
build waits up to 180 s on live transactions, and its runbook is in
MIGRATIONS.md "When it has already failed".

A deleted session is no longer marked `failed` or `running` by provisioning or by the wake finalize. **2. Fenced lease for `session_lifecycle_commands`** (`session-lifecycle/command-lease.ts`). ```text claim status=running, locked_by= succeed|forward|fail|requeue|park|release(lease, …) WHERE command_id AND status='running' AND locked_by = lease.lockedBy withCommandLeaseHeartbeat(lease, work) renews locked_until every LOCK/3 while the drain lane or inline create runs reclaim unchanged: running AND locked_until <= now - grace, under a new locked_by ``` The writers take the claimed row (`CommandLease`) instead of a command id.
