fix(identity): trust SSO emails only on verified domains; scope IAM writes to the account (#7615)

## Summary

Identity inputs now carry only the trust they have earned:

- An email a SAML IdP asserts is trusted outside the IdP's own account
only for a domain that account verified.
- `enforce_sso` applies only to a verified domain, and the API's own
sign-in routes enforce it.
- A project-scoped IAM assignment must name a project of the account it
is written in.
- Losing the owner role ends the super-admin bypass.
- SAML JIT sync runs once per login session instead of on every request.

## Changes

### SSO domain verification (new)
- `account_sso_providers.domain_verification_token` /
`domain_verified_at` (migration `…_sso_domain_verification`). Providers
that exist before the migration count as verified from their creation
time, so current enterprise setups keep working. New providers and any
`primary_domain` change start unverified.
- `POST /v1/accounts/:accountId/iam/sso/provider/verify-domain`: reads
the DNS TXT record `_kortix-verification.<domain>` =
`kortix-verification=<token>`. Returns 422 `sso_domain_unverified` with
the record to publish, or 409 `sso_domain_claimed` when another account
verified the domain first.
- `PUT /v1/admin/api/accounts/:id/sso-domain-verification {verified}`:
operator path, audited as `admin.account.sso_domain.set`.
- The provider response gains `domain_verified`, `domain_verified_at`
and `domain_verification`.
- SDK: `verifySsoDomain(accountId)` and `SsoDomainVerificationRecord`.
Additive only; both surface snapshots are updated.
- Web: the SSO card shows the TXT record and a **Verify domain** action.
**Enforce SSO** can be turned on only for a verified domain; turning it
off always works.
- Docs: `accounts.mdx` gains "Single sign-on domain" and the super-admin
demotion rule.

### Email trust (`apps/api/src/iam/email-trust.ts`)
One rule decides whether an Auth user's email proves ownership: a
non-SSO identity, or an SSO identity whose provider verified that
email's domain. It is used by:
- invite list, describe, accept and decline (`accounts/invites.ts`). An
unverified SSO email matches no invite; accept and decline return 403
`sso_email_domain_unverified`.
- `resolveAccountIdentityByEmail` (add member by email, project invite).
An SSO identity from another account's IdP must be vouched for by a
verified domain.

### SAML JIT (`iam/sso-sync.ts`, `iam/account-identity.ts`,
`middleware/auth.ts`)
- `identitiesMergeableIntoSso` controls which identities are merged into
the IdP identity. It merges only when the provider verified the email's
domain, and never merges an owner or a super-admin of the account. A
skipped identity stays a separate member.
- The same-provider duplicate check reads the indexed
`auth.identities.email` instead of scanning `auth.users`.
- The auth middleware remembers a successful sync per (user, IdP, login
session, claims) for 5 minutes. A failed sync is retried on the next
request.

### `enforce_sso`
- `ssoEnforcedForEmail` (repositories/sso.ts): `enforce_sso` AND a
verified domain. When several providers claim one domain, the verified
provider wins.
- `/v1/access/check-email` and headless `/v1/auth/sign-in/password`,
`/sign-in/magic-link` and `/verify-otp` return 403 `sso_required` for an
enforced verified domain.

### IAM account scope
- `assignRole` and `updateAssignment` refuse a `scope_id` that is not a
project of the URL account (404 `project not found in this account`).
- `loadObjectGrants` and `projectRoleForUser` count only rows whose
`account_id` is the project's account.
- Storage guard: trigger `role_assignments_project_account_guard`
rejects a new or re-scoped project row across accounts (migration
`…_project_assignment_account_guard`).

### Owner demotion
- When a user loses the account-scope `owner` assignment,
`is_super_admin` is cleared and `iam.member.super_admin.revoke` is
recorded. This covers the exclusive grant used by `PATCH
/members/:userId`, revoke, and policy update. A super-admin flag granted
to a non-owner is unchanged.

### Legacy RLS
- The same migration drops the legacy `"Give read only access to
internal users"` policies on `public.messages`, `public.projects` and
`public.threads` where they exist. Each drop is guarded by `to_regclass`
and `IF EXISTS`.

## Tests

(`tests/src/flows/sso-identity.flow.ts`), and `IAM-41`, `IAM-42`

- `middleware/auth-sso-sync.test.ts`: 9 pass. New cases: one sync per

fix(web): harden markdown, frames, credential routing, share links and analytics (#7617)

## Summary

Web rendering, framing, credential routing and analytics hardening, plus
two supporting API/SDK additions.

## Changes

1. **Markdown sanitizer** (`components/markdown/katex-markdown.ts`): raw
HTML keeps structure and text, never `style` or class names. Only the
remark-math classes and `language-*` survive on `code`. KaTeX and code
highlighting still render (they run after sanitize).
2. **Remote images** (`UnifiedMarkdown` `remoteImages="click-to-load"`):
scrape results, generic tool output and the share viewer show a button
in place of an image hosted outside the app; it loads on click.
3. **Mermaid** (`components/ui/mermaid-renderer.tsx`,
`mermaid-render.ts`): the document-wide cleanup sweep and its 5 s
interval are removed. Mermaid initializes with `suppressErrorRendering`;
cleanup removes only the two nodes one render created.
4. **Agent-authored frames** (`lib/security/iframe-sandbox.ts`): the
`show` card and deck slides keep `allow-same-origin` only on an origin
of their own. On the app origin, the configured app URL or the API
origin (path proxy), they run with an opaque origin, the policy
`HtmlPreview` already applies.
5. **Tunnel permission dialog** (`features/tunnel/permission-scope.ts`):
pre-fills from the server's `paths` / `operations` / `commands` /
`workingDir` / `maxTimeout`, keeps the full command, and omits empty
optional fields. An emptied restriction list is still sent so the server
refuses it.
6. **Connector credentials** (`connector-credential-target.ts`,
`connectors-view.tsx`): a static or `client_credentials` credential for
a selected shared account goes through the per-connection route. The
OAuth2 discovery query is keyed per connection
(`qk.project.connectorOAuth2Discovery` gains an optional third argument;
the two-argument key stays the prefix).
7. **Copy link** (`hooks/use-public-share-link.ts`,
`PublicShareLinkConfirm`): opens a confirmation; only the confirm action
creates and copies the public link. File viewer, browser panel and share
button render it.
8. **Session mentions** (`lib/project-preamble.ts`,
`message-parsing.tsx`, mobile `user-message.ts`): both composer paths
use `buildSessionRef`; ids and titles are attribute-escaped (including
`<` `>`) and unescaped on parse.
9. **Chat identity consent**: new `POST
/v1/channels/{slack,teams}/identity/preview` (authenticated, read-only,
same token checks as `/bind`), SDK `previewSlackIdentity` /
`previewTeamsIdentity` / `ChatIdentityPreview` (additive), and the
consent screen names the chat account and workspace. Connect stays
disabled until the preview resolves.
10. **Analytics** (`lib/analytics/gtm.ts`): `page_location` /
`page_referrer` keep only campaign parameters. Expired-link redirects
and the magic-link callback URL no longer carry the email (nothing read
it). GTM and the visitor pixel do not load when the document opens on a
signed-in or capability-token page (`/projects`, `/admin`, `/settings`,
`/secret-intake`, `/connect`, `/share`, chat login pages, …).
11. **Headers** (`lib/security/content-security-policy.ts`,
`next.config.ts`): enforced CSP adds `object-src 'none'` and `base-uri
'self'`; a `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` `script-src` allowlist
reports to `/api/csp-report` (logs directive, blocked origin, first path
segment only); adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and
`Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`.

### Decisions to review

- **`script-src` is report-only, not enforced.** The root layout renders
several inline bootstrap scripts, and GTM, Stripe, PostHog, Vercel and
the visitor pixel load their own scripts. An enforced list that misses
one host breaks sign-in or checkout, and no local check can prove it
complete. Enforce after a release cycle of clean `[csp-report]` logs,
with nonces for the inline scripts.
- **GTM exclusion is decided once per document.** A loaded script cannot
be unloaded, so a visitor who opens a marketing page and then navigates
into the app in the same tab keeps that container.
- **Sign-up/login conversion events** fire on `/projects?auth_event=…`.
With GTM excluded there, those events no longer reach GTM on a direct
post-auth landing. Needs a product decision if the conversions matter.
- **Path-proxy deployments**: the deck slide editor frame now runs with
an opaque origin there. Preview-origin deployments (cloud
dev/staging/prod) are unchanged.

fix(tests): SCOPE-6 uses the Git proxy on deployed targets (#7628) SCOPE-6 (added in #7613) cloned `kortix.projects.repo_url` directly. On a deployed target that is the private managed GitHub repository, so every preview and staging `--target-full` run failed SCOPE-6 with `fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com'` (preview runs 36068206735, twice). Change: when `repo_url` is a remote URL, the flow mints an OWNER token, clones and pushes through `/v1/git/:projectId` with an `Authorization` header passed via `GIT_CONFIG_*` environment (never argv, so a failing git command cannot print it), and revokes the token in `finally`. Local targets keep cloning the bare repository. Same pattern as `AgentPrincipalFixture.commitToMain`. - `pnpm test -- --id SCOPE-6` (local): PASS 25.6 s. - `tests` typecheck clean; `meta.routes` gains the two token routes. - Deployed-path proof: the next preview `--target-full` run on any branch that includes this commit. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

fix(preview): reclaim session sandboxes with their host (#7569)

Preview APIs ran without the deadline reaper, so test-created Platinum
session sandboxes stayed running until the provider's 12-hour idle
timer. On 2026-09-23, those idle sessions exhausted the shared 512 GB
RAM pool and blocked preview and development sessions.

This change:
- stamps every preview session sandbox with its host instance id;
- runs the deadline reaper inside each preview API, scoped to that
instance;
- stops ephemeral preview sessions when the suite exits;
- stops child sessions before host replacement or teardown;
- replaces a detached remote suite left by a cancelled workflow before
reusing its host;
- sweeps running preview sessions whose host no longer exists, plus
untagged legacy sessions idle over six hours;
- keeps persistent branch sessions intact during redeploys;
- sets a 60-minute provider auto-stop backstop;
- reports provider pool usage and top consumers in preview logs.

Session cleanup uses `stop`, so session disks remain recoverable. The
selectors require `kortix.managed=true`, `kortix.env=preview`, and
`kortix.workload=session`. Development, staging, production, app, CI,
and host sandboxes are excluded.

Validation:

- focused preview lifecycle tests — 46/46 passed

apps/api/src/platform/providers/platinum-list-managed.test.ts` — 5/5

reports the final SHA

The preview workflow intentionally runs its deployment controller from
`main`. The target-full run on the preceding SHA passed before the final

change.

refactor(billing): one wallet module for every credit movement (#7624) ## Summary Every credit movement now goes through one module, `apps/api/src/billing/wallet`, with one key contract. Ledger rows are unchanged. ```diff apps/api/src/ ├── billing/ +│ ├── wallet/ +│ │ ├── index.ts # wallet.grant / debit / settle / reset / forfeit / balance +│ │ ├── duplicate-error.ts # moved from services/credit-duplicate-error.ts +│ │ ├── fake.ts # in-memory wallet for caller unit tests +│ │ └── wallet.test.ts # failure branches │ ├── services/ -│ │ ├── credits.ts # grantCredits, deductCredits, deductForLlmUsage, resetExpiringCredits, getBalance (+ 2 read-modify-write fallbacks) +│ │ ├── credits.ts # getCreditSummary, calculateTokenCost only (385 → 82 lines) -│ │ └── settle-credits.ts # settleCredits │ └── repositories/ -│ └── transactions.ts # insertLedgerEntry -└── repositories/credits.ts # router checkCredits / deductCredits (second debit path) ``` ```text wallet.grant({ accountId, amount, kind, description, expiring, expiresAt?, key }) wallet.debit({ accountId, amount, description, kind, key }) # admission, throws InsufficientCreditsError wallet.settle({ …, audit? }) # settlement, may overdraw wallet.reset({ accountId, amount, description, key }) wallet.forfeit(accountId) wallet.balance(accountId) → buckets | null key: { event: id } → stripe_event_id (UNIQUE) grant, reset { request: id } → idempotency_key debit, settle, grant null → not idempotent; must be written at the call site ``` - Transport: the wallet calls the existing `public.atomic_*` SQL functions with named arguments over `DATABASE_URL`, not PostgREST. No migration, no SQL change. - Deleted: both Drizzle read-modify-write fallbacks in `grantCredits` / `resetExpiringCredits`. They ran only when PostgREST returned an error; on the shared connection they would query the same database that just failed. - A deliberate change: a `{ request }`-keyed grant checks the whole ledger in the same statement. `atomic_add_credits` looks back only 1 hour. This affects the gateway hold refund and the trial monthly re-grant. The trial sweep's own ledger pre-check is deleted. - Callers migrated (25 call sites): LLM gateway settlement, compute metering, billing gate, `/billing/deduct*`, router tool/LLM debits and reservation refunds, Stripe and RevenueCat webhooks, subscriptions, auto-topup, proration grants, free tier, rotations, trials, legacy sync and migration, admin credit routes, account deletion, and 2 operator scripts. ## Evidence The first commit (`3148b3b595`) adds `tests/migration/wallet-ledger.test.ts`. It runs against a fully migrated throwaway PostgreSQL and pins the exact `credit_ledger` row and `credit_accounts` buckets for each operation, plus replay, concurrency and refusal behaviour. - **Before:** on the old code, with PostgREST emulated by calling the same SQL function with the same named arguments: `28 pass, 0 fail`. **After:** on the wallet: `29 pass, 0 fail`. The added test moves the old `credit-overdraft-guard` coverage (drain to zero, then refuse) to real PostgreSQL. - Between the 2 commits, no ledger-row or bucket expectation changed. Only return shapes changed (`{success,cost,newBalance}` → `{amount,balance,replayed}`), plus this one: ```diff -test('a request-keyed grant replayed after an hour applies again') → 2 rows +test('a request-keyed grant replayed after an hour still applies once') → 1 row ``` Local runs on this branch: - `bun test --max-concurrency 2 tests/migration`: 55 pass, 0 fail. - `apps/api` unit suite (`bash scripts/test.sh`): 10355 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `pi-worker-park.test.ts` (a port handshake, unrelated to billing). It passes 3 of 3 times when run alone. - `pnpm test` with the API started from this worktree: 452/452 flows passed, and the sdk, flow-runner, route-coverage and worktree lanes passed. - `pnpm test -- --domain billing`: 21/21 passed. - `tsc --noEmit -p apps/api`: clean. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way No migration and no SQL change. The rows are identical, so old and new pods can run side by side during a rollout. A revert restores the PostgREST path. **Blast Radius:** billing - Every wallet operation now takes one short pooled `DATABASE_URL` statement where it used to make a PostgREST HTTP call. This is most visible on the LLM gateway settle path. The pool size and the 25 s statement timeout are unchanged. - Without the fallbacks, a database error during a grant or reset now throws. Stripe and RevenueCat webhooks fail and are redelivered. Operator routes return 500. - Log prefixes change from `[Credits]` to `[Wallet]`. No alert config in the repository references them. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. Autofix is disabled.

feat(listen): capture-position clock for transcripts, audio and live speaker ID (#18995)

* feat(listen): pure audio-timeline v2 primitives

One capture coordinate: a per-socket integer sample cursor over decoded
PCM16 mono, with arrival-time anchors at the first accepted frame and at
measured inter-arrival hiatuses (2 s jitter guard, monotonic-confirmed so
a wall-clock step never mints an hour of audio). Provider timestamps
translate only through SendMap spans the provider actually accepted;
out-of-range or evicted ranges fail closed. segment_wall_window is the
one wall-time conversion; covered_window/coverage_outcome never guess
coverage from timestamps alone. AUDIO_TIMELINE_V2 flag helper is pure
config/, read at the call boundary, default off.

* feat(listen): capture sample timeline through receiver, STT epochs and pusher audio runs

Eligible sessions (flag on, single-channel, server STT) get a
CaptureTimeline; every decoded frame occupies an exact sample range that
is carried into the ring buffer (span ledger), the STT buffer (contiguous
start sample) and the pusher audio runs. Each selected provider socket
gets its own epoch translator created at callback-creation time (legacy
callbacks and the managed chain both rebuild per epoch); the VAD gate
tracks pre-roll/source spans and GatedSTTSocket/LiveLegSocket record
only sends the provider accepted. Mapped segments resolve their owning
conversation from the capture span; straddling segments are dropped.

listen_pusher_session buffers AudioRun(conversation_id, start_wall,
bytes) captured at acceptance, sends one 101 per contiguous
same-conversation run with the retained projected start (opcode 103
ahead of boundaries), and performs the opt-in audio_timeline=2
capability handshake: ack required before any v2 audio and on every
reconnect; capability loss mid-recording withholds audio as a coverage
gap instead of terminating or silently downgrading.

* feat(listen): pin conversation first-audio origin with fenced v2 marker

started_at is set once from the first accepted audio frame associated
with the conversation (not conversation creation, not the first
segment), so pre-roll can leave the first segment at a positive offset
and delayed callbacks cannot shift an origin already emitted to
clients. update_conversation_segments pins the typed audio_timeline
marker and the projected origin in one transaction, only while the row
has no marker; once pinned, stale started_at writes are ignored.

The conversation controller tracks per-conversation origins: fresh v2
generations pin at their first accepted frame (receiver), resumed
conversations reuse the persisted started_at and are never marked v2.
TranscriptProcessor processes epoch-translated segments per owning
conversation from the capture span: the current generation gets the
full live path with offsets projected against the pinned origin; a
late batch may still write its still-open owner, and a terminal owner
is fenced out and counted, never replayed into a newer recording.
Photo-only drains keep ordinary wall lifecycle times.

* feat(pusher): v2 continuity, span-carrying chunks and coverage-true storage

Opted-in connections (audio_timeline=2 query param) get an explicit
pusher->listen acknowledgment (opcode 202, fixed version) before any
v2 audio is accepted. v2 audio frames are checked against the last
accepted run's end with 1 ms tolerance: positive discontinuities flush
the partial private-cloud chunk and close the pending batch for upload
(never concatenating across a gap or inside a 60s batch), exact replays
are ignored, partial overlaps are trimmed after verifying the retained
bytes, and conflicting bytes for an accepted range fail closed.

v2 chunk queues carry their authoritative PCM sample count; uploads
stamp span metadata on the blob and refuse to overwrite a colliding
filename with differing bytes. Listing rehydrates spans; grouping
splits at actual uncovered ends (or overlaps) rather than start-to-start
differences; AudioFile exposes validated chunk_spans whose layout joins
the artifact fingerprint; span-aware merging trims overlaps and
silence-fills only real gaps. Legacy listings behave exactly as before.

* feat(listen): coverage-gated audio consumers

Clips, speaker-tag prompt selection and speaker-sample extraction use
the central helpers: for v2-marked conversations the actual selected
window must be covered by validated chunk_spans (clip endpoint rechecks
through the same conversation_clip_pcm); uncovered, pending-upload,
unsupported and no-audio windows are unavailable rather than a clip of
the wrong audio, with bounded coverage counters at each check. Legacy
conversations keep the timestamp-based best-effort behavior unchanged.
v2 playback parts are contiguous by construction (grouping splits at
every real gap), so one span per part keeps the released clients'
strict-seek arithmetic.

* docs(listen): audio timeline v2 wire/storage contract; dev-on prod-off flag

listen_pusher_pipeline.mdx owns the overlap env/wire contract and now
documents the v2 capture coordinate, epoch translation, the
audio_timeline=2 query-parameter handshake with the opcode-202
acknowledgment, discontinuity/overlap reconciliation, span-carrying
blobs and the coverage-gated consumers. AUDIO_TIMELINE_V2 is true in
the dev backend-listen and pusher values and explicitly false in prod;
no dev backend Cloud Run env surface exists (backend-listen and pusher
deploy through the GKE charts).

* test(listen): hermetic receiver->pusher->storage->clip v2 regression

Drives the actual receiver frame/epoch logic, ListenPusherSession run
buffering, the pusher websocket handler (ack, continuity, batch split,
span uploads), storage upload/listing/grouping/merge, the fenced
conversation persistence and the clip helper against in-memory doubles.

The same burst scenario runs with the flag off — which IS the legacy
calculation — and asserts the acceptance criterion fails there: the
chunk timestamp (last arrival minus the whole buffered run) lands ~10 s
away from the segment position (first audio + provider time), coverage
is unsupported and no correct clip exists. With v2 on: origin pinned to
the first accepted frame, an hour-long wall step mints no audio and no
anchor, a reconnect rebuilds the provider epoch with provider time
restarted, the rollover conversation pins its own origin, out-of-range
provider segments reject, and clips return the exact phrase bytes.
Capability loss withholds buffered audio and never downgrades.

Also: ownership ranges are bounded by capture time (120 s) not a tiny
frame count, batch uploads carry the span start, and the v2 branch in
process_loop reads the timeline defensively for stub hosts.

* feat(probe): opt-in audio-timeline alignment scenario for dev

--alignment-scenario paces two >8 s speech windows in real time with
delivered silence and one actual bounded inter-arrival gap, holds the
socket open through finalization, and checks the v2 marker, span
coverage of the transcript windows, /v1/sync/audio urls, and the clip
endpoint with verify_and_transcribe_sample as an auxiliary ASR check
only (deterministic PCM identity stays the hermetic gate). Enrollment
in private-cloud sync is verified/attempted first; NOT_RUN — never
PASS — when the dev identity cannot enable it. Receipts carry no
transcript, audio, token, or endpoint data; all reads stay inside the
five-minute token TTL. Not executed here: dev-only, run by the
coordinator.

* test(pusher): v2 wire matrix — ack, discontinuity flush, replay, overlap

Old listen (no query parameter) sees no ack and keeps legacy
concatenation; an opted-in connection is acknowledged with opcode 202
before anything else and an unsupported version is refused. A positive
discontinuity uploads the partial run separately (span-carrying, never
concatenated across the gap or inside a pending batch), an exact replay
is ignored, a conflicting overlap fails closed, a partial overlap is
trimmed to continue the run exactly, and a conversation switch flushes
and rebinds. The switch test caught a real bug: the extracted flush
helper skipped the buffer reset, so a switched conversation's audio
appended to the previous conversation's leftover bytes under its old
start; the reset is restored.

* refactor(storage): share v2 span helpers from the pure timeline module

Blob span metadata helpers and coverage-aware chunk grouping move to
utils/audio_timeline.py so storage.py and database/conversations.py keep
only their persistence-specific code (and their line-count growth
shrinks to what the feature genuinely adds there).

* feat(listen): capture-clock speaker ID for every server-STT session

Live speaker identification now locates audio on the capture sample clock
for every single-channel server-STT listen session, not only AUDIO_TIMELINE_V2
admissions. After a mid-session STT failover the replacement provider's
timestamps restart at zero; the legacy first_audio + raw_start window then
lands minutes before the 60s ring buffer and matching returns silently, so
the owner loses live recognition for the rest of the recording even though
the voiceprint is correct.

The sample cursor, per-provider-epoch translators (fresh on every failover
rebuild), the capture-positioned ring buffer and the speaker-ID window are
internal to one listen socket: they run always. Only the v2 persistence
stays flag-gated via state.capture_timeline_v2 (pinned once per recording):
projected segment times, started_at pin/marker and the pusher opcode-101
projection. With the flag off the translator runs in project_times=False
mode - provider-native times pass through untouched, owner fencing is
skipped, unmapped segments stay delivered (origin/main persisted them) -
so persisted fields, WebSocket segment fields and the pusher wire remain
byte-identical to the flag-off baseline; only the speaker-ID window moves.
Multi-channel and custom-STT keep no capture clock at all.

* feat(listen): attributable live speaker-ID match exits

After the 2026-09-25 incident the queued owner detections returned before
any match decision without a single log line; the affected account could
only be attributed by replaying the saved conversation's speaker ids.

Every early return in speakers._match_unmapped and its callers that drops
a queued detection now emits exactly one bounded reason as a Prometheus
counter (label = reason only) plus one log line: window_outside_buffer
(the post-failover clock bug's signature, previously disguised as an
inverted-clamp "too short"), too_short, no_pcm, stale_generation and
already_mapped. Pending evidence accumulation is not a drop - it already
logs and its speaker reaches a decision on the next clip - so it is not

and the replacement stream's timestamps restart at zero, and the owner's

* fix(storage): database-layer pure span helpers; content-hash batch no-overwrite

(datetime/number/ISO string, parsed by persisted_started_seconds in

* fix(listen): introductions run with capture windows; v2 batch parity

P0: queue_from_raw only re-homes the duplicate embedding enqueue; name

so a flag-off pendant user saying 'My name is Alice' keeps the person

writes the v2 marker + started_at — a resumed row projects against its

* fix(pusher): span-walking extract, gap-split 101 frames, flushed-range conflicts

AudioRingBuffer.extract walks the per-write span ledger and copies the bytes
overlapping the window span by span, so a clip crossing a >2 s client stall
returns the audio on both sides instead of converting the whole wall delta
into one byte offset (wrong PCM or ring wraparound). The write path and
per-byte copy are unchanged from origin/main.

ListenPusherSession flushes one 101 frame per contiguous same-conversation
group, splitting when the next run's projected start is more than 1 ms past
the previous run's end, so a disconnect-length gap is never erased from the
stored audio while the header claims the first run's position. Legacy runs
without a projection keep the legacy grouping.

Pusher v2 overlap verification extends past the live buffer through a
bounded digest ledger of flushed runs ((start, end, sha256)); a range that
can be neither byte-compared nor digest-matched is a conflict — the frame is
dropped and counted in omi_audio_timeline_replay_conflicts_total instead of
appending an unverified suffix over stored bytes.

The private-cloud overflow-warning test now asserts the structural invariant
(every enqueue into private_cloud_queue sits in a function that warns) after
the three inline enqueue sites were consolidated into one guarded helper.

* test(listen): accept epoch in the parity socket double; pin audio_timeline field

The parity runtime's _create_stt_socket double predates the epoch argument
the receiver passes (round-1/2 addition the coordinator's partial CI run
never reached), so initialize_stt failed silently and the capture-once
acceptance lost its socket. Conversation.audio_timeline is pinned in the

(never client-authored, no text).

* fix(pusher): drain the retry lane when no batch is pending; fix connect double arity

A failed private-cloud upload's retry batch lives in ready_batches, but the
loop's 'if not pending: continue' skipped the ready-lane drain, leaving the
loop condition truthy forever — a busy spin once shutdown is set (the upload-
failure test hung at 100% CPU). The guard now also checks ready_batches.

The circuit-breaker connect double predates the audio_timeline parameter the
branch added to _connect_to_trigger_pusher; the signature mismatch raised at
call time before the double could set its started event, hanging the stale-
inflight test on await started.wait().

* fix(listen): managed chain keeps the legacy offset rebase in clock-only mode; rebuild-factory stubs

With the capture clock on and v2 persistence off, the managed chain's
callback translated epochs and dropped the leg's own offset/last_end clock,
so flag-off emitted times restarted at 0 per leg instead of staying
monotonic like the pre-timeline managed chain. Clock-only legs now translate
first (attaching the capture window from provider timestamps), then apply
the same gate remap and offset rebase as the epoch-less path, and enqueue
through the receiver's pinned mode. v2 legs keep the projected translation.

The _stt_rebuild tuple became a callback FACTORY in round 1 (a fresh epoch
translator per rebuild); three failover test files still stubbed the old
callbacks-tuple shape and crashed the rebuild with a TypeError.

* chore(failure-classes): FC-transcript-and-audio-on-independent-clocks

Defines the class this branch closes: transcript times and stored/buffered
audio placed by independent clocks (STT provider offset vs frame arrival),
which drifted up to 54 minutes and silently broke clip playback and live
owner recognition after a provider failover.

* fix(listen): owner fail-open only inside the retention horizon

A sample older than the oldest retained run no longer fails open to the
single surviving conversation: retention may have evicted the run — and
every boundary — that owned the sample, so the retained window cannot
prove ownership and the segment stays late_owner_dropped (re-review N1).
The single-conversation fail-open now applies only between retained runs,
inside the retention horizon, where no run covering the sample could have
been evicted yet.

* fix(storage): an exists() probe failure fails closed like an unreadable blob

A raised blob.exists() on the v2 no-overwrite path was swallowed as
'absent', so the upload opened the blob for write and replaced whatever
object actually sat at the colliding 3-decimal batch key (re-review N2).
Any exception from the probe now raises the same ValueError as an
unreadable existing blob and never opens the blob for write.

* fix(pusher): keep the new tail past last_end on an unverifiable v2 replay

An overlap that could be neither byte-compared nor digest-matched dropped
the whole 101 frame, losing the frame's genuinely new audio past the
accepted end as a coverage hole (re-review N3). The conflict branch now
trims to the bytes past audio_timeline_last_end and continues the run
there, still never storing the unverified overlap and still counting the
conflict.

The flushed-run digest ledger is now recorded only after a batch's GCS
upload succeeds (one contiguous entry per batch), so a chunk evicted by
the bounded queue or a batch dropped after exhausting its retries leaves
no entry: replays of that range are unverifiable conflicts instead of
being trusted by a digest whose bytes were never stored.

* fix(pusher): pace ready-lane upload retries one process interval

A failed upload re-queued itself at the front of the ready lane, so the
in-turn while-loop retried it immediately: one fast permanent error
burned the whole retry budget in a single tick, and one slow timeout
blocked this socket's uploader for back-to-back attempts (re-review N4).
The retry now keeps its queue time and is gated by retry_at for one
PRIVATE_CLOUD_SYNC_PROCESS_INTERVAL tick; the gate is skipped during
shutdown so the drain stays bounded.

* fix(listen): deferred STT callbacks count rejections and carry their own segments

A provider callback deferred onto the listen loop via call_soon_threadsafe
ran on the caller's segment list and, if it raised, died as a bare asyncio
callback error: the batch was gone with no counter and no log (re-review
N5). The hop now copies the segment list (a provider may reuse its buffer
once the callback returns) and wraps the deferred action so a failure
increments omi_audio_timeline_segments_total{outcome=rejected} for the
session's mode and logs one bounded line (exception type and count only).
The closed-loop drop stays.

* test(pusher): overflow warning must guard the private-cloud enqueue

The overflow check counted the 'private_cloud_queue full' string anywhere
in the enqueuing function, so a second enqueue on a path the fullness
check never runs on (before it, or in an early return above it) would
drop the oldest chunk silently (re-review N6). The AST test now also
requires the warning's fullness branch to precede each enqueue on its
statement path, and proves the checker flags a synthetic early-return
enqueue.

* docs(listen): round-4 replay, ownership, and loop-hop behavior

The digest ledger is per uploaded batch and written only after the GCS
upload succeeds; an unverifiable replay keeps its new tail past the
accepted end; upload retries are paced by the process interval; the
ownership fail-open is bounded by the retention horizon; deferred STT
callbacks count rejections on their own segment copy.

feat(speakers): resolve one speaker id per voice across a conversation (#18952) ## Problem The mobile conversation header reads "You + 1720 others" on a 3.6h pendant dinner with about six people. Capture restarts speaker numbering on every reconnect, provider failover and uploaded sync chunk (`sync:{segment_id}`, at most 300s). `ConversationSpeakerIdAllocator` gives every `(scope, label)` a fresh conversation id. On top of that, per-chunk diarization over-splits far-field audio. Measured on the owner's own prod conversations (read with their permission): | conversation | segments | scopes | `speaker_id`s | header today | |---|---|---|---|---| | dinner, 3h38m | 2391 | 176 | 1874 | You + 1720 others | | goodbye, 6m47s | 65 | 6 | 52 | You + 47 others | | call, 4.5 min | 12 | 4 | 6 | — | The same fragmentation affects more than the header: - The transcript labels voices up to "Speaker 1874". - Answering a speaker-tag prompt names seven seconds of a person. - Manual "assign speaker" labels one fragment. - Owner attribution sees the owner as dozens of clusters: 243 of the owner's 829 segments in one cluster were marked `is_user`. ## Fix: one speaker id per voice across the conversation `process_conversation` now resolves speakers before it summarizes, on every trigger (`utils/conversations/speaker_resolution.py` → pure `utils/stt/conversation_speakers.py`): 1. **Embed.** Each segment of at least 1s gets an embedding from the stored private-cloud audio, using the production diarizer (`/v2/embedding`, wespeaker). - Each chunk blob is decoded on its own. Merging chunks drifts wherever stored chunks overlap: 2.8s in the goodbye, which shifted every later clip. - Embeddings are cached, encrypted, at `audio/{uid}/{conversation_id}/speaker-embeddings.v1.enc`. A conversation that grows through 54 sync updates embeds each segment once, and conversation and account deletion already purge that prefix. 2. **Cluster.** Average-linkage AHC at cosine 0.70. Short-clip fragments within 0.60 of a voice with at least 30s of speech are absorbed into it. 3. **Identify.** Each voice's pooled centroid is matched to enrolled voiceprints at 0.50 + 0.10 margin, and voices that match the same identity are merged. - Pooled owner voices sat 0.24–0.33 from the voiceprint. A companion pooled at 0.63, inside the per-clip 0.65, which would have named them the owner. 4. **Receipts constrain it.** - A labeled `speaker_id` keeps its id, so the commit's receipt re-application still lands on it. - Ids labeled as the same person become one voice. - Two different labeled identities never merge. - A voiceprint never overrides a manual label. 5. **Rewrite.** Covered segments get `speaker_id_scope = conversation:{id}`, `speaker = SPEAKER_{id}`, and, for a voiceprint match, `speaker_match_source = conversation_voice`. Ids are chosen for stability: a voice keeps the capture id carrying most of its speech, so re-running is idempotent. The result rides the existing fenced processing write. `Conversation.speaker_resolution = {status, version, participant_speaker_ids}` tells clients whether ids are people: - `resolved`: at least 90% of embeddable speech was placed by voice evidence or a label. - `capture`: one scope and no audio, so capture's ids stand. - `unavailable`: anything else. Participants are voices with at least 10s of speech. The app counts unnamed voices only when the status is `resolved` or `capture`. Otherwise it shows "You + others" (new l10n key `participantsSummaryUncounted`, 49 locales). **Scope limit: sync-captured conversations only for now.** Live `started_at` drifts up to 54 minutes from the arrival-stamped chunks until the capture-position clock lands (`omi-knowledge-base/projects/audio-timeline`), and misplaced audio would merge the wrong voices. Live scopes keep capture's ids and report `capture` or `unavailable`. **Failure behavior.** Everything fails open onto capture's ids: no audio, diarizer outage (three consecutive failures), budget (45s / 1500 embeddings per run; the next run resumes from the cache), or any exception. `CONVERSATION_SPEAKER_RESOLUTION_ENABLED=false` is the registered kill switch. ## Evidence **Calibration and real-path runs.** Run on the owner's conversations with the real stage code: GCS chunk listing and decrypt/decode, clip placement, HTTP embedding client, Firestore receipt and voiceprint reads. The embedding endpoint was a local wespeaker stand-in, and cache writes went to local disk. Nothing was persisted. | conversation | ids before | participants after | owner-labeled segments | |---|---|---|---| | dinner | 1874 | 6 (You + 5) | 409 → ~1100 | | goodbye | 52 | 4 (You + 3) | 15 → 33 | | call (desktop mic/system ground truth: 2 people) | 6 | 2 (You + 1) ✓ | 9 → 11 | - **Clip alignment** was checked by transcribing clips with faster-whisper against the stored segment text: chunk placement matches, the merged-artifact placement does not. - **Owner purity** was measured against the enrolled voiceprint. Across AHC 0.65–0.75 × absorb 0.50–0.65, no confident-owner clip left the owner's voice, and at most 5 confident non-owner clips joined it. At 0.80 the owner absorbed 106, which is why 0.80 was rejected. - **Diarizer headroom (prod, read-only).** One T4 averages 7.6% GPU utilization (80% peak over a day). It autoscales on p99 latency, currently 80ms against a 300ms target, up to 10 replicas. The stage adds roughly one embedding per new sync segment. **Tests.** - `backend/tests/unit/test_conversation_speakers.py` (15): pure resolution. Covers fragmentation, stability, receipts (keep id / merge same person / never merge two people), voiceprint merges and the 0.6-near-owner regression, short-clip inheritance, the sentinel, fresh-id collisions, and partial coverage. - `backend/tests/unit/test_conversation_speaker_resolution_stage.py` (14): the stage with fake storage and diarizer. Covers rewrite, cache reuse (zero re-embeds), owner labeling, receipt, no audio, live scopes, diarizer outage, exceptions, kill switch, midpoint ordering (fails on start ordering), and a partial run resuming to `resolved`. - `app/test/unit/capture_groups_test.dart`: the header rules, including the 1720-fragment legacy case, and the wire/cache round trip. - The full backend unit suite ran locally via `test.sh`. ## Product invariants affected - INV-MEM-4 — cited because `process_conversation.py` changed. Canonical memory promotion is untouched: speaker resolution only rewrites `speaker_id`/scope and voiceprint-backed `is_user`/`person_id` on transcript segments before extraction. No intake route, consolidation, or Long-term admission changes. - INV-TASK-2 — cited because `process_conversation.py` changed. Task capture is untouched: no task is created, proposed, or written by this stage. ## Line-count exceptions Line-Count-Exception: backend/database/conversations.py | 3043 -> 3061 | field-masked manual-receipt read belongs to the conversation persistence owner beside decode_manual_speaker_assignments Line-Count-Exception: backend/utils/conversations/process_conversation.py | 3371 -> 3374 | one call into the new speaker-resolution module plus its import; the stage itself lives outside this file Line-Count-Exception: backend/utils/other/storage.py | 1844 -> 1901 | encrypted speaker-embedding cache and per-blob chunk iterator reuse the private-cloud bucket, owner write gate, and chunk decoder that only this module owns (the decoder moved out of a closure, not duplicated) ## Follow-ups - Resolve live conversations once the capture-position clock is on main. - Re-run the calibration with more labeled conversations; the thresholds are env-tunable. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

fix(desktop): split back-to-back calls into separate conversations (#18950)

* fix(desktop): split back-to-back calls into separate conversations

MeetingDetector only reported whether a call was on, with an 8 s off grace,
and conversations rotated only on its edges. Leaving one Google Meet and
joining the next within the grace (the next Meet's green room takes the
microphone within seconds) never produced an edge, so on 2026-09-25 a Devin
ambassador call and a separate call with Ashwin became one conversation.

The detector now also probes which calls are on (Meet code from browser
window titles, native call apps holding the mic). When an identity not seen
earlier in the meeting stays visible for 8 s, it reports a call change and
AppState rotates meeting -> meeting, finalizing the previous call as
meeting_ended. Seen identities never count again within a meeting, so tab
switches and an old Meet window left on screen do not rotate. Without
identities (no Screen Recording permission, non-Meet web calls) behaviour
is unchanged.

fix(mcp): accept 2026 notifications without clientCapabilities; document /v1/mcp LB route (#18951) ## Summary - 2026-07-28 `clientCapabilities` validation now applies to JSON-RPC requests only. Notifications (no `id`, including `id: null`) and `initialize` are exempt, so a 2026-declared notification without `_meta` returns HTTP 202 again. - Requests that declare `2026-07-28` without an object `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]` still return HTTP 400 / JSON-RPC `-32602`. - Documents that every environment's URL map must route both `/v1/mcp` and `/v1/mcp/*` to backend-integration. GCP `/*` does not match the bare path. The URL map itself is not changed in this PR. ## Evidence One native 2026 Go client does `server/discover` (200) then `tools/list` (200), then sends a JSON-RPC notification (no `id`) with `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28` and no `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]`. The server answers HTTP 400 with `-32602` "clientCapabilities must be an object" and `id: null`. The 283-byte response is that body plus headers. About 2 of those notification 400s per hour have been arriving since the 2026-07-28 enforcement shipped in #18745. Before the overhaul these notifications got 202. Production URL map `custom-domains-49a4` (project `based-hardware`), path matcher `api-omi-me`, routes `['/v2/integrations/*', '/v1/mcp/*']` to `prod-omi-backend-integration`. `/v1/mcp/*` does not match bare `/v1/mcp`, so the canonical MCP endpoint falls through to the default `backend` service. That service runs the same image, so the protocol works, but it has no `POSTHOG_EVENTS_API_KEY` (no MCP analytics) and it puts MCP load on the main API. Zero canonical POSTs have reached backend-integration. `/.well-known/*`, `/authorize`, and `/token` stay on `backend`. The coordinator is applying the path-rule change outside this repo. ## Tests Each file via `BACKEND_UNIT_TEST_FILE_LIST` and `backend/test.sh` (Python 3.11.15): - `backend/tests/unit/test_mcp_streamable_http.py` — 250 passed - `backend/tests/unit/test_mcp_request_observability.py` — 55 passed - `backend/tests/unit/test_mcp_batch_tools.py` — 75 passed - `backend/tests/unit/test_mcp_data_endpoints.py` — 98 passed New cases: 2026 header plus `notifications/initialized` and `notifications/cancelled` without `_meta` return 202 on `/v1/mcp` and `/v1/mcp/sse`; `tools/list` with an id and the same header still returns 400 `-32602`. The classified `notifications/initialized` log records HTTP 202 and `is_handshake`. ## Product invariants affected - INV-INT-1: no change to integration auth or data scope; only protocol-version validation of notifications. feat(speakers): resolve one speaker id per voice across a conversation

Capture restarts speaker numbering on every reconnect, provider failover and
uploaded sync chunk, and the allocator gives each piece fresh ids, so one
pendant dinner carried 1874 speaker ids for about six voices and the mobile
header read "You + 1720 others". The same fragmentation left speaker tagging,
manual assignment and owner attribution working on seven-second shards.

before it summarizes: per-segment wespeaker embeddings (cached, encrypted, next
to the audio), average-linkage clustering calibrated on real pendant audio,
fragment absorption, pooled voiceprint matching, and receipt constraints so a
labeled speaker keeps its id. The conversation carries speaker_resolution, and
the app counts ids as people only when the server says they are countable,
otherwise "You + others".

Live scopes stay on capture's ids until the capture-position clock lands,
because live started_at can drift minutes from the stored chunks.

fix(sync): release backfill inflight slot on terminal status poll after stale self-heal (#18906)

When a backfill sync job goes stale in 'processing' (or unstarted 'queued'
cloud_tasks dispatch), get_sync_job(job_id) self-heals the job to 'failed'
on read and records the pending dead-letter entry. Because job['status'] is
already 'failed' when get_sync_job returns to get_sync_job_status, the
subsequent is_sync_job_stale(job) branch in get_sync_job_status evaluates
to False and never reaches release_backfill_slot(uid, job_id).

Once get_sync_job_status verifies the durable dead-letter record for a
terminal ('failed' or 'partial_failure') backfill job, release the per-UID
backfill slot via release_backfill_slot(uid, job_id) (which uses an atomic
Lua compare-and-delete keyed to job_id) so client retries are not blocked
for 48h by HTTP 429 backfill_paced.

feat(mcp): modernize hosted MCP to spec 2026-07-28 with canonical /v1/mcp (#18745)

# feat(mcp): modernize hosted MCP to spec 2026-07-28 with canonical
/v1/mcp

## Summary

- Make `https://api.omi.me/v1/mcp` the single advertised Streamable HTTP
endpoint across hosted metadata, Flutter, macOS, Windows/Linux, the web
app, examples, and public documentation. Keep `/v1/mcp/sse` a permanent,
equivalent alias for released clients.
- Support the stateless MCP 2026-07-28 `server/discover` and per-request
metadata/headers while retaining handshake-era protocols (2024-11-05
through 2025-11-25), existing `/sse`-audience tokens, and legacy
clients. Share hosted tools and REST handlers; add bounded batch-shaped
tools, cursors, structured outputs and model-visible `isError` results.
- Harden OAuth with CIMD, PKCE, `iss` metadata, bounded SSRF-safe
metadata fetching, separate capture-only PostHog credentials, and
Firestore-authoritative token validation when Redis is unavailable.
Deprecate but do not publish the `mcp-server-omi` stdio package
(`0.2.0`).

## Rulings and compatibility

| Released client or contract | Previous behavior | This branch /
migration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MCP clients using `/v1/mcp/sse` | Hosted Streamable HTTP, legacy
handshake and optional `/sse` OAuth audience | Permanent path alias; old
protocol revisions and tokens bound to `/sse` remain accepted on both
paths. New configs advertise `/v1/mcp`; GET still does not hold an idle
SSE stream. |
| MCP 2026-07-28 clients | No stateless discovery | `server/discover`,
version/capabilities in `_meta`, required request headers, deterministic
tool list with private cache metadata and `resultType: complete`;
explicit 2026 requests lacking a `clientCapabilities` object now return
HTTP 400 / JSON-RPC `-32602`. Older handshake clients still work.
JSON-RPC arrays remain supported only for negotiated versions through
2025-03-26, with per-message admission charges; array POSTs always
return an array when they have a response. |
| Hosted tool callers | Single-id fan-out, text-only success, JSON-RPC
execution errors | Add `get_conversations_by_ids`, `create_memories`,
`group_by`/cursor for screen activity and list cursors. Preserve text
content while adding `structuredContent`; execution failures return
`isError`, protocol failures remain JSON-RPC errors. Hosted timestamps
now serialize as ISO-8601 in structured/text results; REST wire formats
remain unchanged. macOS Context for Claude labels truncated transcripts
as partial and does not cache them. |
| `/v1/mcp/*` REST consumers | Top-level list arrays and existing key
auth | Keep arrays and routes; additive `X-Next-Cursor` and bounded
detail responses. `action-items?updated_since=` has a real `(updated_at
ASC, id ASC)` keyset feed; re-read from watermark minus 60 seconds and
dedupe by id. Hard deletes cannot appear in this feed. |
| REST conversations/memories incremental sync | No trustworthy
revision-ordered feed | A supplied valid `updated_since` returns **400
`incremental_sync_unsupported`**, with a supported pagination
alternative and **no Retry-After**. For conversations use the
`(created_at DESC, id)` cursor; this is a permanent capability gap, not
a retryable outage. |
| OAuth connectors | Omitted scope defaulted to `memories.read`; only
registered clients | Omitted scope grants all available **read** scopes,
never write; registered Claude/ChatGPT clients stay valid. HTTPS Client
ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) enable third-party PKCE clients; DCR
remains unsupported. `iss` is sent and advertised. |
| Desktop and app setup | Several clients advertised `/sse`; Flutter/web
suggested the local Docker bridge or an invalid Claude OAuth secret |
Claude Code uses remote HTTP config in `~/.claude.json` with a Bearer
key; Claude Desktop uses Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector
with the URL and OAuth (advanced client ID `omi-claude-prod`, blank
secret). Windows Codex/Hermes write native HTTP configs with private
file permissions. Existing local `/sse` entries are detected as needing
an update, never mistaken for a canonical connection. |
| `mcp-server-omi` stdio package | Published 0.1.9 local 8-tool REST
bridge | Code still builds and works; 0.2.0 in-tree version adds an
stderr-only startup deprecation warning and a hosted migration guide.
**Do not publish** as part of this PR. |

### Security, data authority, and rollout decisions

- CIMD URL-form client IDs reject query/fragment variants and unsafe DNS
answers (including NAT64, 6to4, and embedded private IPv4); every
resolved address must be safe, TLS pins the validated address, enforces
TLS 1.2+, and tries IPv4 first. One monotonic 3-second deadline covers
DNS, connection, and bounded incremental reads. Separate bounded
fetch/DNS pools, per-normalized-client-host admission plus a global
ceiling, and a short failure cache protect unauthenticated `/authorize`
and `/token`. A test-only loopback hook exercises real slow-drip and
stalled-TLS peers; production still denies loopback. OAuth errors now
use approved descriptions rather than exception text, and
account-deletion auth-fence error logs omit raw UIDs.
- Redis is a **cache**, not OAuth authority. `ENCRYPTION_SECRET`
supplies an HKDF-`mcp-cache-v1` signing key for typed (`at`/`cimd`)
Redis envelopes; missing secret fails token validation closed. When
Redis is unavailable, valid tokens are checked against authoritative
Firestore without cache fill or `last_used_at` writes; marker-first
**revocation remains fail-closed**. There is a narrow in-flight revoke

## Summary
- Normalize meeting identity before note generation: deduplicate the
account owner across names and emails, distinguish human participants
from AI agents, resolve known people, and replace screen-window titles
with useful call labels.
- Keep mixed desktop remote audio unattributed unless a strict one-human
binding guard proves a speaker. Share the factual roster with notes,
memory extraction, and app prompts, but append prior conversations,
people facts, goals, matched memories, and optional screen text only to
the notes-specific background suffix.
- Produce scannable main sections and one closing Side notes section;
add optional participant, meeting-type, and private insight fields.
Public shared conversations receive named participants without emails
and meeting type, never private insights.
- `MEETING_NOTES_RICH_CONTEXT_ENABLED` and
`MEETING_NOTES_SCREEN_TEXT_CONTEXT_ENABLED` default off; both are true
only in dev and false in prod across backend-listen, pusher, backend,
and backend-sync. Flag-off prompts, serialized notes, and old-document
decoding retain their previous shape.

## Design and safety
- Best-effort bounded read-only context queries: at most 60 prior
conversations and meetings in a 180-day window, three matching prior
notes, five goals and memories, 100 people, and 80 screen rows. Each
source fails independently without blocking conversation finalization.
- Prior meeting links and goals are restricted to private insights.
Background text is never passed to the shared memory-extraction prefix,
and screen text is only spelling/identification evidence rather than a
new claim about what speakers said.
- The runtime SDK and fallback structures, generated OpenAPI app-client
contract, and generated Dart conversation wire model retain additive
optional decoding. No database index, dependency, workflow, or
production traffic change is required.

## Product invariants affected
- INV-MEM-4: Memory authority is unchanged. Only factual roster metadata
enters the memory extractor's shared prefix; historical facts enter
notes-only volatile instructions, so old background facts cannot be
promoted as new conversation memories.
- INV-TASK-2: The existing conservative task filter and desktop
Suggested Candidate policy remain intact. The new note prompt asks for
action-item owner names only when transcript evidence supports them.

## Coordinator evaluation (offline replay, real meetings)

I replayed 9 of David's real desktop meetings through the notes code on
this branch, using the production model `gpt-6-luna` at low reasoning
effort. The baseline was frozen `origin/main`.

Each note was judged by `gpt-6-sol` against a checklist built beforehand
from the transcript alone. The judge compared notes pairwise with the
order randomized, and saw the same screen context for both. Transcripts
and outputs stay private and are not in this repo.

| | baseline | this PR (roster + background + screen text) |
|---|---|---|
| judge preference | 2/9 | **7/9** |

| action-item owners OK | 2/9 | **6/9** |
| unsupported claims | 9 | 14 |
| mean latency | 19.4 s | 29.2 s |
| mean cost / note | $0.0036 | $0.0043 |

**The motivating example.** A 3-person Google Meet with an AI intro
agent: the stored note, and the baseline, say "the candidate"
throughout. This PR produces the title "Intro with Sarath Donepudi:
founding engineer". The name comes from the digest of the LinkedIn
profile the owner opened from the invite during the call, and Boardy is
recognised as an AI agent. The tangents the attendee asked for (Aside,
Dia, Atlas) now appear under Side notes.

- Persona-named agents ("Boardy Boardman", "O. Omi Agent") were
classified as humans. Detection now matches the first token or a phrase
on word boundaries.
- Prompt-rewrite `assert`s are replaced with logged fallbacks, and the
anchors are pinned by a test.
- New `screen_text_digest.py` renders distinct window titles first, then
OCR with chrome that repeats across frames removed. OCR from messaging

- Names found in screen context can corroborate participants. The owner
is kept out of titles. A name is never derived from an email address.
Owners with no known name get a role label.
- Rules added for pronouns, organization, accepted requests becoming
action items, and specific-only insights.

**Known limitations:**
- Unsupported claims rose from 9 to 14. Most are speaker attribution
inside the single remote desktop audio channel, which the baseline also
gets wrong. Only diarizing the remote channel fixes this.
- Gendered pronouns are reduced but still present.
- Insights are rare. With David's data the only matches were goals and
one prior meeting.

fix(composer): prefer text for rich Excel clipboard pastes (#21031)

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

When Excel copies cells on Windows, the clipboard can contain plain
text, an HTML table, and an image representation. The composer preferred
any supported clipboard image, so copied tables could reach text-only
models as screenshots.

After this PR:

When non-empty plain text and HTML representations accompany a supported
image, the composer treats the clipboard as rich text and preserves the
existing textual path:

- short rich clipboard text is inserted as text;
- long rich clipboard text follows the existing pasted-text-file path;
- screenshot-only clipboard pastes remain image-first;
- image-plus-text pastes without an HTML representation remain
image-first.

Fixes #6119

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Excel's clipboard payload is a rich document representation, not a
screenshot intent. Preferring the image representation makes copied
tables harder for text-only models to read and forces users to route the
data through a text editor first.

The discriminator is deliberately narrow: both non-empty `text/plain`
(or the existing `text` fallback) and `text/html` must be present. This
distinguishes document-style clipboard content from Windows screenshot
clipboards that can also expose a text flavor.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- preserve screenshot-only behavior instead of globally preferring text
whenever any image is present;
- preserve the existing long-text file path instead of adding a new
attachment type;
- avoid HTML-to-Markdown conversion, dual attachments, wildcard file
semantics, or a broader paste refactor.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Prefer text whenever any `text/plain` flavor exists. Rejected because
screenshot clipboards may expose text alongside image bytes, and this
would regress screenshot handling.
- Parse HTML into Markdown. Rejected because it expands the behavior and
format contract beyond the reported regression.
- Attach both image and text. Rejected because it duplicates content and
leaves attachment selection ambiguous.

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

The two affected paste entry points are covered because short text stays
in `ComposerSurfaceRuntime`, while long text is delegated to
`handlePaste`.

Verification:

- `pnpm exec vitest run --project renderer
src/renderer/components/composer/__tests__/ComposerSurface.test.tsx
src/renderer/components/composer/paste/__tests__/pasteHandling.test.ts`
— 2 files / 179 tests passed;
- targeted Oxlint — 0 warnings / 0 errors;
- targeted ESLint — passed;
- targeted Oxfmt check — passed;
- `git diff --check` — passed;
- commit is SSH signed and includes a DCO `Signed-off-by` trailer.

Native Windows Excel clipboard integration E2E was verified on
2026-09-25 07:42:49 (Beijing time). Microsoft Excel 15 copied short and
long worksheet ranges onto the real Windows clipboard; both exposed
`text/plain`, Excel `text/html`, `text/rtf`, and `Files/image.png`.
Electron 44.2.0 / Chromium then dispatched real paste events into this
PR's production `handlePaste`:

- short range: text was inserted normally, with no temporary file or
image attachment;
- long range (80 × 4 cells): 3,751 text characters were written to
`pasted_text.txt` with `composerFileKind: pasted_text`, and the Excel
PNG was not attached.

The probe is local Windows-only tooling and is not committed. A full
packaged Cherry Studio UI run was not completed because the local `pnpm
dev` launch stopped before startup while rebuilding `better-sqlite3`
(Visual Studio C++ tooling was unavailable); repository CI remains the
canonical full-suite signal. The repository-wide Windows suite was also
attempted, but unrelated main-process tests currently fail on POSIX path
expectations, Windows symlink privileges, and existing mock/export gaps;
the changed-scope renderer suites above are green.

This change is intentionally independent of the wildcard/file-extension
behavior discussed in #20357: it does not add `*` support or change
path-backed file acceptance.

### Checklist

- [x] Branch: This PR targets `main`
- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future
contributors
- [x] Code: The implementation is kept scoped to the reported
rich-clipboard regression
- [ ] Refactor: No unrelated cleanup is included
- [x] Upgrade: No persisted data, defaults, or upgrade flow changes
- [ ] Documentation: Not required for this narrow behavior fix
- [x] Self-review: The diff, tests, lint, formatting, signature, and DCO
trailer were reviewed

### Release note

```release-note
[Composer] Copied Excel cells now paste as text when the clipboard provides rich text alongside an image, while screenshot-only pastes remain image-first.
```

fix(openclaw): report schema probe timeouts instead of binary incompatibility (#21036)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

- Every OpenClaw preflight command shared one hardcoded 10 s budget
(`OPENCLAW_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`), including the runtime config-schema
probe (`openclaw config schema`).
- A probe that exceeded that budget was rejected as a generic preflight
failure, and `assertSchemaCapability()` turned *every* failure — a
timeout included — into `kind: 'binary_incompatible'` with the message
"The OpenClaw binary used by Cherry Studio is incompatible with the
generated configuration. Upgrade OpenClaw." Because the launch path is
`syncConfig()` → `syncProviderConfig()` → `assertSchemaCapability()`, a
slow probe aborted gateway startup and told the user to upgrade OpenClaw
even though neither the config nor the binary was at fault. #21035
measured a consistent ~12.5 s for this probe on a slow Windows disk, so
the launch failed every time.

After this PR:

- The schema probe has its own 30 s budget
(`OPENCLAW_SCHEMA_TIMEOUT_MS`); all other preflight commands keep the 10
s budget.
- A probe timeout is reported as `kind: 'preflight_timeout'` and is
re-thrown unchanged by `assertSchemaCapability()`, with its own message:
"OpenClaw did not return its configuration schema within {{seconds}}
seconds. Cherry Studio stopped waiting. OpenClaw may start slowly on a
slow disk or under high load. Try again." The "incompatible / upgrade
OpenClaw" wording no longer appears for a timeout.
- Genuine incompatibility detection is untouched: an unknown `config
schema` command, a non-zero exit, invalid JSON, a non-object payload and
oversized output still classify as `binary_incompatible`, and `config
validate` keeps both its 10 s budget and its existing failure
classification.

Fixes #21035

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Only the schema probe got the wider budget. `config validate` and the
other preflight commands still time out at 10 s, so the same slow
machine can still abort a launch at that later stage — but it now
surfaces the pre-existing, non-misleading `preflight_failed` message
("Cherry Studio could not validate the OpenClaw configuration.") instead
of an upgrade hint. Raising every preflight budget would change startup
latency on genuinely broken installations, which is a product decision
outside this bug.
- No retry and no user-facing setting were added. The report shows a
consistent ~12.5 s probe; a single 30 s budget covers it without adding
a second wait or a new preference.
- The timeout budget and failure kind are per-call options on
`runOpenClawCommand()` whose defaults preserve the previous behaviour,
so no other caller changes.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Retrying the probe once before failing — rejected as speculative for
the reported shape and larger than the fix needs.
- Exposing the timeout as a setting — out of scope (product decision).

Links to places where the discussion took place:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/21035

### Breaking changes

None.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- The new failure kind `preflight_timeout` stays inside
`OpenClawService`: `OpenClawPreflightError.kind` has no consumer outside
this module and its tests.
- Not reproduced end to end: the slow-disk Windows launch cannot be
reproduced here. Making a ~12.5 s probe succeed by construction follows
from the 10 s → 30 s budget, but "the reporter's launch now succeeds" is
an inference, not a verified result.
- Tests added to the existing `OpenClaw config preflight boundaries`
group: a hung probe times out as `preflight_timeout` with the new
message, is not classified as `binary_incompatible`, and the child
process is `SIGKILL`ed; the probe is still waiting at 12.5 s and only
times out at 30 s (the case the report hits); the user-visible
`syncProviderConfig()` result carries the timeout message and contains
neither "incompatible" nor "Upgrade OpenClaw". The existing "unknown
schema command → `binary_incompatible`" case still passes.

### Checklist

- [x] Branch: This PR targets `main`
- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future
contributors
- [x] Code: [Write code that humans can
understand](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Martin_Fowler#code-for-humans)
and [Keep it simple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KISS_principle)
- [x] Refactor: You have [left the code cleaner than you found it (Boy
Scout
Rule)](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/97-things-every/9780596809515/ch08.html)
- [x] Upgrade: Impact of this change on upgrade flows was considered and
addressed if required
- [x] Documentation: A [user-guide update](https://docs.cherry-ai.com)
was considered and is present (link) or not required. Check this only
when the PR introduces or changes a user-facing feature or behavior.
- [x] Self-review: I have reviewed my own code (e.g., via
[`/gh-pr-review`](/.claude/skills/gh-pr-review/SKILL.md), `gh pr diff`,
or GitHub UI) before requesting review from others

### Release note

```release-note
[OpenClaw] Fixed launches that failed with "The OpenClaw binary used by Cherry Studio is incompatible with the generated configuration. Upgrade OpenClaw." when the config-schema probe was merely slow: the probe now has a 30-second budget and a timeout is reported as a timeout instead of a binary incompatibility.
```

chore(deps): upgrade vitest to v5 (#21032)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->
<!--  Thanks for sending a pull request!  Here are some tips for you:
1. Consider creating this PR as draft:
https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

> ### Branch strategy
>
> - Active development targets `main`.

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The test toolchain is on Vitest 4 (`^4.1.10`).

After this PR:

- `vitest` and `@vitest/*` are on `^5.0.1` in the root and all 7
workspace packages.
- The root pins `@opentelemetry/api` to `1.9.1`, so `packages/ui`
resolves the same `vitest` copy as the root.
- Both benchmarks use the new `bench` test-context fixture, and the
`bench:*` scripts target the new `<name> (bench)` projects.
- Two tests that broke under Vitest 5 are fixed (`sentryLog.test.ts`,
`AppShellTabBar.test.tsx`).
- `CLAUDE.md` now says Vitest 5.

Fixes #21024

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

Vitest 5.0 shipped on 2026-09-03. Every suite and `pnpm typecheck` were
run on the upgraded tree, and each breakage was fixed directly:

- **`clearMocks` now defaults to `true`.** We adopt the new default. The
only test that relied on mock-call history across tests was
`sentryLog.test.ts`, which looked up a handler that `LoggerService`
registers at import time. It now captures the handler once at module
scope.
- **Non-writable global stubs.** `AppShellTabBar.test.tsx` replaced
`requestAnimationFrame` / `cancelAnimationFrame` with non-writable
properties. Under v5, `vi.useRealTimers()` throws on them, and the
leftover fake timers broke 3 later tests. The descriptors are now
writable.
- **Benchmark API rewrite.** `bench` is no longer exported from
`vitest`. Benchmarks are now `test('…', async ({ bench }) =>
bench.compare(...))`. The tinybench `setup` / `teardown` options become
per-bench `beforeAll` / `afterAll`, and `iterations` /
`warmupIterations` move to the `bench.compare` run options. Benchmarks
also run in a separate `<name> (bench)` project, so the old `--project
renderer` filter fails with `No projects matched the filter`.
- **jest-dom matcher types lost in `packages/ui`** (543 `tsc` errors
across 42 files). Vitest declares `@opentelemetry/api` as an optional
peer. The lockfile had resolved it to 1.9.0 for several workspace
packages (a stale resolution already present with v4), which installs a
separate `vitest` copy for `packages/ui`.
`@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest` augments only the root copy. Pinning
the root dependency to `1.9.1` re-resolves the peer, and its lockfile
diff is limited to the `vitest` / `@vitest/mocker` peer variants.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- `@opentelemetry/api` is pinned exactly, so future bumps are manual.
The root already pins `vite`, `jsdom` and `typescript` exactly.
- jest-dom's `Assertion<T>` augmentation still conflicts with Vitest 5's
`Assertion<R, T>` (testing-library/jest-dom#738). With our TypeScript
7.0.2 and `skipLibCheck: true`, that is only a suppressed TS2428 inside
`node_modules`, and the matchers still type-check. We can upgrade
jest-dom once testing-library/jest-dom#742 is released.

The following alternatives were considered:

- `pnpm update -r @opentelemetry/api` or `pnpm update -r vitest`: both
leave the stale peer resolution in place.
- `pnpm dedupe`: rewrites many unrelated packages.
- A pnpm `overrides` entry for `@opentelemetry/api`: also unifies the
copies, but any `overrides` edit re-resolves the lockfile and moves root
`react` to 19.2.7 while `react-dom` stays at 19.2.3. `react-dom` then
throws `Incompatible React versions` on load.
- A local jest-dom type shim, or replacing jest-dom: unnecessary once
the `vitest` copies are unified.
- Pinning `clearMocks: false`: rejected. About 700 test files already
call `vi.clearAllMocks()` by hand.

Links to places where the discussion took place: #21024

### Breaking changes

None. Only dev dependencies, tests, benchmarks and a docs line change.
`@opentelemetry/api` already resolved to 1.9.1 at runtime.

### Special notes for your reviewer

- The commits are split: two test fixes, both also valid on Vitest 4,
followed by the upgrade itself.
- Verified locally on Node 24.21.0: every Vitest project, the standalone
package suites (`dsh-bridge`, `remote-protocol`, `remote-transport`,
`ai-sdk-provider`), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm test:lint`, `pnpm
bench:renderer`, and `pnpm test:coverage` (the report covers 5088 source
files, with no test files, type declarations, `dist` output or
`node_modules` among them).
- One `probes.e2e.test.ts` case fails locally whenever the DNS resolver
answers `.invalid` names (for example a fake-IP proxy). It is unrelated
to this change.
- Inline projects in `vitest.config.ts` now inherit the root config by
default, so the explicit `extends: true` flags are redundant. They were
left in place to keep this diff focused.

### Checklist

This checklist is not enforcing, but it's a reminder of items that could
be relevant to every PR.
Approvers are expected to review this list.

- [x] PR: The PR description is expressive enough and will help future
contributors
- [x] Code: [Write code that humans can
understand](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Martin_Fowler#code-for-humans)
and [Keep it simple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KISS_principle)
- [ ] Refactor: You have [left the code cleaner than you found it (Boy
Scout
Rule)](https://learning.oreilly.com/library/view/97-things-every/9780596809515/ch08.html)
- [x] Upgrade: Impact of this change on upgrade flows was considered and
addressed if required

was considered and is present (link) or not required. Check this only
when the PR introduces or changes a user-facing feature or behavior.

[`/gh-pr-review`](/.claude/skills/gh-pr-review/SKILL.md), `gh pr diff`,
or GitHub UI) before requesting review from others
