fix(desktop): Windows sidecar/backend startup failures (#14401)

* fix(hub): start the desktop backend reliably on Windows proxy machines

Two Windows-specific defects kept the desktop sidecar from ever seeing the
Hub daemon it had just spawned (#14265, #14292):

- Bun's fetch honors HTTP(S)_PROXY with no localhost bypass, so on machines
  whose system proxy exports those variables (Clash, v2ray, corporate
  setups) every loopback discovery probe was sent to the proxy and failed.
  The healthy daemon looked unreachable, the sidecar died with "No
  compatible hub runtime is available" before publishing its endpoint, and
  every respawned daemon exited with "Hub instance lock is held by a live
  Hub". New ensureLoopbackProxyBypass() appends the loopback spellings to
  NO_PROXY/no_proxy whenever a proxy variable is set; it runs at every
  entrypoint (desktop sidecar, hub daemon, CLI, menubar) and lazily inside
  probeHubServer/requestHubDrain/requestHubShutdown so every embedder of the
  hub client is covered. Reproduced end-to-end on Linux: the compiled
  sidecar with a dead HTTP_PROXY fails exactly like the Windows reports
  before this change and publishes its endpoint after it.

- Compiled-Bun embedded entry detection only knew the POSIX /$bunfs/ mount,
  not the Windows B:\~BUN\ drive, so Windows daemons were spawned with a
  dead B:\~BUN\root\entry.js argument (visible verbatim in #14292) instead
  of the --cline-hub-daemon marker, hiding them from cline doctor's
  marker-based process scan. New isBunEmbeddedModulePath() handles both
  spellings and replaces the three divergent checks (hub daemon spawn, CLI
  internal launch, menubar entry detection).

The compiled-backend startup test now also boots the sidecar behind a dead
HTTP(S) proxy so the regression stays locked in CI.

* fix(desktop): clamp the main window to the monitor work area

The window opens at a fixed 1500x980 logical pixels. On small or DPI-scaled
displays — a 1920x1080 laptop at 150% scaling has only a 1280x720 logical
desktop — it came up larger than the screen, leaving the bottom and side of
the UI (the settings and account controls among them) off-screen and
unreachable (#14270). Shrink an oversized window to the monitor's work area
(which already excludes the taskbar) minus the OS chrome, and re-center it;
windows that fit are left untouched, and a nonsense work area reading never
collapses the window.

* fix(shared): merge both NO_PROXY casings instead of copying one over the other

ensureLoopbackProxyBypass picked whichever of NO_PROXY/no_proxy was set
first and wrote that value (plus the loopback hosts) to both casings. On
POSIX the two variables can be populated independently — a launcher setting
one and a shell profile the other — and different tools read different
casings, so exemptions present only in the other casing were silently
dropped and previously exempt traffic could start routing through the
proxy. Merge the union of both casings (first spelling wins on duplicate
entries, compared case-insensitively) so entries are only ever added, and
honor a wildcard opt-out in either casing.

Review finding from cline/cline#14401.

* test(core): clear proxy env before setting it in the loopback-exemption test

On Windows process.env is case-insensitive, so the previous order — assign
HTTP_PROXY, then delete http_proxy — deleted the variable that was just
set. ensureLoopbackProxyBypass then correctly saw no proxy and wrote
nothing, and the assertion received '' on the Windows CI leg (Ubuntu
passed because POSIX treats the casings as separate keys). Delete all four
variables first, then set HTTP_PROXY, which behaves identically on both
semantics. Test-setup fix only; verified against a simulated
case-insensitive env that the old order reproduces the CI failure and the
new order passes.

* ci: retrigger checks after unrelated Windows python-hook flake

The previous run's sole failure (hook-file-hooks.test.ts > executes python
hook files, 15s spawn timeout on the windows-latest runner) is untouched by
this branch and passed on the prior commit of this same branch; the
loopback-exemption test fixed in 01009dd91 now passes on Windows.

* chore: trim duplicated call-site comments in the loopback proxy bypass

Keep the explanation once, on ensureLoopbackProxyBypass, and reduce each
call site to a one-liner.

* fix(shared): exempt loopback in the non-wildcard casing when only one NO_PROXY casing is *

A wildcard in one casing left the other casing untouched, so a tool that
reads only the lowercase variable could still route 127.0.0.1 through the
proxy. Leave the wildcard casing alone and merge loopback into the other.

commits.message:
perf(claude): skip stale files for date-bounded loads and bound statusline blocks (#1794)

* perf(claude): skip usage files last written before --since

Session JSONL files are append-only, so a file whose mtime predates the
--since window cannot hold an entry inside it. Both Claude loaders now
drop such files before reading, with a 24-hour margin for timezone
bounds and late flushes. Unbounded reports, future windows, and files
with unreadable metadata keep every file.

Refs #1791

* perf(statusline): bound the active block load

The active block query loaded the whole Claude history on every cold
render. It now sets --since to one day behind the session window so the
Claude adapter only reads recently written files.

Refs #1790

* test(claude): cover bounded daily totals with pruned files

Run claude daily through the CLI with stale, in-margin and fresh session
files so the --json and table outputs guard that mtime pruning keeps
late-flushed entries and leaves the bounded totals unchanged.

* fix(claude): keep --since pruning from changing report output

Codex review found four ways mtime pruning changed bounded reports:

- A sidechain replay of a parent message in a stale file was counted twice.
  Files are now kept or skipped per session (the transcript together with
  its subagent transcripts), so replays still meet their parents.
- Unified `session --since` totals whole sessions, and blocks anchor on
  earlier entries, so both read the full history again through
  `load_entries`. Reports that drop entries dated before `--since` opt into
  pruning via the new `load_entries_since`.
- The statusline active block now widens its window until it reaches back
  past an idle gap longer than a session, which is where block boundaries
  stop depending on older history, and otherwise reads the full history.
- Unified reports lost `Detected: Claude` when every file predated the
  window; skipped files are now checked for usage when nothing else is found.

Regression tests run each case twice, with stale and freshly touched
mtimes, and require identical output.

* fix(claude): group pruned sessions across roots and flat agent files

Key sessions relative to `projects/` so a copy in another config root is
kept with the live original, and key legacy flat `agent-*.jsonl`
transcripts on the `sessionId` inside them so sidechain replays still meet
their parents.

The statusline active block also reads the full history when entries are
future-dated, since a pause before such an entry could otherwise anchor
blocks after the current one.

* fix(claude): group pruned files by the session IDs they record

Workflow subagent transcripts can live under one session directory and
record another session's ID, so path-based groups let a stale parent be
dropped while its in-window replay survived. Files now join a union-find
over their path-derived session and the first `sessionId` they record,
which is the identity the loaders deduplicate on. This also covers
legacy flat `agent-*.jsonl` files and copies in another config root, and
the probe parses JSON lines so whitespace or long leading lines no longer
hide the ID.

perf(pricing): index normalized spellings for exact lookups (#1796)

perf(pricing): index normalised spellings for exact lookups

`find_exact_normalized` scanned every pricing entry and allocated a
normalised copy of each key on every call. Antigravity and Hermes price
each usage event through `find_exact_with_fallback`, once per fallback
candidate, so large histories spent most of a report in that scan and
the Antigravity stage looked hung.

Build a lazy map from normalised spelling to the single entry key that
carries it, marking spellings shared by several keys as ambiguous so
they still resolve to nothing. The map stores keys rather than rates, so
in-place rate patches stay visible; it is dropped with the find cache,
which the built-in entry helpers now also clear so a lookup made before
a later insert cannot serve a stale answer.

40,000 normalised lookups against the embedded table: 49.9s -> 21.6ms.

Co-authored-by: LivioGama <6930498+LivioGama@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(pr-gate): enable OIDC for the PR verdict job (#1795)

The Pullfrog judge in the PR gate needs a short-lived OIDC assertion to
reach the configured model proxy. With id-token set to none it fell back
to a model that requires META_MODEL_API_KEY, failed, and every outside
contributor PR was left open instead of receiving a verdict.

Mirror the issue gate fix from #1655. The job still checks out only the
base branch, keeps read-only GitHub API permissions, and runs Pullfrog
with shell and push disabled.

commits.message: docs(durable): clarify scratch examples
feat(durable): add typed IDs and explicit ownership

fix(ai): price OpenAI Fast mode service tier like priority

GPT-6 models return service_tier "fast" for Fast mode requests (the new
name for priority processing), which fell through to the 1x default.

closes #10034

fix(ai): upgrade openai SDK to 7.19.0 (#10044)

* fix(ai): upgrade openai SDK to 7.19.0

Adds the "fast" service tier to the SDK types, needed to price
GPT-6 Fast mode requests correctly. Drops the local
prompt_cache_options type, which the SDK now defines.

* fix(coding-agent): check Cloudflare compat request via fetch instead of SDK mock

pi-ai now resolves its own nested openai 7.x while evals keeps 6.x at the
root, so vi.mock("openai") in coding-agent no longer reached pi-ai's client.
Capture the outgoing request with a fake fetch and assert the URL and headers.

* fix(ai): drop any casts for stream_options and max_tokens in openai-completions

stream_options is typed by the SDK, so assign it directly. max_tokens is
deprecated by OpenAI but still needed for OpenAI-compatible providers
that reject max_completion_tokens; use a narrow cast instead of any to
avoid the deprecation warning.

fix(coding-agent): save new session file at the first user message

A new session was only written to disk once the first assistant message
existed. If pi exited during the first turn (Ctrl+C twice while streaming,
or the process was killed), the user's prompt was lost and the session
never appeared in /resume.

The file is now created as soon as the session has a user or assistant
message. A session with only setup entries (model, thinking level) still
stays in memory, so starting pi and quitting without chatting leaves no
file. Forking uses the same rule through a shared helper, so the two paths
cannot drift apart and write the header twice (#1672).

closes #10000
feat(durable): add conversation document forks

fix(ai): ignore empty Mistral content deltas

GLM models on Mistral send empty content deltas at the start of a
response, alongside tool call fragments, and sometimes mid-thinking.
Each one opened an empty text block, and a mid-thinking one split
thinking into two blocks, which Mistral rejects on replay with
"Expected at most one leading ThinkChunk".

closes #9674

fix(ai): apply model samplingParams in direct stream()/complete() calls

Model-level samplingParams were only merged by streamSimple(). Direct
stream()/complete() calls, such as extensions using
modelRegistry.complete(), dropped them. The OpenAI-compatible adapters
now merge model defaults with request keys, and request keys take
precedence.

closes #9506
fix(coding-agent): honor truecolor in custom themes (fixes #9973) (#10039)

feat(coding-agent): report prompt disposition in RPC responses

Successful RPC prompt, steer, and follow_up responses include
data.disposition ("handled", "queued", or "started" for prompt), so clients
know whether to wait for agent_settled.

fixes #9098

fix(tui): keep cursor visible when overlays close after stop

Closing the last overlay hid the terminal cursor. If an extension closed
an overlay during session shutdown, this ran after stop() had restored
the cursor, leaving the shell with an invisible cursor.

closes #10026

feat: build with TypeScript 7 and run sources with plain node

Replace the tsgo native preview with typescript@7.0.2 and port the check scripts to the TS 7 API. Target ES2024, drop useDefineForClassFields: false and unused decorator options, and enable verbatimModuleSyntax. Replace tsx with node plus the source resolver hook, passed to --import as a file URL.

closes #9965

fix(coding-agent): hide line range for full-file read calls with null offset/limit

Strict tool schemas make models send null for omitted optional fields.
The read renderer only treated undefined as missing, so full-file reads
rendered as "path:1".

fixes #9996

fix(coding-agent): stop RpcClient skipping listeners on unsubscribe

closes #9990

fix(coding-agent): use per-ref cache folders for pinned temporary git extensions

Temporary git extensions (-e git:...@ref) were cached in a folder keyed
only by host and repo path. After changing the pinned ref, pi reused the
old checkout without refreshing it and kept loading the first downloaded
commit. Include the ref in the temporary folder hash so each ref gets
its own checkout. Unpinned sources keep their existing folder.

closes #9982

fix(flows): detect thought-only and whitespace turns as empty content

When models return turns that contain only reasoning thoughts
(parts with thought=True) or whitespace text with finish_reason=STOP
after tool execution or under streaming, BaseLlmFlow previously
treated them as complete final responses because parts was not empty.
This caused the agent loop to silently terminate without answering the
user or surfacing an error.

- Add has_meaningful_content(llm_response) helper in _finalizer.py
  to verify if an LLM response contains actionable content (tools, code,
  data, or non-thought non-whitespace text).
- Update apply_empty_response_policy in _model_call.py to stamp
  MODEL_RETURNED_NO_CONTENT when an LLM response has finish_reason=STOP
  but lacks meaningful content.
- Ensure LiteLlm.generate_content_async streaming always yields a terminal
  partial=False response on normal termination even when no content chunks
  were emitted.
- Add unit tests covering has_meaningful_content, BaseLlmFlow error events
  for thought-only and whitespace-only turns, and LiteLlm empty stream fallback.

Co-authored-by: Shangjie Chen <deanchen@google.com>

Remove trailing whitespace in the E2B and GCS integration guides. Add docs to the default precommit check targets so documentation formatting is checked locally before export.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 988455161

feat: add pagination to list_accessible_data_agents in data_agent toolset

By default, list_accessible_data_agents now fetches every page automatically, so
a single call returns all accessible data agents. Callers that want to page
manually can pass the optional page_size and page_token arguments and resume
from the nextPageToken in the response; passing an empty page_token explicitly
requests the first page rather than the automatic drain.

The automatic drain is bounded by safety limits (1000 agents, 100 pages, 90
seconds) and retries transient page failures. Truncation is always visible to
the caller. If the drain runs out of time it returns the pages it did fetch as a
successful result carrying both a nextPageToken to resume from and a
paginationWarning. If instead the API cycles its page tokens it returns a
paginationWarning with no token, because resuming would replay pages forever. A
failure before any page has been fetched is still reported as an error, so an
incomplete list is never mistaken for an empty one.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 988447545

Remove obsolete google.adk.flows.llm_flows._fencing compatibility shim now that
all callers import from google.adk.flows.llm_flows.context._fencing directly.

fix: resume a remote A2A agent when a human answers its relayed pause

RemoteA2aAgent chose whether to flatten a human's answer to text by the pause's function call name alone, so the answer to a confirmation or input request that the remote agent raised itself and relayed up was sent back as plain text, the remote agent never resumed, and under the legacy executor the approval-gated tool never ran. The answer is now flattened only when the pause was raised on the caller's side or synthesized by ADK for a non-ADK peer, so a pause relayed by the remote agent is resumed with a function response as it was before 2.7.0, and text sent alongside that answer is dropped because the remote runner rejects a message that mixes the two.

Close #6721

fix: accept a client factory written against either httpx major

A caller's httpx client factory is written against one httpx major while ADK
binds whichever one the installed MCP SDK uses, and each major stores the other
major's Timeout whole in every field instead of rejecting it, so the client
failed with a type error on its first request. Hands the factory a Timeout that

ADK keeps its own state under <owner>:<key> names, some built from a plugin's configurable name, so narrowing the bypass to the app:, user: and temp: prefixes made OAuth auth_config nodes, MultimodalToolResultsPlugin with retention='session' and SaveFilesAsArtifactsPlugin raise StateSchemaError in any workflow that declares state_schema. commits.message:
fix(python): remove resource variable printout (#3785)

Stop printing the model's resource variable count each time the
Python interpreter loads a model. The print went to stdout without
being asked for, and it cluttered the output of every script and test
that loads a model. The interpreter still counts the resource
variables and passes the count to the C++ interpreter.

BUG=see description

feat(compression): refuse to compress required constants (#3782)

Refuse to compress a tensor that a kernel must read during Prepare,
and name the operator and the input that need it. Compression
replaces a constant with the output of a DECODE operator. That output
has no values until DECODE runs in Invoke, and the kernel rejects a
non-constant input in Prepare, so the model fails to prepare.

List the inputs that the portable kernels check this way, keyed by
operator and input position, in one table that the compressor reads.

Fix output_dir flag spelling in mutable-op resolver test (#3776)

Use the two-dash form required by argparse. This preserves behavior
after replacing Abseil flags.

Change-Id: Ifa1ec7b3c9fb364360f03578a01f29e1a945698a

fix(pypi): build each wheel for its own Python (#3780)

Pass the rules_python version flag to the wheel build, so each wheel
compiles against its target Python version. The build script chose a
Python by linking it into PATH, but under bzlmod the hermetic
toolchain ignores PATH and defaults to 3.13. Every wheel since the
bzlmod migration has had a 3.13 extension module, which fails to import
on 3.10--3.12, and 3.14.

Keep a wheel's tags when the wheel test renames the file, so pip
refuses a wheel tagged for a Python other than the one under test.
The rename to py3-none-any turned that check off, and the test also
ran 3.13 for every tag, so it passed the broken wheels.

Fix two additional faults that went unseen because the test ran only
3.13. On 3.11 and 3.12, a venv made from the runfiles symlink to the
interpreter cannot find the standard library, so resolve the symlink
first. On 3.10 and 3.11, the resource lookup in the post-install check
needs a package, not a module name.

BUG=fixes #3765

feat(compression): name operators in the model editor (#3779)

In the model editor used by the compression tooling, give the operator
wrapper a property that returns the operator's kind as text. A custom
operator goes by its custom code, a builtin by the name of its
enumerator, and an unrecognized code by its number. Naming an operator
is a property of an operator, so it belongs with the wrapper that
models one, where every caller can reach it.

This prepares for errors and reports that name the operators reading
a tensor.

Re-enable Python tests and clean up legacy imports (#3781)

- Re-enable `lstm_test_data_generator_test`, `audio_preprocessor_test`, and `hello_world:evaluate_test` without TensorFlow.
- Remove legacy `tflite_runtime` import fallbacks and obsolete `nomicro_static` tags.

Post-merge publication crashed after creating v6.2.67 because GitHub

fix: keep stdin open until the CLI reports idle so follow-up turns are served (#1190) (#1279)

Fixes #1190. Builds on the background-task tracking added for #1088 /
#1103.

## The bug

`query()` with hooks, `can_use_tool` or SDK MCP servers keeps stdin open
so the CLI can ask the SDK questions. It closed stdin at the first
result that arrived with no tracked background task in flight.

A subagent that finishes just before the turn's result is already
untracked at that result. Its completion still wakes the parent for a
follow-up turn, and that turn's hook, permission and SDK MCP requests
then fail with "Stream closed". The model reports that the tool was
refused. Task bookkeeping cannot tell that result from the last one.

## The fix

The CLI already reports when no follow-up turn is owed, through
`session_state_changed` messages:
- It reports `running` while a background agent is live or its
completion is still to be handled.
- It reports `idle` only once the session is done.

The SDK asks for these messages the same way the TypeScript SDK does:
- With `CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE=1`, the CLI sends them
marked `sdk_host_only: true`.
- If the caller also set `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS`, they
come unmarked. That variable stays the caller's own opt-in to seeing
them.

Changes:
- **`SubprocessCLITransport`:** sets
`CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE=1` unless the caller's
`options.env` or the process environment already names the variable (any
case). Setting it to `0` opts out. The SDK no longer sets
`CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS`.
- **Hidden messages:** `Query` drops only the messages marked
`sdk_host_only`, for both `query()` and `ClaudeSDKClient`. Unmarked ones
(the caller opted in) reach the caller. Both kinds drive the run end the
same way.
- **`Query`, when the run ends:**
  - at the `idle` that follows a result;
  - at a result that follows `idle`;
- at a result when the CLI sent no state (an older CLI), or when nothing
needs stdin;
  - never at an `idle` that comes before any result.
- **Bounded wait:** the CLI's own background-wait ceiling only starts
once stdin is closed. So `Query` also ends the run if the CLI still
reports `running` `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` after a result
with no new turn.
- The value is read from `options.env`, then the inherited environment.
The default is 10 minutes; `0` means no limit.
- The ceiling restarts at each result, and whenever the CLI reports
`running` again between turns.
- It counts only the wait between turns. It is not armed while a
main-thread turn is under way (from its first `assistant`/`stream_event`
until its result), or while the SDK is answering a request
(`requires_action`).
- A tracked background agent still in flight (#1088) is not cut off. The
ceiling starts over once the last one settles, so the ledger's guarantee
holds as it does without state.
- **`AsyncIterable` prompts:** each prompt written reopens the run, and
so does work the CLI takes up after the run ended (`running`,
`requires_action`, a main-thread turn). The last prompt waits for its
own run, not an earlier one's. Once stdin is closed it stays closed.
- **Older CLIs:** a CLI too old to know the variable sends no state. The
SDK then closes stdin at the first result with no tracked task in
flight, which is today's behaviour; the #1088 task ledger still applies.

No public API changes. This matches the TypeScript SDK, which follows
the same contract.

### Behaviour change

A one-shot run with callbacks now stays open for as long as the CLI
reports work that can still wake the session, up to the ceiling between
turns:
- **Keeps the run open:** background agents, bounded monitors and MCP
tasks.
- **Doesn't extend the run:** background shells, persistent monitors and
long-running remote agents. The CLI excludes these from its `running`
report, so stdin still closes at `idle` as before.

The fix takes effect with a CLI that knows
`CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE`. The bundled 2.1.282 predates it,
so with that CLI runs close stdin at the first result as they do today.

This replaces two earlier approaches in this PR:
- a new `end_user_input` control request plus result folding
(`ResultMessage.turn_results`), which needed a CLI change no released
CLI has and added public API;
- turning on `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS` and hiding every
state message from the caller.

## Testing

**Unit tests:**
- `tests/test_query.py::TestStdinStaysOpenUntilIdle`: a background agent
that settled before the result keeps stdin open through the second
result, and stdin closes at `idle`. Also covers:
  - marked messages dropped, unmarked passed through;
  - no state at all (closes at the first result);
  - `idle` just before a result;
  - `idle` before any result;
  - `idle` with a tracked task still in flight;
  - a single-message `AsyncIterable` prompt;
  - a later prompt waiting for its own run;
  - a stream reopened by `running` / `requires_action` after `idle`.
- `tests/test_query.py::TestRunEndCeiling`:
  - the ceiling ends the run with no `idle` (asyncio and trio);
  - a main-thread turn stops it; subagent messages don't;
- `requires_action` stops it, including when the result arrives
mid-request;
  - it is not armed mid-turn;
- it leaves a tracked agent alone and starts over once the agent
settles;
  - `0` and huge values wait for `idle`;
  - a stream the ceiling ended reopens for a main-thread turn;
  - no ceiling is armed once stdin is closed.
- `TestRunEndCeilingFromEnv` covers parsing the variable: default, `0`,
`options.env` over the environment, and invalid values falling back to
the default.
- `tests/test_transport.py`: `CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_READS_SESSION_STATE` is
set only when neither `options.env` nor the process environment names
it, in any case. `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS` is never set.
- `tests/test_run_end_subprocess.py` (new) runs `query()` against a
stand-in CLI that speaks the new contract. It checks three things: the
follow-up turn's hook is answered on stdin; marked messages stay hidden
while opted-in ones show; the ceiling closes stdin when `idle` never
comes.
- ruff, mypy and the full unit suite (1587 passed, 6 skipped) pass.

**E2E** (`e2e-tests/test_run_end.py`, haiku):
- `test_hook_run_ends_with_one_result`: a string prompt with a hook
still gives exactly one result, and no state messages leak into the
stream.
- `test_follow_up_turn_after_a_background_subagent_is_served`: the model
starts a background subagent and ends its turn, then writes a file when
the subagent finishes. The `Write` hook must run in that follow-up turn.
It runs in two variants:
- `sdk`: the SDK asks for the messages. It skips when the CLI sends no
`sdk_host_only` messages, i.e. a CLI that predates the variable.
- `caller`: the caller sets `CLAUDE_CODE_EMIT_SESSION_STATE_EVENTS=1`
and sees the messages.

| | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| CLI 2.1.282, `caller` | pass (idle-based run end with a real CLI) |
| CLI 2.1.282, `sdk` | skipped (CLI predates the variable) |
| CLI 2.1.282 behind a shim that marks state messages the way newer CLIs
do, both variants | pass |

- **Full e2e suite, CLI 2.1.282:** 46 passed, 1 skipped (the `sdk`
variant above), 1 failed. The failure is
`test_include_partial_messages_thinking_deltas`, from the local machine
(haiku producing no thinking deltas); it fails the same way on `main`.
- **Ceiling with a real CLI** (2.1.282 behind the same shim,
`CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=5000`, a background subagent left
running): the SDK closed stdin 5.0 s after the first result.

## Related

- #1212 attempts an SDK-only mitigation by deferring the close for one
extra result after a task settles unobserved. It can hang `query()` on a
plain foreground-subagent run, and it can't tell a pending follow-up
turn from the end of the run.
- #1088 / #1103: the original report and the task-ledger mitigation,
which stays as the fallback for CLIs without state events.

fix(returns): use non-excess kurtosis and omit NaNs in deflated Sharpe ratio

The Deflated Sharpe Ratio standard error of Bailey and López de Prado,
sqrt((1 - g3 * SR + (g4 - 1) / 4 * SR^2) / (T - 1)), takes g4 as the
non-excess kurtosis (3 for Gaussian returns, which recovers the Lo (2002)
standard error sqrt((1 + SR^2 / 2) / (T - 1))). scipy.stats.kurtosis
returns the excess kurtosis by default, so the term was off by 3 / 4 * SR^2
and could turn the variance negative, yielding NaN.

Missing returns were also replaced by zero-return periods before computing
the moments and the horizon, diluting skewness and kurtosis and inflating
the horizon, while sharpe_ratio ignores them. They are now omitted from the
moments and the per-column horizon.

Tests use the reference formula directly rather than only stored values.

fix(generic): return NaN from expanding_mean/std when minp exceeds the length

expanding_mean_nb and expanding_std_nb delegate to the rolling functions
with window = len(a), so a minp larger than the number of rows raised
'minp must be <= window' in the Numba engine, while the Rust engine and
pandas' expanding(min_periods=minp) return NaN. Use window = max(len(a),
minp) so both engines agree with pandas.

fix(mcp): stop swallowing worker task cancellation (#5055)

_ServerWorker._run wrapped command execution in except BaseException, so
an external task.cancel() was recorded on the command future and the
worker went back to the queue loop while staying in the cancelling state.
is_done never flipped and anything awaiting the task, including loop
shutdown, hung

The loop now compares the worker task cancellation count before and after
each command and re-raises CancelledError only when that count grew while
the command ran, which keeps a server raising CancelledError on its own
recoverable through the future while an external cancel ends the worker.
The count is carried by the worker itself and every cancel() on the task
is counted through a shim installed at creation time, so the distinction
works on Python 3.10 too, where Task.cancelling() does not exist, and the
worker task is still created through the event loop's task factory so
applications supervising tasks through set_task_factory keep seeing it

When the external cancel lands while a command runs, the worker runs the
server cleanup in the same task before re-raising, so a partially acquired
connection from an interrupted connect is released instead of leaked. That
emergency cleanup is bounded by the manager cleanup timeout instead of the
interrupted connect command's own timeout, since connect and cleanup have
separate allowances and an unbounded cleanup could still hang loop shutdown

A failed or timed-out emergency cleanup used to be swallowed silently, so
the worker still looked cleanly stopped: the done callback discarded it,
and a later reconnect started a second connection over the transport that
was never cleaned up. The failure is now recorded on the cleanup result
future, which keeps the worker registered, keeps the failure observable
through the manager errors, and keeps reconnect from retrying the
uncleaned server

The worker loop also settles the futures of commands still queued when it
exits for any reason, so callers waiting on a queued command get
CancelledError instead of hanging forever

fix(sessions): close SQLiteSession connections owned by exited worker threads (#5090)

* fix(memory): close SQLiteSession connections owned by exited worker threads

A file-backed session registers one sqlite connection per worker thread so
close() can release connections it does not own, but nothing removed an
entry when the owning thread exited. The thread-local slot dies with the
thread, so the registry became the only reference to a connection nobody
could reach, and an application running one event loop per turn accumulated
open connections until the process ran out of file descriptors.

Record the owning thread for each tracked connection and close the ones
whose owner has exited when a new worker registers a connection.

* fix(memory): reap retired connections before allocating a new one

Move the dead-owner sweep ahead of sqlite3.connect() and
_configure_connection() so a worker releases its retired predecessors'
handles before allocating its own, and evict a connection from the
registries only after closing it so an interrupted close leaves it
tracked for later cleanup.

Cover the burst case with a regression test: three workers hold at a
barrier so they retire together, and the next allocation must find every
retired connection already closed while the stored history stays usable.
fix(sessions): match literal Unicode content in AdvancedSQLiteSession (#5143)

fix(mcp): keep the Streamable HTTP session usable after a 5xx (#5061)

With MCP Python SDK v2, the response hook that `MCPServerStreamableHttp`
installs on its HTTP client called `raise_for_status()` for every 5xx.
The hook runs inside the MCP transport task group, so a single transient
5xx on any request tore down the shared transport. Every later
`call_tool()` and `list_tools()` then failed with `MCPError: Connection
closed` until `cleanup()` and `connect()`. A 5xx on the
`notifications/initialized` notification to a legacy-protocol server did
the same while `connect()` still reported success.

The hook now skips the raise only for a post-handshake MCP transport
message, meaning a request body that is a JSON-RPC message other than
`server/discover` and `initialize`. MCP v2 fails such a message on its
own, so the session stays usable and `max_retry_attempts` retries on it.

Every other response keeps the existing HTTP error mapping. A handshake
5xx still fails `connect()` with the HTTP status, so a failed discovery
probe is not mistaken for a legacy server. OAuth auth-flow sub-requests
such as token and registration requests are not transport messages, so
their failures also stay on that path instead of reaching MCP's OAuth
exceptions, which carry the authorization server's response body.

feat(enhancement): LocalVQE AEC with safe streaming and benchmark validation (beta) (#930)

### Why is this change needed?

Adds LocalVQE acoustic echo cancellation, noise suppression and
dereverberation for 16 kHz speech, addressing the [LocalVQE request in
#49](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/issues/49#issuecomment-5719663475).
Includes the Core ML consumer, CLI, benchmark corrections and safe
streaming lifecycle. **Beta: live capture/playback integration on target
devices remains unvalidated.**

Companion conversion and evaluation PR: [mobius
#96](https://github.com/FluidInference/mobius/pull/96). Models:
[FluidInference/localvqe-coreml](https://huggingface.co/FluidInference/localvqe-coreml).

### Implementation

- `LocalVqeManager` for files/whole clips and `LocalVqeStream` for
arbitrary buffer sizes; v1.3/v1.2, fp32, 16 ms or 256 ms model chunks,
CPU default.
- Sample-aligned output, length preserved after flushing, and explicit
recurrent state.
- Per-stream FIFO serialization spans asynchronous inference:
overlapping pushes, flushes and resets cannot overwrite input/state
buffers. Independent streams remain concurrent.
- Queued cancellation leaves the active clip untouched; active
cancellation or prediction failure clears the unfinished clip before
reuse. Reset waits for earlier operations.
- `enhance` CLI plus the exploratory `enhance-benchmark`; fixes the
shared WER scorer's swapped insertion/deletion labels and adds
regression tests.

### Benchmark findings and fixes

The main evaluation covers 800 real AEC-Challenge recordings. Direct
reference comparisons support port fidelity, but the complete Hugging
Face table is **not reproduced**. The legacy protocol reproduces the
unprocessed baseline exactly; v1.2 far-end echo remains unresolved. The
model card declares plain whole-signal ERLE, while its reported values
resemble a separately reconstructed gated metric, so the two are now
reported separately instead of treating gated ERLE as the confirmed
upstream protocol.

The companion PR now includes a standard-library verifier that checks
all 13 saved result-file hashes, exact 800-clip coverage, scenario
membership, metric availability and every stored aggregate without
rerunning inference. The published model-card targets and source
revision are pinned alongside it.

The separate training-shard ASR study remains exploratory: 167/200
examples scored after excluding 33 empty reference transcripts.
Corrected v1.3 recall is 77.6% versus 44.1% unprocessed; leakage is 1.1%
versus 34.0%. Its dataset revision, archive and metadata hashes are now
pinned and verified. Malformed metadata, duplicate IDs and missing audio
fail loudly; JSON output records exact selected/excluded IDs, machine
transcripts and raw metric numerators/denominators.

[Benchmark data and
investigation](https://github.com/FluidInference/mobius/blob/3dc9231c1825ed04375b79ce0328fc81179ac2b9/models/enhancement/localvqe/coreml/REPRODUCTION.md)
retain all tested configurations, the historical 300-recording
follow-up, evidence verifier and unresolved differences.

### Automated LocalVQE benchmark

The new `LocalVQE Benchmark` workflow runs both variants over the pinned
200-example study on relevant PR changes, split into 5 contiguous shards
(`enhance-benchmark --shard i/5`) on parallel macOS runners because a
single runner exceeded the 60-minute job limit; a final job merges the
shard reports in order and verifies them as one 200-example report.
Protocol `localvqe-asr-v2` fixes Parakeet v3 int8 scoring to CPU,
records model/audio SHA256 fingerprints, per-file S/D/I counts and
timing, and rejects incomplete or invalid runs. An independent Python
verifier recomputes every score and aggregate and checks all selected
waveforms against the archive-derived 600-file manifest. Both variants
must improve recall and reduce leakage over the same-run unprocessed
baseline.

The workflow uploads the JSON report, logs and environment and publishes
a job summary. The first cloud run is
[here](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/actions/runs/35483779013)
(still running as of 2026-09-20 03:19 UTC). All 14 other PR checks
passed, including the full macOS test suite.

The **full local 200-example real-model run passed** on revision
`de4c0c03`: 167 examples scored, 33 empty-reference transcripts
excluded. The independent verifier passed coverage, audio/model
fingerprints, recomputed scores and improvement gates; all 12 verifier
tests passed on the full report, including deliberate corruption of
report coverage, counts and fingerprints.

| Condition | Recall | WER | Leakage |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Unprocessed | 42.47% | 112.71% | 34.03% |
| LocalVQE v1.3 | 77.08% | 29.48% | 0.95% |
| LocalVQE v1.2 | 73.34% | 33.78% | 1.09% |

These use protocol `localvqe-asr-v2`, Parakeet v3 int8, CPU-only and
256ms enhancement exports. They remain exploratory training-shard
results with machine transcripts, not a reproduction of the upstream
800-recording table. Historical exploratory figures above are not a
frozen baseline for the new explicit CPU protocol.

The macOS suite's cold-cache Sortformer download race is addressed by
running speaker-enrollment tests serially before the remaining parallel
tests; assertions are retained.

### Validation

- Release build, strict Swift formatting and diff checks passed.
- The committed evidence verifier passed for 13 runs × 800 unique clips.
- Standalone harness linked to actual FluidAudio and real v1.3 models
passed 13 audio comparisons: overlap ordering, cancellation,
reset/reuse, independent streams, buffer sizes and chunk parity.
- Release streaming and whole-clip output were bit-identical, finite and
length-preserving on three predetermined real mic/reference recordings.
- Added XCTest regression methods; explicit
`FLUIDAUDIO_LOCALVQE_MODEL_DIR` enables real-model tests in CI and
missing supplied bundles fail.
- Local XCTest execution was blocked by this Mac's missing Xcode/XCTest
framework. The PR's Xcode CI executes the test suite.

[Streaming validation
report](https://github.com/FluidInference/FluidAudio/blob/367024e451f94fc8f7dcefe02acc2cf2bb523c15/Documentation/Enhancement/LocalVQEValidation.md)
records coverage and timing limits. Target-device reference timing,
route changes, audio callbacks and sustained live-call performance still
need application-level validation.

fix(tts/luxtts): remove spurious mid-phrase pauses and chunk long text (#937) (#942)

Fixes #937.

The pause is model-inherent and stochastic, not a conversion or
token-count bug: the upstream PyTorch reference renders the same texts
with the same gap at speed 1.0, and sweeping speed 1.0–1.3 makes it come
and go non-monotonically. Each (length, seed) is a fresh draw; longer
text just has more chances to land one. Upstream hides it via a silent
speed×1.3.

Host-side handling in `LuxTtsManager.synthesize`:

- Text that fits one pass (≤ 102 tokens and the graph limits) is
synthesized as before. The 102 cap is measured: the 106-token issue text
paused on 6 of 8 raw single-pass draws, while as two ~53-token spans all
six seeds were clean.
- Longer text is split into balanced continuation-prompted spans,
bounded by the prompt's frames-per-token ratio so each span stays ≤ 5 s
and can prompt the next one untruncated, and by the 256-token bucket
next to the prompt transcript. `speed` applies to the first span only;
later spans inherit pace. Implausible prompt ratios (> 12 frames/token,
or spans < 8 tokens) throw `inputTooLong` instead of rendering dozens of
passes.
- Each pass is scanned for gaps ≥ 80 ms between sustained-speech runs
(−45 dB rel. peak). Gaps beyond the span's punctuation (incl.
ellipses/quotes the G2P drops, via the text API) trigger a re-seed, up
to `maxRedraws` (default 3, CLI `--redraws`, 0 pins the raw pass).
Cleanest pass kept; never errors; the result reports `redraws` /
`residualPauses`. Cancellation is checked before every pass.
- Onset/tail trimming anchors on sustained speech, not the vocoder's
opening click, bringing seams from ~190 ms to ~80 ms.

Verification (gpu variant, quick-brown-fox 5 s prompt): reporter's 101-
and 138-char texts render with no gap ≥ 80 ms at −45 dB and verbatim
Parakeet transcripts across seeds 42–47; a 305-char paragraph keeps only
comma/period pauses plus one text-driven break the ladder cannot remove;
speed 1.2 propagates without compounding; speed 0.8 no longer errors;
E2E fixture parity exact with `maxRedraws: 0`. Each re-draw is one extra
pass (~60–100 ms on GPU).

Reviewer notes: second commit addresses the code-review findings
(details in its message). `LuxTtsContinuationTests` covers chunking,
token/frame budgets, single-pass fit, pause detection incl. the onset
click, trims, and the text pause allowance.

fix(vocab): make alignBaseWordsToUTF8Ranges iterative (#961) (#962)

Fixes #961.

`alignBaseWordsToUTF8Ranges` recursed once per base word and copied the
path at each level, so `ctcTokenEvaluateCandidates` SIGBUSed inside
Swift concurrency tasks at ~1–2k words (linear depth, quadratic memory,
quadratic time).

**Fix**
- Explicit-stack backtracking over one shared path (no recursion, no
per-level copies)
- Candidate starts limited to the delimiter run after the cursor, probed
with anchored literal matches
- Memoize `(wordIndex, cursor)` states that yielded no alignment
- Uniqueness semantics unchanged (0 or ≥2 alignments → all `nil`)

**Verification**
- Differential vs. old implementation: 0 mismatches over 200k randomized
texts
- 16k words in 7 ms, 50k in 21 ms inside a detached `Task`; old code
SIGBUSes at 1k in the same harness
- New test: 20k-word alignment in `Task.detached`, plus fail-closed on a
truncated word list

commits.message:
[Jobs] Managed job dependencies (#10876)

* [Jobs] Managed job dependencies

sky.jobs.launch(depends_on=[...]) makes a managed job wait for other
managed jobs: a controller claims it only once all of them are DONE, and
it runs only if all of them succeeded; otherwise its tasks are
cancelled with the reason. Dependencies are recorded in a new
job_dependencies table and require consolidation mode.

* [Jobs] sky jobs launch --depends-on; reject depends_on without consolidation mode

The CLI takes comma-separated managed job IDs and passes them as
depends_on. The /jobs/launch route answers 400 when depends_on is set
and the server does not run managed jobs in consolidation mode.

* [Docs] Regenerate the CLI reference for --depends-on

* [Jobs] Show which dependencies a waiting job is waiting for

A WAITING job whose dependencies are not all DONE shows 'Waiting for
dependency jobs 17, 18 to succeed' in details. Such a job no longer counts
toward the highest blocking priority, and its eligible_at is written when
its last dependency ended rather than at submission, so it is not reported
as never claimed while it waits.

fix(workflows): reject a multi-argument filter call in expressions (#3893)

* fix(workflows): reject a multi-argument filter call in expressions

`_apply_filter` parses a call with `re.fullmatch(r"(\w+)\((.+)\)")` and
hands the ENTIRE captured argument text to `_evaluate_simple_expression`
as one expression. Every filter in this subset takes exactly one argument,
so a two-argument call is not a valid expression and evaluates to None:

  {{ inputs.missing | default(1) }}        -> 1
  {{ inputs.missing | default(1, 2) }}     -> None    <-- silently wrong
  {{ inputs.name | join(",", "extra") }}   -> ValueError: join: expected a
                                              string separator, got NoneType

So `default` silently returns None instead of its default, and `join`
raises a message blaming the separator rather than the extra argument.

Fall through to the existing "unsupported form" error, which names the
filter and lists the accepted forms:

  filter 'default' used in an unsupported form (got '| default(1, 2)'): ...

The check is quote-aware, because a single argument may legitimately
contain a comma — `join(", ")` and `default("a, b")` must keep working, so
a plain split would reject valid expressions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(workflows): use the bracket-aware scanner for the multi-arg filter check

Review catch: my hand-rolled `_has_top_level_comma` was quote-aware but NOT
bracket-aware, so it treated the comma inside a list literal as an argument
separator. The evaluator supports list literals, so this rejected
expressions that work on main today:

  main:        {{ inputs.missing | default([1, 2]) }} -> [1, 2]
  with my PR:  ValueError: filter 'default' used in an unsupported form

That is a breaking change, not a fix.

Drop the helper and use `_find_top_level`, the same scanner the operator
splitting already uses — it skips commas inside quotes AND inside nested
brackets. Verified:

  default([1, 2])            -> [1, 2]      (restored)
  default([1,2])             -> [1, 2]      (restored)
  default([])                -> []          (restored)
  join(", ") / default("a, b") -> unchanged
  default(1, 2)              -> rejected    (the actual bug)
  join(",", "extra")         -> rejected
  default([1,2], 3)          -> rejected    (real 2nd arg after a literal)

Dict literals resolve to None both before and after, matching main.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(workflows): drop the unsupported dict-literal example from the comment

Addresses review feedback: `_evaluate_simple_expression` implements a list
literal branch only. A mapping such as `{"a": 1}` has no branch there and
falls through to dot-path resolution:

    list literal  [1, 2]     -> [1, 2]
    dict literal  {"a": 1}   -> None

So the comment's claim that the evaluator supports dict literals was wrong.

Comment-only; no behaviour change. `_find_top_level` is brace-aware as well as
bracket-aware (`_find_top_level('{"a": 1, "b": 2}', ',')` returns -1), so the
scanner treats such a comma as nested either way -- the example was simply
describing syntax the evaluator does not implement, which is exactly the kind
of thing a future change might have relied on.

feat(auth): add Bitbucket authentication provider (#4629)

* feat(auth): add Bitbucket authentication provider

Add a `bitbucket` provider to the authentication registry so private
Bitbucket Cloud and Data Center repositories can serve extension,
bundle, preset, and workflow artifacts through the existing opt-in
`~/.specify/auth.json` mechanism.

Schemes:
- `bearer` — repository/project/workspace access tokens (Cloud) and
  HTTP access tokens (Data Center): `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- `basic` — Atlassian API tokens: `Authorization: Basic
  base64(<username>:<token>)` where username is the Atlassian account
  email. Unlike Azure DevOps' `basic-pat` (which hardcodes an empty
  username), this credential needs a real username, so `auth.json`
  gains a `username` field.

Config validation (`load_auth_config`):
- `username` must be a non-empty string when present, must not contain
  ':' (RFC 7617 §2), is whitespace-normalized like `token_env`, and is
  required when `auth == "basic"`
- `basic` joins `bearer`/`basic-pat` in requiring `token` or `token_env`

Design: `resolve_token` returns the composite `<username>:<secret>`
credential for `basic` and `auth_headers` encodes it verbatim, keeping
the `AuthProvider` interface and the shared HTTP layer unchanged.
`auth_headers("basic")` rejects a token without ':' so a bare secret
cannot silently become a well-formed header with an empty username.

No changes to the download/redirect security path. Bitbucket Cloud's
Downloads endpoint 302s to a pre-signed S3 URL; the existing redirect
handler strips `Authorization` when leaving the declared hosts, which
is required (S3 rejects pre-signed requests carrying an auth header),
and catalog `sha256` covers integrity of that hop. Documented in
docs/reference/authentication.md with ready-to-paste examples.

Tests: 26 new cases in tests/test_authentication.py covering config
validation, provider headers (incl. UTF-8 credentials and the
bare-secret guard), token resolution, registry, and an end-to-end
`build_request` check against api.bitbucket.org.

* fix(alquimia): render /speckit-<name> invocations for the skills-only agent

`alquimia` was the only one of the 19 SkillsIntegration subclasses absent
from every set in _invocation_style.py. It installs
`.alquimia/skills/speckit-<name>/SKILL.md` and its own
`build_command_invocation()` already returns `/speckit-plan`, but
`is_slash_skills_agent("alquimia", True)` returned False, so the two
callers that consult it emitted the dotted form Alquimia never registers:

* HookExecutor._render_hook_invocation -> `/speckit.plan`
* `specify init`'s Next Steps panel    -> `/speckit.plan`

Measured before, for an identical on-disk layout:

  alquimia -> 2.1 /speckit.constitution      <-- wrong
  droid    -> 2.1 /speckit-constitution

and after:

  alquimia -> 2.1 /speckit-constitution
  droid    -> 2.1 /speckit-constitution

Added to CONDITIONAL_SLASH_AGENTS rather than ALWAYS_SLASH_AGENTS: it is
the conservative choice, matching `claude`, which shares alquimia's
`commands_subdir: "skills"`. `specify init` writes `ai_skills: true` for
alquimia, so this covers the real path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(alquimia): pin the invocation invariants instead of asserting them in prose

Addresses review feedback. The inline comment claimed "with skills disabled
the dotted form is correct" -- that is wrong. The dotted form is never correct
for Alquimia, which registers only `speckit-<name>/SKILL.md`.

The classification itself stays conditional, because the reviewer's mechanism
does not hold:

* `is_slash_skills_agent` returning False is not the last word. The remaining
  consumer falls through to `integration.build_command_invocation`, and
  `SkillsIntegration` overrides that to emit the hyphenated form
  (base.py:1607-1617). Both states render `/speckit-git-commit`.

* The `False` argument is unreachable. Both writers of `ai_skills` key off
  `integration.is_skills_mode(...)` (init.py:777-780,
  _helpers.py:288-291), and `SkillsIntegration.is_skills_mode` returns True
  unconditionally (base.py:1564-1570).

* Being a `SkillsIntegration` does not imply always-slash: ALWAYS_SLASH
  (devin, droid, grok, trae, zed) and CONDITIONAL_SLASH (agy, hermes, lingma,
  vibe, rovodev) are BOTH populated entirely by SkillsIntegration subclasses.
  Moving Alquimia alone would split it from five identical peers while
  changing no rendered output.

Replaces the incorrect comment with three tests:

  test_ai_skills_is_always_persisted_for_alquimia
  test_classified_like_its_skills_only_peers
  test_never_renders_the_dotted_form_in_either_skills_state

The last one asserts the rendered invocation is `/speckit-git-commit` in both
skills states, exercising the `build_command_invocation` fallback -- so the
reviewer's actual concern is enforced by a test rather than by prose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(alquimia): drive the real hook renderer and drop two inaccurate claims

Addresses three review comments, all of which were right.

1. `test_never_renders_the_dotted_form_in_either_skills_state` recreated the
   production if/elif chain inside the test instead of invoking it, so
   deleting the real fallback would have left it green -- it did not pin the
   regression its docstring claimed. Replaced with
   `test_hook_invocation_renders_the_hyphenated_form`, which drives
   `HookExecutor._render_hook_invocation`, one of the two production consumers
   of `is_slash_skills_agent`. Its non-slash path ends at
   `return f"/{command_id}"`, so the dotted form really is what the renderer
   emitted before this change. It now fails with the source reverted.

2. The inline comment said Alquimia matched "every other skills-only agent".
   It does not: Droid, Grok, Trae and Zed are skills-only too and sit in
   `ALWAYS_SLASH_AGENTS`. Narrowed to the other *conditionally classified*
   skills-only agents.

3. `test_ai_skills_is_always_persisted_for_alquimia` presented persistence as
   the discriminator between the two sets. It is not -- every
   `SkillsIntegration` subclass records `ai_skills` the same way, always-slash
   ones included. The docstring now says only that the conditional is
   satisfied for Alquimia, and `test_classified_like_its_skills_only_peers`
   states plainly that the split is a conventional grouping rather than a rule
   the code enforces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(alquimia): assert only Alquimia's own classification

Addresses review feedback. `test_classified_like_its_skills_only_peers`
asserted that a fixed peer list sat in CONDITIONAL_SLASH_AGENTS:

    peers = {"rovodev", "agy", "hermes", "lingma", "vibe"}

displayio: fast OnDiskBitmap on rotated displays

displayio: cache 64 bytes of an OnDiskBitmap file

get_pixel() did a seek and a read of 1-4 bytes for every pixel. The
file system caches the sector, but the calls alone cost about 13 us a
pixel on an RP2040. Read 64 bytes at a time and take the next pixels
from them.

busdisplay: refresh rotated displays in bands of columns

At rotation 90 and 270 a panel row is a column of the source bitmap.
Refreshing in panel rows made TileGrid read every source pixel from a
different source row. Refresh in bands of panel columns instead, so the
sources are read along their rows.

This matters most for OnDiskBitmap, which reads the file in that order.

displayio: 2048 byte area buffer on ports with a 24 KB stack

CIRCUITPY_DISPLAY_AREA_BUFFER_SIZE is now a make variable, 512 by
default. raspberrypi, espressif and samd51 set it to 2048, so a refresh
sends 4x fewer pieces and the fixed cost of a region update is paid
4x less often.

docs: generate llms.txt at the end of the HTML build

A small Sphinx extension writes llms.txt at the root of the HTML output:
one line per page with its title and first paragraph, in table-of-contents
order, so a coding agent pointed at the docs gets a compact map of them.
It only reads what the HTML build already parsed, so there is no second
build and no new dependency.

displayio: composite common TileGrid rows without per-pixel calls

For the common case - an 8 or 16 bpp Bitmap, a Palette without
dithering, a 16 bpp display, no scaling, no x flip and no transpose -
fill_area now handles a row in one function: it reads the bitmap row
directly and takes the colour from the palette cache, so get_pixel and
palette_get_color are no longer called for every pixel. palette_get_color
is only called when a colour is not cached yet. Everything else takes the
existing loop.

Full-screen repaint, main -> this commit:

  PicoPad (RP2040)             320x240 SPI   203 -> 90 ms
  Fruit Jam (RP2350)           320x240 DVI    92 -> 29 ms
  PyBadge (SAMD51)             160x128 SPI    60 -> 30 ms
  Feather ESP32-S3 TFT         240x135 SPI    70 -> 53 ms

Flash +0.8 to +0.9 KB depending on the port.
Output is unchanged: 16 test scenes checksum identically via fill_row

colours, a 16 bpp bitmap with indices past the end of its palette, and
a TileGrid with more than 255 tiles.

rp2 sdioio: make flush() wait for the SD card to finish

On RP2 boards, flush() and close() on an SDIO card returned before the
card had finished saving the data. The driver keeps a write open between
calls for speed, and the sync step that should close it did nothing.

Now sync, unmount and deinit end the open write and wait for the card.
flush() takes about 1 ms longer and write speed is unchanged.

Found by @ptorrone while testing SD speed on the Fruit Jam.

commits.message:
codegen: escape a oneof enum name that PascalCases to Self (#465)

A oneof named `self` makes code generation fail outright. PascalCasing
the name produces `Self`, which is a reserved Rust identifier, so the
generator emits `pub enum Self`, the generated file does not parse, and
`generate` returns an error that names no oneof at all. The same escape
is already applied one function below to the oneof's *variant* names,
and to the struct field, so this applies it to the enum's own name as
well and the three finally agree.

`oneof_enum_ident` (`buffa-codegen/src/oneof.rs:932`) builds the
identifier with a bare `format_ident!`. `self`, `self_` and `_self` all
reach it, because `to_pascal_case` (`oneof.rs:972`) splits on `_` and
capitalises each part, and `Self` is the only reserved Rust identifier
with a leading capital, so it is the only reachable case. The ident is
produced once in `resolve_oneof_idents` (`oneof.rs:954`) and consumed
for both the owned enum (`oneof.rs:679`) and the view enum
(`view.rs:1105`). `format_tokens` (`buffa-codegen/src/lib.rs:4332`) runs
`syn::parse2::<syn::File>` before prettyplease sees the tokens, so the
result is `CodeGenError::InvalidSyntax("generated code failed to parse
as Rust: ...")` for a perfectly legal `.proto`.

`oneof_variant_ident` (`oneof.rs:967`) already routes through
`make_field_ident`, and its doc comment spells out this exact failure:
it "would otherwise produce `pub enum Foo { Self(...) }` and fail to
parse". `CodeGenContext::oneof_ident` (`context.rs:534`) escapes the
struct field too. Only the enum's own name was left raw, so for a oneof
named `self_` the generated field is `self_` and the type it points at
is `Self`.

No fixture puts a keyword on the oneof itself, which is why this
survived: `buffa-test/protos/keywords.proto` covers keyword package,
message, field and enum-value names, including `string self = 4;` at
line 35, but its one oneof is named `value`, and the #47 regression test
(`buffa-codegen/src/tests/naming.rs:1147`) puts the keyword on a variant
while naming the oneof `identity`.

The fix routes the enum name through `make_field_ident`
(`idents.rs:67`), exactly as the variant name already is, so `Self`
becomes `Self_` and matches the #47 convention. It is a no-op for every
other name: `make_field_ident` only rewrites when `is_rust_keyword`
matches, PascalCasing always yields a leading capital, and `Self` is the
only capitalised entry in that table (`idents.rs:181`). The checked-in
generated trees are unaffected, since the only oneof in either is
`google.protobuf.Value.kind` yielding `Kind`, so nothing needs
regenerating. `format_ident!` had no other use in `oneof.rs`, so its
import goes with it; that is the only other line in the diff.

`test_oneof_named_self_escapes_its_enum_to_self_underscore` sits beside
the #47 test it mirrors: it generates a message with a oneof named
`self_` and asserts the enum is `Self_` while the non-keyword variant is
untouched. On unpatched source it is the `generate(...).expect(...)`
that fails, because generation errors out before any assertion runs.

`cargo fmt --check -p buffa-codegen` is clean on the pinned 1.95.0
toolchain. I have not run the test suite on this machine, so CI is the
check on the new test.

The changelog fragment is
`.changes/unreleased/fixed-20260919-210200.yaml`. It does not cite a PR
number yet; happy to amend that in once this has one.

messages_fetch: report the conversation each message belongs to (#245)

Messages the user sends from another device are synced to chat.db
without a sender handle, so until now most of the user's own messages
came back with sender "me" and nothing to tie them to a conversation;
a client could not thread them or tell who they were sent to.

identifier, its display name (group chats) and its participants.
Chats are looked up once per call and shared by their messages.

commits.message:
feat(clip): publish queue for clips (#1751)

* test(server): give the streamer service fixture the clip exports

The clips field was added to ServiceRegister (#1747) while the streamer
service tests (#1749) were written against the old struct, so the biliup-cli
lib tests no longer compile on master.

* refactor(upload): split studio building and report upload progress

Split the template-to-Studio builder out of build_studio as
studio_from_template (cover upload stays in build_studio), share the @credit
expansion as desc_with_credits, add upload_single_file_with_progress and make
resolve_source crate-visible, so the clip publisher can reuse them.
Whole-stream uploads behave as before.

* feat(clip): publish settings and archive rendering for clips

- Clips pick an upload template (default: the streamer's) and may override
  title, description, tags, category, schedule and cover (StudioOverride,
  stored in clips.studio_override); the override is merged into the template
  and built through the same studio_from_template path as whole-stream uploads.
- New title / description variables {clip_title} and {clip_time}; % in values
  is escaped and a malformed strftime in the template is kept as text instead
  of panicking. @credit is expanded like whole-stream uploads.
- Copyright is always forced to reprint (2); the source is the template's
  reprint source, falling back to the live room URL. A self-made template is
  not followed.
- Pre-flight problems (no template, empty title, no tags, Noop uploader,
  scheduled time outside 4 hours to 15 days) are reported before queueing.
- clips gains set_publish_settings and mark_published; the latter records
  archive_bvid / published_at and releases the clip's segment pins in the same
  transaction, keeping the clip file.

* feat(clip): single-concurrency publish queue that pauses on 601

- A dedicated queue (not the recorder's UActor) handles one archive at a time:
  export when needed -> initialize_upload_context -> upload each part ->
  cover -> submit_to_bilibili, reporting the step, detail, upload ratio and
  parts already uploaded per job. Jobs live in memory only.
- B站 601 pauses the whole queue until resume() is called; nothing is retried
  automatically and there is no daily cap.
- Other failures keep the reason on the job (a rejected cover says so) and can
  be retried; parts already uploaded are not uploaded again, and a part whose
  clip range changed is dropped and re-uploaded.
- Jobs can be cancelled while exporting or uploading, not while submitting.
- On success the clips are marked published with the BV id.

* feat(clip): grab a JPEG frame from a recording for clip covers

thumb::grab uses the quick-cut plan to find the keyframe range covering t,
pipes it into FFmpeg (tools::ffmpeg_command, so the configured or bundled
ffmpeg is used) and decodes up to t. A frame on the segment still being
written waits up to 5 s; a time past the recording or in a gap says so in
cover terms.

* feat(clip): publish, cover and frame endpoints

- POST /v1/clips/{cid}/publish (optionally saving publish settings first)
  queues export -> upload -> submit and returns 202; POST /v1/publish-jobs
  publishes several clips, one archive per clip by default or one multi-part
  archive (combine: same session, up to 100 parts). Every archive is checked
  before anything is queued.
- GET /v1/publish-jobs, POST /v1/publish-jobs/preview, /resume,
  /{jid}/retry and DELETE /v1/publish-jobs/{jid} expose the queue.
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/thumb returns a frame; GET / PUT / DELETE
  /v1/clips/{cid}/cover sets a clip cover from a frame, the recorded live
  cover or an uploaded JPEG / PNG / WebP (up to 5 MB).
- PATCH on a clip stores template_id / studio_override; clips in the queue
  cannot be re-ranged or deleted (409).
- Routes are classified in the policy table: publishing needs upload.submit,
  viewing the queue and frames file.view, changing covers clip.edit.

refactor(server): extract config apply and streamer ops into services (#1749)

* refactor(server): extract configuration apply into a service

Move the body of `put_configuration` (validate, upsert the `config` row,
set the ffmpeg path, resize the download/upload pools, swap the in-memory
config and hot-reload the log filter) into
`server::services::configuration::apply_config`, which takes no axum types.
The handler now only maps `ApplyConfigError` to the same responses as
before: `Invalid` -> 400 with `ApiError`, `Internal` -> `report_to_response`.

No behaviour change. Refs #1744.

* refactor(server): extract streamer operations into services

Move the core of the streamer add / update / delete / pause handlers
(write the row, then `add_room` / `del_room` / pause state changes) into
`server::services::streamers`. Permission checks on hook fields and
response redaction stay in the handlers; status codes, bodies and log
messages are unchanged.

No behaviour change. Refs #1744.

* refactor(server): expose Slots::occupied

Report how many slots are currently taken; the slot tests use it instead of reaching into the private state. Refs #1744.

* refactor(server): make SystemStats deserializable

Derive Deserialize for SystemStats and its nested Sample / MemoryUsage / DiskUsage / CpuInfo. Serialized output is unchanged; a round-trip test pins the exact JSON. Refs #1744.

feat(clip): clips table and export API (#1747)

* feat(clip): add the clips table and CRUD API

Migration 10 adds `clips`: a range on a session's timeline (in_ms/out_ms)
plus what its latest export produced. GET/POST /v1/sessions/{id}/clips,
PATCH/DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/clips/{cid} and GET /v1/clips/{cid} are
declared in the permission table: file.view to look, clip.edit to change.
Responses carry the output file name, never a path.

* refactor(clip): let the workbench reuse the DVR FLV tag and TS packet helpers

* feat(clip): plan keyframe cuts from session time to segment byte ranges

The in point snaps to the keyframe at or before it and the out point to
the keyframe at or after it (or the segment end), the same rule as
/v1/sessions/{id}/keyframes. Segments in between are taken whole and
recording gaps are spliced without black frames. A deleted or missing
segment, or a change of codec parameters inside the range, is reported
with its position instead of being skipped. When the out point is in the
segment still being written and no keyframe follows yet, resolve() waits
for the live index to catch up (up to a timeout).

* feat(clip): remux FLV clips in-process

Quick cuts copy tag by tag from the planned keyframe, rewrite DTS so the
clip starts at 0 and stays strictly increasing across segment joins, drop
audio before the first keyframe and the sources' script tags, and write a
fresh onMetaData (duration, filesize, keyframe table) that is backfilled
once the clip is complete. No transcoding.

* feat(clip): remux MPEG-TS clips in-process

The clip starts with the first segment's PAT/PMT and the video IDR PES.
PTS/DTS/PCR are shifted so video starts at 0 (33-bit wrap handled),
continuity counters carry on across segment joins, and audio before the
first keyframe is dropped.

* feat(clip): remux fragmented MP4 clips in-process

For Bilibili hls_fmp4 sessions: copy the first segment's ftyp + moov, then
moof/mdat pairs from the planned keyframe on. mfhd sequence numbers are
renumbered, every track's tfdt is rebased (in its own timescale) so the
clip starts at 0, absolute base_data_offset is rewritten, and other
top-level boxes (styp, sidx, prft) are dropped.

* feat(clip): export clips in the background, pin their sources and cut the last N seconds

POST /v1/clips/{cid}/export (202, also the retry) runs a quick cut as a
background job: at most two at a time, progress (phase + ratio) kept in
memory and returned with the clip, output written to
clips/<session>/<clip>.<ext> via a .part file. A failure removes the
partial file and stores a reason that says what to do; exports cut off by
a restart are marked failed at startup and can be retried.
GET /v1/clips/{cid}/download serves the finished file.

A clip pins the segments under [in_ms, out_ms] as clip:<id> from the
moment it is created, widens the pin to the keyframe actually cut at,
follows range edits and drops it on delete, so the rm post-processor
defers deleting them. clips::release() is there for publishing later.

POST /v1/sessions/{id}/clips also takes last_ms ("cut the last N
seconds", out point converted from what is on screen the same way as
markers) and export to start right away.

* feat(clip): precise cuts and MP4 downloads via ffmpeg

Precise export feeds the same keyframe-aligned stream the quick cut builds
(segment joins, gaps and the growing tail already handled) into ffmpeg
through a pipe and trims frame-accurately with -ss/-to after the input,
encoding H.264 (libx264 veryfast crf 20) + AAC 192k MP4 with faststart.
At most one runs at a time.

GET /v1/clips/{cid}/download?format=mp4 serves MP4 output as is and
otherwise remuxes the quick cut with -c copy once, cached next to it.

When ffmpeg is missing, lacks libx264, runs out of disk, is interrupted,
or cannot read HEVC that Chinese platforms write into FLV as codec id 12,
the failure says so and what to do instead (quick cut, source download,
another ffmpeg via ffmpeg_path). Loader warnings are not taken as the
reason.

* fix(clip): rebase PES timestamps of streams missing from the first PMT

Some Huya HLS first segments declare only the video PID in their PMT
while audio PES are already on the wire; the later PMTs in the same
segment list both. Treat any elementary PID that starts a PES as a
stream so its PTS/DTS get rebased, and only copy PSI into the file
header.

* fix(clip): keep waiting when a live segment is renamed off .part

stream-gears renames x.flv.part to x.flv when it closes a segment. A
cut whose out point is at the live tip could plan against the old name
and fail with "source file missing". Wait and re-plan when a recording
segment's file disappears, and fall back to the renamed file when
opening a planned piece.

* fix(clip): give a live session a moment to open its next segment

The recorder closes a segment and opens the next one as two events, and
waiters wake after each. A cut whose out point lies past the segment
that just closed could be planned in between and silently stop at the
old segment's end. While the session is recording and the plan ends on
its last segment, re-plan for a few seconds before cutting what exists.

* fix(clip): delete half-written clip files left by a crash at startup

A kill during export left clips/<session>/<id>.<ext>.part behind until
the clip was retried or deleted. Startup recovery now removes them
alongside marking the interrupted exports as failed.

* refactor(clip): clean up half-written clip files in a separate startup step

Keeps recover() about the clips table and gives the .part cleanup its
own function and test.
