fix(clip): keep marked footage until the marker is removed (#1746)

* fix(clip): keep marked footage until the marker is removed

Markers from the live preview only wrote the markers table, so the
segments they covered had no reference and the post-processing `rm`,
the small-file filter and upload-while-recording deleted them right away,
although the retention setting says marked footage waits until the
reference is released.

Each marker now pins [at_ms - lookback_ms, at_ms + lookahead_ms] as
`marker:<id>` through retention::pin, in the same transaction as the
marker write: creating pins the range, changing the time or range moves
it, renaming leaves it alone, deleting (including undo) unpins it. A
range that reaches into the part still being recorded covers segments
opened later, as pin already handles.

* fix(clip): pin markers made before pinning on startup

Markers created before markers pinned their range have no segment_pins
row. The startup recovery now registers the missing pins once (only
markers without one) and refreshes pin_count for the affected sessions.

* style(clip): rustfmt the marker pinning code

fix(upload): turn template credits into desc_v2 @mentions (#1745)

* fix(config): accept documented {username, uid} credits in config files

StreamerConfig.credits was typed as the B站 desc_v2 node
(biliup::bilibili::Credit, requires type_id/raw_text), so a config file
written as documented in public/config.toml / config.yaml
({ username, uid }) failed to parse with "missing field type_id".
Use a TemplateCredit type with the same shape the Web UI stores in
uploadstreamers.credits; uid accepts a number or a string.

* fix(upload): turn template credits into desc_v2 @mentions

build_studio() hard-coded .maybe_desc_v2(None) since the Python backend
was removed, so the template credits were never read and the literal
"@credit" placeholder was submitted as plain text.

Replace each @credit with the configured user in order, producing the
same desc / desc_v2 shape as the old Python creditsToDesc_v2, except that
no empty text node is emitted (B站 rejects a leading empty type-1 node
with 21010). Unusable entries (empty username, non-numeric uid) are
skipped with a warning; extra credits or extra placeholders are logged.

feat(clip): markers from live preview (#1742)

* feat(auth): add the clip.edit permission

New permission point for the clip workbench (markers now, clip drafts later). Admins have every permission; operators get it by default; viewers do not, so a viewer can watch previews and browse sessions but cannot mark or cut. Roles are fixed in code, so no migration is needed.

* feat(workbench): register recording sessions with a timeline anchor

The live-session registry (P4) now also carries a (session time, wall clock) pair: the session writer records one every time a segment opens or closes, and markers use the latest pair to convert 'now' into session time. The session timeline follows container time inside a segment and wall clock between segments, so the conversion restarts from the latest segment boundary instead of from the session start.

A session resumed after a stream drop is registered before its next segment opens and has no pair until then. When the only segment of a session is discarded as empty, the registration is dropped with it, so /v1/streamers never reports a session that has no timeline.

* feat(clip): markers table and API

- Migration 9: markers (session time, label, color, author, look-back / look-ahead range; default look-back 60 s). LF only, digest pinned in the frozen migration list.
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/markers (file.view)
- POST /v1/sessions/{id}/markers, PATCH / DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}/markers/{mid} (clip.edit)

The routes are declared in the permission route table and checked by the policy layer like every other route; the handlers do not look at roles.

A marker created from the live preview carries no session time. The client sends the moment the button was pressed and the moment the request was sent, both on its own clock (only the difference is used, so the client clock does not have to be right), plus the player's latency (buffered media not yet shown). The server subtracts both from its own clock to get the wall-clock time the frame on screen was recorded, then converts it with the recording session's timeline anchor. An explicit at_ms is taken as is, for marking while watching a recording.

* feat(api): report the live session's marker count on /v1/streamers

Rooms that are recording already carry session_id (P4); they now also carry marker_count, so cards and the multi-view can show how many markers this broadcast has. The count is null whenever session_id is null, and a failed count query only drops the field for that poll.

* feat(ui): mark the live picture from the preview

- Preview modal: a Mark button under the player and the M shortcut while the modal is open. Marking shows one toast with Undo / Rename and does not take focus or pause playback. The request carries the press time and the player's buffered-but-not-shown time, so the marker lands on the frame that was on screen.
- Without clip.edit (viewers) the button is disabled and the reason is shown next to it; before the first segment is written it explains that too.
- Streamer cards and multi-view tiles show how many markers this broadcast has.
- Phones: the Mark button is a full-width 48 px button.

* fix(clip): place live markers by what the open segment has written

* fix(clip): keep sampling the open segment and take the most advanced recent write

* fix(clip): count segment open and close as timeline observations

* fix(clip): observe tapped segments where the index task has scanned them

The keyframe index task sees each write of an in-process downloader before its write buffer. It now remembers how far each tapped segment has got and when it first got there, and the marker sampler uses that instead of rescanning the file; external downloaders keep the disk rescan. Low bitrate mesio streams only reach the disk every ten seconds or so through the 1 MiB write buffer, which left marks there up to 2.5 s early.

* refactor(auth): gate "keep this session" behind clip.edit

PATCH /v1/sessions/{id} (retain_until) was declared under recording.control
until the clip workbench had its own permission point. Keeping a session is
part of the clip workflow, so it now needs clip.edit. Both points belong to
admins and operators, so who can call the route does not change.

* fix(clip): find tapped segments by the recorded path

Since the recorder and retention normalize segment paths (dropping "."
components), a segment the writer reports as ./x.flv is recorded as x.flv,
while the streaming index still keyed it by ./x.flv. Lookups with the
recorded path missed it, so live markers fell back to scanning the file on
disk (off by up to a few seconds on low-bitrate streams) and reads of the
open segment rescanned instead of using the live index. Key the live index
by the same normalized path.

* test(clip): pin the live index key with the ./ prefix the writer reports

The previous test joined "." into an absolute temp path; Path equality
already ignores interior "." components, so it passed without the fix.
Only a leading "./" differs from the recorded path, so check register /
advance / written / unregister with "./x.flv" against "x.flv" directly,
in memory.

* fix(ui): point the marker hint at the recording playback page

Clipping happens in the existing live and recording playback pages rather than a separate clip page, so the hint under the Mark button now says the marker can be cut later in recording playback.

fix(config): reject zero pool sizes and clarify when a larger download pool applies (#1743)

Pool sizes now take effect on save, so a 0 silently stops every new
recording or upload. Reject pool1_size / pool2_size = 0 with 400 in
PUT /v1/configuration and set min={1} on both inputs. Note in the
download pool hint that rooms skipped while the pool was full start at
their next check.

Follows the choices ForgQi confirmed for #1741.

fix(workbench): normalize segment paths in the recorder and retention (#1740)

* test(mesio): read segment events as WriterEvent in the path test

The test added with the ./ prefix fix destructured segment events as tuples;
the recorder change turned them into WriterEvent, so the biliup-cli test
target no longer compiled once both landed.

* fix(recorder): record each mesio segment once

With the default mesio downloader the writer reports `./x.flv` when a
segment opens, but the close callback now strips the prefix and reports
`x.flv`. The session recorder compared the two literally, treated them as
different segments and wrote two rows per file, doubling the session
timeline.

Normalize every path at the recorder entry points (opened, closed,
deleted, and the danmaku path) by dropping `.` components, so all
downloaders' open and close events meet on one spelling. mesio's open
callback and index tap now use the same prefix-free form as its close
callback, matching stream-gears.

* fix(retention): match segments by the same normalized path as the recorder

The recorder stores segment paths without `.` components, but deletion
and move points look rows up with the path post-processing hands them.
External ffmpeg / streamlink segments arrive there as `./x.flv`, so a
referenced or retained segment would not be recognized and would be
deleted right away.

Move the normalization into workbench::segment_path and use it both at
the recorder entry points and wherever retention binds or compares a
segment or danmaku path.

feat: system stats on the console and runtime pool resizing (#1741)

* Add system stats and runtime pool resizing

This change adds a system monitor for console CPU, memory, disk, and network stats, served from a new /v1/system-stats endpoint with incremental polling support. It also introduces runtime-adjustable slot pools for download and upload concurrency so configuration saves immediately resize active pools without restarting in-flight work. The UI text is updated to clarify the behavior, and permissions/router registration are wired up for the new stats API.

The upload actor in the previous commit still carried the
'Updated upstream / Stashed changes' conflict markers, so the crate
did not compile. Keep the slot-based dispatcher (run_in_slots +
free handle_message) and use the renamed session_id column from

Show the new GET /v1/system-stats data on the console: CPU and
network sparklines over the server-side history, memory and the
recording directory's disk as usage bars, with the container-limit,

feat(api): session list and seekable DVR media stream (#1739)

* feat(downloader): let readers wait for ByteCounter growth

ByteCounter gains watch(): a subscriber waits until the byte total moves past what it has seen, instead of polling. Writers only touch the Notify while someone is watching, so the hot path is unchanged when nobody subscribes.

* fix(workbench): write keyframe index through a unique temp file

The recorder finalizing a segment and a reader refreshing the same index could both write <segment>.idx.tmp and rename it underneath each other. Each writer now uses its own temp name; the later rename wins and both copies are complete. A failed write no longer leaves the temp file behind.

* feat(workbench): register sessions being recorded

Once a session has its first segment (or is resumed within the merge window with segments already on it), the session writer registers it together with the download's byte counter, and bumps a change watch after every segment-table update (segment opened / closed / removed, recording ended). Readers following the tail of a live session subscribe to both instead of polling the file. Downloads without a byte counter (upload-while-recording, yt-dlp) are still registered but cannot be followed.

* feat(workbench): seekable DVR stream over recorded segments

Serve a session from any time position straight from the segment files: file header and sequence headers first, then tags / packets from the nearest keyframe not later than the requested time.

- FLV and MPEG-TS are remuxed in place, rewriting timestamps to the session timeline (session ms + 1000) so they stay monotonic across segments; TS PTS/DTS/PCR handle the 33-bit wrap and continuity counters are spliced per PID at a join. Fragmented MP4 is refused.
- Adjacent segments are joined when there is no gap and the decoder configuration is unchanged; a gap, a codec change or a different container ends the stream so the player reopens at the next segment.
- A segment still being written is followed through the byte counter and segment-table notifications, never by polling.
- Sending is paced to 1x after a fixed read-ahead so catching up does not flood the player buffer.

* feat(api): session list and seekable DVR media stream

- GET /v1/sessions: paginated, filterable by streamer
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}: segments and gaps
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/keyframes?from=&to=: cut positions on the session timeline
- GET /v1/sessions/{id}/media?from=: chunked FLV / MPEG-TS for mpegts.js; 415 for fragmented MP4, 429 beyond 8 concurrent DVR streams per process

Only sessions with a timeline are listed: rows left by older versions, and sessions that have not written a segment yet, have none. Sessions are addressed by id and session time only; no file paths are accepted.

Access is decided by the policy layer from the route table: file.view for the listing endpoints, preview.view for the media stream; the handlers make no permission checks of their own. The stream has no Content-Length, so the access layer cuts it off when the caller's session is revoked.

* feat(api): expose the recording session id on /v1/streamers

Rooms that are recording carry session_id so the UI can open the live session's timeline.

* fix(workbench): report a caught-up DVR stream as recording stopped

When the stream reaches the end of the last segment and nothing is recording, the session may still resume within the merge window (e.g. while the downloader reconnects), so do not log it as the session having ended.

* docs(api): note that session list totals only count finished segments

* fix(downloader): make ByteWatch wait until the total passes the given mark

grown_since returned as soon as the total differed from the argument, so a caller could not ask to be woken only after a certain amount of further growth. The counter only increases, so compare with >.

* perf(workbench): back off DVR tail reads while counted bytes are not on disk yet

mesio counts every FLV tag before its repair pipeline, but the pipeline writes to disk in GOP-sized bursts, so a reader following the tail woke about 40 times a second and found nothing new almost every time. After a wake that reads nothing, wait for the counter to grow a further 16 KiB, doubling up to 256 KiB while reads keep coming back empty, and reset once data arrives. Segment-table changes still wake the reader immediately.

* feat(workbench): wait for the streaming keyframe index before joining a new segment

When a DVR stream reaches a segment that was just opened and has no keyframe yet, it used to re-check the index every 256 KiB of byte-counter growth, which re-scanned the recording file. Segments indexed while recording now publish a notification each time their index cache is saved, or when streaming indexing gives up on them. The reader waits for that and reads the cache without touching the file. Segments without a streaming index (external downloaders) keep the byte-counter probe and scan on demand.

* fix(api): report only what is on disk as playable in session detail

* fix(workbench): end a DVR response before an unreadable segment

* fix(api): estimate the on-disk playable end past the last written keyframe

* fix(api): check the session before taking a DVR connection slot

* fix(mesio): report opened segment paths without the ./ prefix too

With the output directory `.`, mesio's writers report `./x.flv`. Closing a
segment already strips the prefix, but opening one did not, so the session
recorder saw `./x.flv` opened and `x.flv` closed as two different files:
it finalized the open row and inserted a second row for the same file,
doubling every segment on the session timeline.

Strip the prefix in one place for both events, and update the test to the
open/close event channel so it compiles again.

* fix(mesio): key the streaming keyframe index by the reported path

The index tap opened the live index under the writer's `./x.flv` while the
segment rows now record `x.flv`, so lookups for a segment being recorded
missed the streaming index and fell back to scanning the file on disk.
Open it under the same reported path as the segment events.

* test(workbench): fill the new SessionTarget field in retention tests

* fix(workbench): keep playing segments that are waiting for deletion

Segments marked pending_delete keep their files so they can still be
watched and cut; locate already treats them as readable. The DVR stream
used its own stricter check and ended the response at such a segment, or
when the segment it was reading was marked. Use the shared check and
treat pending_delete like finished at the end of a file.

* chore(router): drop the patch import now that PATCH shares the session route

feat(storage): pin referenced segments and retention sweeper (#1738)

* test(mesio): read WriterEvent::Closed in the ./ prefix test

The test from #1737 destructured the segment channel as a tuple, but #1736
changed it to carry WriterEvent, so the biliup-cli test target no longer
compiled on master.

* feat(storage): pin referenced segments and retention sweeper

Deletion points (postprocessor rm, sync-downloader cleanup after the
part is confirmed, FileValidator dropping small files) now go through
workbench::retention::remove. A recorded segment that is referenced
(pin_count > 0), belongs to a session before its retain_until, or has
to be kept for retention_hours after upload is marked pending_delete
instead of being deleted; a sweeper running every minute deletes it
(with its .idx and danmaku XML) once it is due and unreferenced.
Otherwise the file is deleted right away as before and the row becomes
deleted. Files without a segments row are handled exactly as before.

- mv moves the .idx along and updates segments.path / index_path /
  danmaku_path.
- pin/unpin register a session time range per owner (segment_pins,
  migration 8); pin_count is recomputed from the ranges on pin, unpin
  and segment writes, so ranges reaching into the live tail cover
  segments written later and re-pinning is idempotent.
- min_free_space: when the disk holding recorded segments drops below
  it, delete finished segments oldest-first, unreferenced before
  referenced, never the one being recorded. Off by default.
- retention_hours defaults to 0: rm keeps deleting immediately.
- A late close event no longer overwrites a pending_delete / deleted
  decision; pending_delete segments stay readable.

Ref #1726

* feat(api): keep a session with PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}

Sets or clears stream_sessions.retain_until. Until then, the session's
segments are only marked pending_delete at deletion points and rank
after unreferenced segments in the free-space guard. Uses the
recording.control permission for now.

Ref #1726

* feat(ui): settings for keeping recordings after upload and minimum free space

A switch plus hours for retention_hours (the switch is derived from the
value, so saving still sends the same keys) and a size field for
min_free_space. Empty values are normalised before the whole-config PUT.

Ref #1726

* fix(storage): keep filtered segments of kept sessions when the close event lands first

The recorder marked a segment below the filtering threshold as deleted as
soon as its close event arrived. When that write beat the validator's
deletion, the deletion point no longer recognised the segment and removed
it at once, ignoring the session's retain_until. Record the row by what is
on disk and let the deletion point decide.

* chore(ui): drop unrelated reformatting from the global settings panel

Only the retention and minimum free space fields change; the existing help
texts keep their original line breaks.

* fix(storage): leave keyframe indexes still being built to the recorder

With the index built while recording, the index task saves <segment>.idx
once more when the segment closes. Deleting that file earlier would leave
an orphan index behind. Deletion points skip the index of a segment the
index task still holds (the recorder removes it after syncing), and the
sweeper and low-disk guard leave such segments to the next round.

* fix(storage): let filter deletion wait for the recorder to settle the closed segment

FileValidator removed too-small segments from a spawned task that raced the
recorder. With stream-gears the row still carried the .part path, so the
deletion point did not recognise the segment and deleted it immediately even
when the session was kept, leaving the row finished without a file. The
deletion now waits on RecorderHandle::settled(); sync recording does the same.

* fix(mesio): report segment start paths without the ./ prefix too

#1737 stripped the ./ prefix from the paths mesio reports when a segment
closes, but not from the path reported when it opens. The recorder matches
the two by path, so with the output directory . every mesio segment was
recorded twice: the ./ row closed as a gap, and a second row inserted by the
close event.

feat(recorder): stream sessions, segments table and keyframe index (#1736)

* feat(recorder): add stream_sessions, session_streamerinfo and segments tables

Migration 7 creates the recording-side tables for the clip workbench:
one row per live session, the streamerinfo rows it spans (a session
merged across a short disconnect keeps several), and one row per
segment file with its position on the session timeline in ms.

Keyframe indexes stay out of SQLite; they are cached next to each
segment as <segment>.idx. Migrations 1-6 are untouched; the frozen
checksum list and the upgrade test now include migration 7.

* feat(recorder): keyframe index for FLV, TS and fragmented MP4 segments

A read-only scanner maps segment time to byte offsets and caches the
result next to the segment as <segment>.idx (versioned header with the
header-region length, then (t_ms, byte_offset) per keyframe).

- FLV: reads tag headers plus the first body bytes only; a finished
  mesio FLV is seeded from onMetaData.keyframes and only the tail is
  scanned, falling back to a full scan when the metadata is missing,
  truncated or points at non-keyframes.
- TS: PAT/PMT to the video PID, keyframe = PES with the random access
  indicator or an IDR as first picture NAL (H.264/H.265), 33-bit PTS
  wrap handled.
- fMP4: video track from moov/trex, keyframe = moof whose first video
  sample is a sync sample. Non-fragmented MP4 is reported unsupported.

Segment time starts at 0 on the first keyframe; the container's raw
timestamp there is kept in the index, so absolute stream-gears FLV
timestamps, the source tfdt kept by bilibili hls_fmp4 and TS PTS are
handled without rewriting files. Segments still being written are
scanned incrementally from the last offset; a shrunk or replaced file
truncates or rebuilds the cache.

Uses the ts crate from rust-srec at the rev already in the lock. The
mp4 crate only probes init segments and keeps its box walker private,
so fMP4 uses a minimal box reader here.

* feat(recorder): record stream sessions and segments from the segment callbacks

Each download task gets a session recorder: downloader callbacks only
push an event into an unbounded channel, and a per-task writer task
writes stream_sessions / segments in order and builds the keyframe
index after a segment closes. Nothing on the recording path waits on
SQLite or disk scans, and database errors are only logged. Upload goes
through UActor exactly as before.

Timeline: t = 0 is the wall clock when the session's first segment
starts writing. Inside a segment time follows the container (duration
reported by the downloader, else the scanned index, else wall clock);
between segments the wall clock at segment start continues the
timeline, and a start more than 1 s after the previous end is stored as
gap_before_ms.

Downloader coverage:
- mesio: start and close callbacks through one channel, close carries
  duration and size.
- stream-gears: LifecycleFile gains a start hook fired on create(), the
  .part name is renamed to the final path on close.
- ffmpeg (external segmenting) and streamlink: start when the process
  is spawned, close on rename.
- ffmpeg internal segmenting and yt-dlp: close only; the start is
  derived from the segment's content duration.

Segments filtered by filtering_threshold are kept as 'deleted'; files
that never reached the disk leave no row, and a task that produced no
segment leaves no session.

Merge: a new task reuses the streamer's previous session when it ended
at most clip_session_merge_minutes ago (default 10, 0 disables); the
new streamerinfo row is linked through session_streamerinfo.
streamerinfo, filelist and upload behaviour are unchanged.

Startup recovery, before monitors start: leftover 'recording' segments
are finished from the file length with end_ms from the (truncated or
resumed) keyframe index, and unended sessions get ended_at from their
last segment.

Internal API for later workbench parts: locate(session, t_ms) returns
segment, header length and byte offset of the keyframe at or before
t_ms; session_keyframes(session, from, to) lists keyframes across
segments. The postprocessor rm step also deletes the .idx cache.

* feat(sync): record 边录边传 segments in the session timeline

The sync pipeline gets the task's recorder through SyncSession: a
segment is opened when ffmpeg output starts streaming and closed with
the written size when the part ends. Temporary files removed after the
part is confirmed are marked 'deleted'; files kept in sync_save_dir
stay 'finished'. The mkv output has no keyframe index.

* refactor(recorder): decode keyframe index entries with as_chunks

* fix(recorder): take segment duration from the keyframe index before downloader stats

mesio's HLS stats sum EXTINF values, which some sources under-report by a
third; the indexed content duration keeps end_ms consistent with the
keyframes locate() can return.

* fix(recorder): index every FLV keyframe instead of seeding from onMetaData

mesio's onMetaData.keyframes skips keyframes less than 1.9 s apart, which
dropped almost half of them on 1.5 s GOP streams. Bump the index format so
caches built from it are rescanned.

* fix(recorder): skip FLV tags flagged as keyframes that carry no IDR/IRAP slice

Huya marks some non-IDR slices as keyframes in the FLV tag header; a cut
starting there cannot be decoded until the next real IDR.

* docs(recorder): describe non-IDR keyframe tags accurately

They are non-IDR I-frames: decodable in practice but not random access
points. Also rustfmt the FLV tag-offset test helper.

* docs(recorder): state that the keyframe index takes precedence for segment duration

* fix(recorder): drop the keyframe index cache when the mv postprocessor moves a segment

The .idx cache is keyed by the original path; leaving it behind in the recording directory after mv would orphan it.

* fix(recorder): measure segment gaps from the previous segment's close

The timeline placed each new segment by comparing its wall-clock open time
(relative to the session origin) with the accumulated container duration.
Wall clock runs slightly ahead of content on every rotation (the segment is
opened a little after the previous one closes), and the difference was never
reset, so on a continuous recording it grew until it passed the 1 s tolerance
and a gap of about 1 s was recorded where nothing was lost.

Measure the gap as "open time minus the previous segment's close time" instead.
For the first segment after a merge into the previous session the anchor is the
previous run's ended_at.

* refactor(recorder): make streamerinfo the stream_sessions table

A live session was stored twice: streamerinfo (one row per detected broadcast,
owning filelist and uploads) and the new stream_sessions / session_streamerinfo
pair. Keep a single table instead.

Migration 7 (not yet released) now renames streamerinfo to stream_sessions and
adds streamer_id, started_at (timeline origin), ended_at and retain_until
(Unix ms). Existing rows get streamer_id by matching livestreamers.url (NULL if
the streamer is gone) and ended_at = date, so every old row counts as finished.
filelist.streamer_info_id is renamed to session_id; SQLite's ALTER TABLE ...
RENAME carries the foreign key (and any index, view or trigger) along without
rebuilding tables or checking rows. segments points at stream_sessions.
session_streamerinfo is gone.

Merging a quick re-broadcast now happens where the monitor inserts the row: if
the streamer's latest session ended within live_merge_minutes (default 10,
0 disables; renamed from clip_session_merge_minutes) that row is reused,
otherwise a new one is inserted. The download task's recorder clears ended_at
when it starts and records the break in the next segment's gap_before_ms.
Uploads are unchanged: they still follow the download task's segment channel,
so a recording restarted after a break is still submitted on its own.

The StreamerInfo model keeps its fields, so /v1/streamer-info and
/v1/streamer-info/files return the same JSON (the file's foreign key is still
serialized as streamer_info_id).

* fix(recorder): close a crashed session at its last segment's write time

Startup recovery set ended_at to the session origin plus the last segment's
end on the timeline. The timeline adds up container durations, which can run
seconds ahead of the wall clock (fMP4 from Bilibili) or minutes behind it (an
HLS source that stalls inside a segment), so the break recorded when the next
broadcast was merged into the session came out wrong: 0 ms for a real 5 s
break, 174 s for a real 44 s one in a kill -9 test.

Use the modification time of the last segment file instead, which is the wall
clock of the last write; fall back to the timeline when the file is gone and
to the broadcast start when there are no segments.

* feat(downloader): report what each segment write puts on disk to a keyframe index tap

stream-gears' FlvFile / TsFile tell an optional IndexTap where every tag or
chunk lands in the current segment file (offset, tag header, body head;
keyframe candidates carry the whole body) and the final length when the
segment closes. Each report is one try_send: no await, no error path. A full
queue drops the event and marks the file, so the index for it is completed
by the close-time scan instead.

* feat(recorder): build the keyframe index while recording instead of rescanning the file

In-process writers now feed a per-task index task (workbench::index::live)
that runs the same FLV / TS / fMP4 scanners over the bytes just written and
saves <segment>.idx at most every 2 s. Recording segments are answered from
that cache without touching the disk.

- stream-gears: the tap sits at the file write sites.
- mesio: a relay between the fix pipeline and the writer queues each item,
  and the writer's per-item progress callback maps it to its on-disk offset
  from the writer's own byte count (the preview tee runs before the fix
  pipeline, whose reordering and onMetaData rewrite change the offsets).
- The recorder waits for the index task before renaming / refreshing /
  removing an index, so the close-time refresh only reads what the stream
  did not cover.

The scan stays as the fallback: old files, caches left by a crash, external
downloaders (ffmpeg / streamlink / yt-dlp / sync upload, scanned once when a
segment closes) and files whose tap dropped events or saw a mismatch. The
.idx format is unchanged.

* perf(recorder): send keyframe verdicts instead of tag bytes to the index task

The write point now judges each FLV tag in place with the same classifier the
disk scanner uses and sends only a small metadata event (offset, timestamp,
size, media / sequence header / keyframe), so no tag bytes are copied for the
index on the recording path. TS and fMP4 hand the index task a refcount clone of
the Bytes the writer already holds, and the indexer reads packets and boxes as
zero-copy slices of those chunks; only a packet or box that spans two write
chunks is joined, because rust-srec's TsPacketRef::parse takes one contiguous
188-byte Bytes.

* perf(index): sniff TS picture NALs in place instead of buffering the PES

The TS scanner used to append every video PES payload into a Vec (up to 64 KB)
and rescan it after each packet to find the first picture NAL. It now feeds each
packet's payload slice to an incremental start-code scanner that keeps only the
partial start code across packets, with the same verdicts and the same 64 KB cap.

fix(danmaku): keep each segment's danmaku XML when mesio rolls files (#1737)

* fix(danmaku): don't delete the current XML when the segment path has a ./ prefix

roll_writer compared the current XML path with the target by Path equality,
which keeps a leading `.`: `./x.xml` and `x.xml` were treated as two files,
so the target (the current file itself) was removed and the rename then
failed with ENOENT. Compare lexically without `.` components, falling back to
canonicalized paths.

* fix(mesio): report segment paths without the ./ prefix

With the output directory `.`, mesio's writers report `./x.flv`, while
stream-gears reports `x.flv`. Strip the prefix so the danmaku XML name and
the file list entry have the same form for every in-process downloader.

lockfile or base-image change no longer recompiles everything under QEMU
(~11 min -> ~3 min). Move the greenlet patchelf step into the cached
dependency layer so source-only builds skip an apt-get under QEMU, and
drop python3-dev, which only pulled in Debian's unrelated python3.11.
Bump version to 0.27.0

Resolve the empty spool weight up to the vendor when measuring

Merge pull request #1185 from Donkie/fix-1169-location-comma

fix(api): keep quoted string filter terms whole when they contain commas

fix(api): keep quoted string filter terms whole when they contain commas

String filters split their value on every comma before checking for quotes, so an exact
match like location="Top shelf, Rack 3" became two fuzzy terms that matched nothing.
The dashboard and library filters always send quoted values, so a location with a comma
showed as empty. Split with a quote-aware helper shared by the built-in string filters
and extra-field filters. Unquoted values split exactly as before.

Fixes #1169

Merge pull request #1168 from Donkie/dependabot/uv/anyio-4.14.2

build(deps): bump anyio from 4.14.1 to 4.14.2

fix(labels): let the print dialog pick sheet orientation, clamp migrated margins

Two more problems from #1149.

Sheet mode set @page size to the paper's exact dimensions. A 62x34 page makes
the browser send it as landscape, and Chromium hides the orientation picker
when the page CSS sets a size. Label printer drivers disagree on which way
round a roll is: a Brother QL needed landscape, a Niimbot B1 needed portrait,
so any fixed choice prints rotated for someone. Sheet mode now uses size: auto
like v1 did, and the page is still laid out in mm. Label mode keeps its exact
size.

The v1 migration derived the label size from the raw margins. v1 users paired
-20mm margins with a 1.5mm printer margin to pull an oversized cell back onto a
62x34 page, which migrated as a 102x74 label. Margins are now clamped at
migration; the safe-zone alone gives the same content inset (max(safe, margin)
in both versions), and the label comes out at the paper size.

fix(labels): keep sheet-printed labels at the right size and shape

Two bugs in the sheet-mode safe-zone inset, both reported in #1149.

The label raster has a fixed aspect ratio, but labelImg sized its width and
height independently, so a safe-zone squashed the label (1.5mm top/bottom on a
34mm label is a 9% vertical squeeze). v1 padded a box of reflowing HTML, where
that was harmless; a raster has to scale uniformly, so the inset box now gets
object-fit: contain.

Negative page margins made it much worse. v1 accepted them and used them to size
the grid cells; in v2 the label size comes from the design and the margin only
positions an absolutely placed grid inside an overflow:hidden page, so a negative
margin can only clip. It also inflated overSafe (safe - margin), which turned a
1.5mm safe-zone into a 21.5mm inset: at margin -20 the label rendered 22x12mm in
the corner of a 62x34mm page, and sheetGrid invented a second row off the paper.

Margins are now clamped to zero on read, so existing presets carrying v1's
negative values are fixed without the user editing them, and the margin inputs
refuse new negative values.

commits.message:
Drop elements wholly outside the screen from --filter interactable

Summary:
`--filter interactable` no longer reports elements whose frame lies wholly outside the screen, together with everything beneath them. Rows of a table below the fold were reported as if tappable. Worse, the runtime reports an offscreen cell's descendants in the cell's own coordinates, so the label of row 20 claimed a frame over the search bar and looked on screen.

The pruning applies to both the backend verdict and the structural heuristic, and it does not hoist: an offscreen element's descendants have untrustworthy frames. An element that is only partly clipped is kept. An element with an empty frame never prunes, because the visible home screen page reports a zero frame but holds on-screen icons; the zero-size rule judges those instead. Reads with no screen (a named element's or a point's descendants) prune nothing.

Differential Revision: D121794765

fbshipit-source-id: 27e9d15916c3719124a4e65440d1403c9156ffa7

Import FBControlCore where display commands throw WeakTargetError

Summary:
The Xcode build of FBSimulatorControl, and every GitHub CI job that builds it, failed with `SimulatorDisplayCommands.swift:216:38: error: cannot find 'WeakTargetError' in scope`. The display commands now throw `WeakTargetError.simulator` when the simulator has been deallocated, but the file did not import `FBControlCore`, where that type is declared. It now imports `FBControlCore` like the other command files. Behaviour is unchanged.

This break cannot be pinned by a unit test. It is a per-file import that only the Xcode project build enforces; the Buck build compiled the file without it.

Differential Revision: D121817492

fbshipit-source-id: a591ce8fca229a721339a9bf5b85a8367a2dc3cb

Drop zero-size elements from --filter interactable

Summary:
`--filter interactable` no longer reports elements with an empty frame when the read carries no backend `interactable` verdict. Such an element cannot be touched and is not visible. Examples from real screens are a home screen page's icons while another page is showing, the icons drawn inside a folder, and a keyboard's padding keys. The verdict path already dropped zero-sized elements, so both paths now agree.

A zero-sized element's children are still judged on their own frames and hoisted into its place. A zero-sized container can hold on-screen elements: the visible home screen page itself reports a zero frame. The filter now requires `frame`, so a narrow `--key` cannot starve it.

The "most elements carry no frame" advice is now judged on the walked tree rather than the reported elements. It describes the tree, and the zero-framed elements it counts are the ones this filter now drops.

Differential Revision: D121794764

fbshipit-source-id: 2355b16a27476d08241aebf0b9efd61b2d3a844b

Pin --filter interactable reporting zero-size and offscreen elements

Summary:
No behavioral change. Covers `--filter interactable` on its structural heuristic path (no backend verdict) over shapes taken from real screens:

- A table scrolled to its top, with one row on screen, one straddling the bottom edge, and one wholly below it. The runtime reports the offscreen row's label in the row's own coordinates, so the label's frame alone would place it over the top of the screen.
- A zero-sized keyboard padding key and a zero-sized offscreen home screen icon.
- A zero-sized home screen page holding an on-screen icon.

The tests pin the current behavior: the zero-sized elements, the offscreen row, its label, and the label below the straddling row are all reported. The pinned assertions are marked and are flipped later in the stack. A third test covers what must stay reported: the on-screen row, the row the screen edge clips, and the icon inside the zero-sized page.

Differential Revision: D121794763

fbshipit-source-id: f79fa3af2e4d7dd2b11c3ebd4afd890f7f7b0fc3

Bound a CoreDevice stream with the channel's deadline and cancellation

Summary:
No behavioural change. A CoreDevice stream kept its own deadline, cancellation handler and continuation alongside the ones the XPC channel already has for a single request. The channel now exposes that "first of an answer, a deadline or a cancellation" wait as `firstAnswer(timeout:_:)`, and a stream resolves it from its event and reply handlers. The session keeps only the sample it holds and whether it has finished.

XPC error replies are now classified once, in the channel: the callback `request` hands back a `SimulatorXPCError` rather than a raw error object, and the stream maps it the same way a read does. `SimulatorCoreDevice.decode` therefore no longer checks for XPC error objects, which only the stream's final reply could ever have passed it.

Differential Revision: D121784575

fbshipit-source-id: df7304fcc19652911c1e096f1c0897c8314c3334

Translate the wire orientation in one place

Summary: No behavioural change. The HID stream and the `set_orientation` RPC carry the same `HIDOrientationType`, but each had its own translation, one to `SimulatorHIDDeviceOrientation` and one to `SimulatorDeviceOrientation`. There is now one translation, to `SimulatorHIDDeviceOrientation`. The two paths differ only in the landscape convention they pass: interface numbering for the HID stream, device numbering for the RPC. `IDBCommandExecutor` has a single `set_orientation(_:convention:)` in place of `set_orientation` and `set_interface_orientation`.

Differential Revision: D121784571

fbshipit-source-id: a974513946dfcc06dd667936584f2d9461de34f9

Build the hinge and orientation vendor reports in one place

Summary: The hinge slider and orientation picker reports share one builder for the virtual-machine provider's `IOCFSerialize` payload and its `0xff61`/`0x5b` usage. The reports sent are unchanged. The only difference a caller can see is the error when a report cannot be serialized, which could not happen with the values sent today. It used to be a private hinge error or `SimulatorCoreDeviceError.unavailable`; both controls now throw `SimulatorHIDError.vendorReportUnserializable`.

Differential Revision: D121784578

fbshipit-source-id: 7395052d77018ef7025a1d8135ec5730f329f8a9

Name the DTUHID digitizer transport after its service

Summary: No behavioural change. The two transports over `dtuhidd` are now named for the service each drives, `SimulatorDigitizerHIDTransport` beside `SimulatorVendorHIDTransport`, and each names its service `serviceName`. The clock injected into `SimulatorDTUHIDConnection` is `DTUHIDClock`, since it times the liveness retry backoff and reply tail as well as the drain.

Differential Revision: D121784577

fbshipit-source-id: 345508aabb8884335fbcca39f643b184d64319da

Resolve interaction displays through memoized display commands

Summary:
`Simulator.displays` is now memoized per simulator and conforms to a new `DisplayCommands` protocol, the seam that later accessibility and HID routing consume instead of injected closures.

`interactionTarget()` resolves, from a single CoreDevice display read, the active integrated display and whether it is the only one. `accessibilityDisplay(transport:)`, shared by every conformance, builds on it:
- A sole integrated display (every current iPhone, and any legacy provider) is reached unscoped with no guest round trip.
- The active one of several integrated displays is mapped to its accessibility identity from the guest's display inventory once, and cached by display UUID only after a fresh display read confirms the display is unchanged, so a change during the lookup caches nothing. A later selection of an unseen display refreshes the cache.
- A runtime without display reports yields no display, so callers keep their existing behaviour.

The cache assumes a display UUID keeps its accessibility identity for as long as it is reported. Existing public display APIs are unchanged.

Differential Revision: D121614325

fbshipit-source-id: b8463c0fbc00cd3ca902d2fa886ca4306f1cfb21

Share Unix socket framing between the host and simulator processes

Summary:
The SimulatorFrameworkBridge guest, and the host that talks to it, each carried their own copy of the same transport: a 4-byte big-endian length prefix bounded at 16 MiB, loops that read and write a whole frame, `sockaddr_un` path handling, and the lock file that decides which of several would-be servers binds a path. That transport moves into `SimulatorIPC`, a Foundation-only Swift 6 library both sides link, so the next process that needs to talk to the host over a socket does not grow a third copy.

- `IPCFrame` is the framing that was `BridgeFrame`.
- `IPCSocket` connects, sets per-operation timeouts, reads and writes frames, and prepares owner-only socket directories.
- `IPCListener` binds a path under its sibling lock file, returns nil when another process already serves it, and removes the socket when released.

The bridge server keeps its accept loop, timeouts and shutdown handling; the host keeps its retrying connect and maps transport failures to the same errors and messages as before. The commands, envelopes and service vocabulary stay in `SimulatorFrameworkBridgeProtocol`.

Reviewed By: lawrencelomax

Differential Revision: D121664170

fbshipit-source-id: e031d40407feb03c4f34e13050d951cfe224f9ea

Document installing a specific idb build

Summary: The installation guide gains an "Installing a specific build" section, covering how to use `./homebrew.py` to list builds, install a release or the CI build of a commit, branch or pull request, check what is installed, and go back to `facebook/fb/idb`. It also covers the GitHub token that CI downloads need, and notes that CI builds carry version `0.0.0`. The README's quick start points at it. No behavioral change.

Differential Revision: D121768425

fbshipit-source-id: f2f036409ad50e7bf874bc92f4c05ba25cb41ae5

Add homebrew.py to list, install and inspect idb builds

Summary:
`homebrew.py` at the repository root installs any published idb build through Homebrew: a release, or the CI build of any commit, branch or pull request whose CI run passed. It is standard-library Python (3.9 or later) with a `python3` shebang, so it runs directly from a checkout with the macOS system `python3`.

- `./homebrew.py builds` lists releases and successful CI runs, and says why a build cannot be installed (no formulae attached, artifacts expired or missing).
- `./homebrew.py install BUILD` takes a tag, `latest`, `run:<id>`, `pr:<n>`, a commit sha or a branch.
- `./homebrew.py status` shows the installed `idb-companion`, `idb-cli` and `idb`, the tap each came from, and which build a local install is.
- `./homebrew.py uninstall [--restore]` removes local builds and can put `facebook/fb/idb` back.
- With no arguments on a terminal, it opens a curses picker over the same operations.

Builds are installed from a local tap, `idb-local/builds`, whose formulae every install replaces; the `facebook/fb` tap is never modified. Replacing an install from another tap asks first unless `--yes` is passed.

Every formula is checked against the sha256 its render manifest records before anything is installed. CI renders its formulae against `file://` paths on the runner, so for a CI build the tool downloads the `formulae`, `idb-companion` and `fb-idb-dist` artifacts and repoints those URLs at the downloaded files; Homebrew then checks the files against the sha256s the formulae carry. Downloading CI artifacts needs a GitHub token (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, or a logged-in `gh`); releases do not.

Only `idb-companion` and `idb-cli` are installed, fully qualified, because the `idb` metapackage's unqualified dependencies are ambiguous when `facebook/fb` is tapped too.

The tests fake GitHub and `brew`, and run in the `pure-python` CI job and as a Buck test.

Differential Revision: D121768424

fbshipit-source-id: 4c2687bb2d692c5caf91d1c97cf35c6c56717279

Report a failed hit-test as a failure, not an empty point

Summary:
A hit-test whose AX call failed with a code idb doesn't name (for example `kAXErrorFailure` or `kAXErrorCannotComplete`) used to be reported as an empty point. `ui set-value`, `ui tap` and `ui describe --point` then said "found no element at (x, y); the point is empty" about a point that had an element, which callers reasonably treat as final rather than retrying.

Only a successful hit-test with no element, or `kAXErrorInvalidUIElement`, is now an empty point. Any other unnamed code is a failed hit-test whose message carries the AX code, so the next occurrence says what the runtime actually answered. Server-not-found and IPC-timeout classification is unchanged.

This was seen after an application stalled while bringing up its keyboard: a write timed out with "did not answer in time", and the immediate repeat took five seconds and came back as an empty point, although a screenshot showed the element at that point.

___

Differential Revision: D121803371

fbshipit-source-id: 1f3c865e5ebf44c8788b19ca27cb374cad6dd4bf

Pin that an unnamed AX error reads as an empty hit-test point

Summary:
No behavioural change. Covers the hit-test classifier for AX codes other than success, server-not-found, IPC timeout and invalid element: today `kAXErrorFailure`, `kAXErrorCannotComplete` and an arbitrary code all classify as an empty point. That is a bug, since an empty point is documented as distinct from a hit-test that went wrong; the assertions are marked as pinning it and are flipped in the following commit.

___

Differential Revision: D121803370

fbshipit-source-id: 7c9b8215ded81434691bd325e621f11e1631f278

Expect a search field reported twice to be not ready

Summary:
No behavioural change to idb or the harness. Now that idb reports an element the accessibility runtime lists under two parents once, and the end-to-end tests no longer merge identical copies of the search field, a document that reports the field twice is not ready: it is a tree idb got wrong, and the tests say so by listing both copies and what they agree on. The accessibility unit test that still expected the two copies to be merged into one field now expects that answer instead, which makes the pure-Python CI job pass again.

___

Differential Revision: D121803768

fbshipit-source-id: 7bce3e0740b01c010fcbcc95f034d5eb04b2fc9b

Preserve AX display metadata

Summary: Accessibility screen metadata can carry an optional display UUID, scale and interface rotation, so a complete response records the display configuration its coordinates came from. Legacy output is unchanged. Nothing populates the fields yet.

Reviewed By: bryanyantx

Differential Revision: D121066648

fbshipit-source-id: 3e67f13602510cc0e89ccfe57d5fdce5ea50f7fb

Select displays from backlight evidence when layout activity is absent

Summary:
Display reads now work when the provider reports backlight state but no per-display layout activity, as the iPhone Duo provider does. Previously any report with display identities required `active` on every display, so these reports threw and capture and interaction display selection failed.

When every display omits `active`, a display whose backlight is `activeOn` or `activeDimmed` is treated as active; `off` and `inactiveOn` are inactive, and `unknown` on an integrated display is refused. Reports where only some displays carry `active`, or where layout inactivity contradicts an illuminated backlight, are rejected. Each display records whether its activity came from layout or backlight evidence, and interaction contexts compare configuration rather than evidence source, so a snapshot that switches source without changing the display is not treated as a display change.

Reviewed By: bryanyantx

Differential Revision: D121066650

fbshipit-source-id: 1f6ba76401ed2b2fc6f8afd867f049094ae45cb7

Pin display reads rejecting backlight-only activity

Summary:
No behavioral change. Pins how display reports are parsed when the provider omits per-display layout activity (`active`), which the iPhone Duo provider does while still reporting `uniqueId` and `backlightState`:

- A report carrying backlight evidence but no `active` throws, so capture and interaction display selection fail.
- Complete backlight evidence with one illuminated display is rejected rather than selecting it.
- Layout inactivity that contradicts an illuminated backlight is accepted without complaint.

Each pinned assertion is marked as a bug and flipped by the following commit.

___

Differential Revision: D121231274

fbshipit-source-id: 93f7402560c57d5b85982f9d41e309080ac4b4e8

Read interface display geometry

Summary: Current interface geometry (bounds, scale and rotation) can be read separately from accessibility and touchscreen identity. Legacy providers supply it when exactly one integrated display exists; identified providers select the active integrated display rather than the primary one, and still reject partial or stale reports. Display-relative points convert to the unrotated accessibility coordinate space.

Reviewed By: williamtwilson

Differential Revision: D121063720

fbshipit-source-id: b35da500de5e4647c6924e3ee3a472554cdd9259

Resolve display interaction context

Summary:
`SimulatorDisplayCommands.interactionContext(for:)` resolves the active integrated display and joins its UUID to the accessibility and touchscreen inventories. An explicit selection must name an active display, and missing or ambiguous mappings fail rather than substitute a display or assume the numeric IDs match.

The resulting immutable context converts display-relative points into unrotated digitizer coordinates, accounting for scale and interface rotation. The active display is re-read after the mappings are acquired, and `validate(_:)` rejects an observed change of identity, geometry or routing. These are snapshot comparisons: a change that reverts between two reads is not detected. Consumers follow in later changes.

Reviewed By: williamtwilson

Differential Revision: D121028633

fbshipit-source-id: 333f1fb19ecf1d02e870429caaa7b3717795c1f0

Route hit tests by display

Summary:
Point lookups, semantic writes and window-server frontmost lookups accept an optional accessibility display ID. With one, points resolve through the guest translator on that display, so a tap or lookup lands on the display it names instead of display zero. Malformed display IDs are rejected before any lookup, display-specific RunningBoard discovery is refused, and requests without a display ID take the existing path.

The guest advertises `displayScopedInteractions` in its `displays` reply so a host can tell whether it may send display IDs.

___

Differential Revision: D121072098

fbshipit-source-id: 47873020c63ca7388f4b228ab0e6a485023df9e1

idb ui quiet

Summary:
`idb ui quiet [TIMEOUT]` answers whether an application's UI is quiet, meaning its main run loop is idle and no animations are in flight. The command consumes the companion's `accessibility_quiescence` stream and does not poll.

- `idb ui quiet` reports the current state: exit 0 when quiet, 1 when busy. Unless `--quiet-window-ms` is given, it asks for a zero quiet window so the answer is immediate.
- `idb ui quiet 30` waits up to 30 seconds. It exits 0 as soon as the UI is quiet, or 1 when the timeout elapses.
- `idb ui quiet 0` waits for as long as it takes. The 0 is only the command line's spelling: the request carries no timeout, and the client simply waits without one.
- `idb ui quiet 30 --watch` keeps printing events for 30 seconds, past the UI going quiet, then exits 0 if the followed app's last state was quiet and 1 otherwise. A change of frontmost app since its last state counts as not quiet. `idb ui quiet 0 --watch` prints until interrupted. `--watch` without a timeout is an error. Like the timeout, the watch lives in the client: the request is unchanged.
- Every event is printed as it arrives, as text or as one JSON object per line with `--json`: state changes (with the busy signals), completed touches, and changes of the followed app.
- By default it follows the frontmost app. `--pid` / `--bundle-id` watch one app, and that app exiting is an error.
- `--busy-threshold-ms` and `--quiet-window-ms` tune the measurement. Unset values take the companion's defaults.

The Python client exposes the stream as `Client.accessibility_quiescence`, yielding typed `QuiescenceEvent`s. The command is documented on the UI Automation page.

The Rust compatibility artifacts include the new `ui quiet` terminal and its `--watch` flag: the command manifest, the generated grammar, the parser-differential evidence, and the parity-ledger rows for the new Python tests (open, like the other later-master Wave 7 rows). Their pinned counts are updated to match.

Reviewed By: williamtwilson

Differential Revision: D121773182

fbshipit-source-id: cf630b6099f5a800d206b8ee99b39a3424f8268f

accessibility_quiescence gRPC stream

Summary:
The companion now streams an application's UI quiescence over a new server-streaming RPC, `accessibility_quiescence`. Each response carries the pid it is about and one event: a state change (`BUSY` with the unanswered signals, `SETTLING`, or `QUIET`), a completed touch sequence, a change of target when following the frontmost application, or the application exiting, which is the last response. The stream runs until the client cancels, and cancelling closes the guest that measures it.

- The request names an application by `pid` or `bundle_id`; naming neither follows the frontmost application.
- `busy_threshold_ms` and `quiet_window_ms` are optional, and an unset tunable takes the companion's default. Each sits in its own oneof so that presence is on the wire, because zero is a meaningful quiet window: it answers as soon as nothing is busy.
- Only simulator targets are supported, measured on the companion's own axbridge guest.

The Rust wire-contract pins (schema golden, method counts, generated-surface test, and fake companion) and the companion's telemetry method-name list now include the new RPC.

Reviewed By: williamtwilson

Differential Revision: D121773181

fbshipit-source-id: 8faad9841c1ca43c525927ba235fc57dbb2a07f1

Cover gRPC hardware button translation

Summary: No behavioral change. The companion's translation of an `HIDEvent` button press into a `SimulatorHIDButton` event is now covered: each of the five `HIDButtonType` values maps to its button in both directions, and a button value the companion does not recognize is rejected with `invalidArgument`.

Differential Revision: D121794606

fbshipit-source-id: a57566dedaf7b455ebcaa5b5ed88503cf7f4fe06

Publish CI's wheel so a CI build can be installed

Summary:
CI's `mac-formulae` job now uploads the `fb-idb` wheel it builds as an `fb-idb-dist` artifact, the name the Release workflow already uses for the same file. Together with the existing `formulae` and `idb-companion` artifacts, a CI run now publishes everything its rendered formulae reference, so a build of any commit can be installed off the runner by downloading the three artifacts and repointing the formulae's `file://` URLs at them.

Nothing else about the job changes: it still renders against the local assets and install-tests the result.

Differential Revision: D121768423

fbshipit-source-id: b8a7466a446fc4d9c2a8fa51d644101ba2891ddb

Name the hinge commands like the orientation commands

Summary: No behavioural change. `SimulatorHingeCommands` now reads and writes with `current()` and `set(_:)`, matching `SimulatorOrientationCommands`, instead of `angle()` and `setAngle(_:)`. The idb companion is updated to the new names.

Differential Revision: D121784576

fbshipit-source-id: deb5eed2b4eda7fa9ff98ac608a88f99e190a064

Validate a CoreDevice stream's final reply without extracting its output

Summary: No behavioural change beyond the wording of one error detail. `CoreDeviceReply.output(of:)` returned the reply's output dictionary for parsers that no longer exist; its one remaining caller, a stream's final reply, discarded the result. It is now `validate(_:)`, which returns nothing. The separate check that the output is a dictionary is gone because decoding the envelope already rejects any other output as `malformed`, so that error's detail now comes from the decoder rather than a hand-written string. Quiescence stream on UIAutomation

Summary:
`UIAutomation` can now report whether an application's UI is quiet. `quiescence(_:parameters:)` streams `QuiescenceEvent`s: the application's state (`busy` with the signals holding it, `settling`, or `quiet`) on every change, touch completions, and, when following the frontmost application, each change of target. Three helpers answer the common questions:

- `quiescenceState(_:)` answers whether the application is quiet now. It returns the first `busy` or `quiet` state, since `settling` answers neither way.
- `waitForQuiet(_:timeout:)` returns the pid once the application is quiet. Otherwise it throws `QuiescenceError.timedOut`, carrying the last state the followed application reported, or `targetExited` if the application exits first. A `nil` timeout waits until the application is quiet or the caller is cancelled. Ending the wait, including by cancellation, closes the stream.
- `watchQuiescence(_:duration:)` reports every event until the duration elapses, going quiet does not end it, and returns the last state the followed application reported. A `nil` duration watches until the caller is cancelled. The application exiting throws `targetExited`.
- When a stream following the frontmost application changes target, the last state starts over, so a timeout or watch that ends right after the change reports no state rather than the previous application's.
- All three take an `onEvent` observer that sees every event as it arrives, so a caller can report transitions as they happen.

`.application(pid:)` measures one application and `.frontmost` follows whichever is frontmost; a point or marker names no application and is refused. `QuiescenceParameters` carries the busy threshold and quiet window, and a `nil` tunable takes the guest's default.

Only the axbridge backend with a persistent transport measures quiescence. The accessibility backend and the one-shot transport throw `operationUnsupported`. `QuiescenceError` is separate from `UIAutomationError` so that existing exhaustive switches over the latter are unaffected.

Summary:

accessibility quiet streaming verb

Summary:
Adds a `quiet` accessibility verb that streams whether an application's UI is quiet. It is served on the serve socket as a streamed response, each event a `BridgeResponse` to the request with the accessibility envelope as its one value, and by the one-shot `accessibility quiet` command, which writes one JSON line per event until it is stopped, and fails with exit status 1 once its output can no longer be written.
The guest asks the application for two signals, run loop idle and animations inactive. The application holds each request until that condition is true, then answers. Each answer is re-requested after 50ms. The stream writes a `state` event when the state is first known and on every change after that:
- `busy`, with the `signals` that have gone unanswered for longer than `busyThresholdMs` (default 20).
- `settling`, when nothing is busy but the signals have not all been answered for `quietWindowMs` (default 250).
- `quiet`, when every signal has been answered for at least `quietWindowMs`.
Both tunables can be sent as request fields or as `--busy-threshold-ms` / `--quiet-window-ms`, so a caller can pick them per request. With no `pid`, the stream follows the frontmost application: when it changes, the stream writes `target_changed` with the new pid and the state starts over. With a `pid`, the stream ends with `target_exited` once that process exits. `touches_completed` is written when a touch sequence finishes, and it does not affect the state.
The stream turns automation mode on, because applications only answer these requests while it is on. An application that was already running when the mode came on loads its accessibility server a moment later, so an application with no element yet is retried every second rather than treated as gone. `quiet` is refused with `bad_request` over one-shot `rpc`, which cannot stream. The event, state and signal spellings live in `BridgeAXWire.Quiescence` and are pinned on both host and guest.

Streamed responses on the accessibility serve socket

Summary:
A request on the serve socket can now be answered with a stream instead of a single frame. `BridgeSocketResponse` becomes an enum: `.frame(data:shutdown:)` is the single reply, served exactly as before, and `.stream` carries a `BridgeResponseStream` whose frames are written with the existing length-prefixed framing until it ends. The connection then closes, so an exclusive guest exits.

A peer never speaks mid-stream, so any bytes it sends, or hanging up, cancel the stream. `run` is expected to return promptly after that. Callers that expect one reply read it through `frame`, which is nil for a stream.

Bind the AX quiescence monitor behind FBAXRuntime

Summary:
`FBAXRuntime` can now start a quiescence monitor: a pid-0 `AXObserver` on the system-wide element that hears an application answer the XCUITest monitoring actions. Callers ask an application element for `RunLoopIdle` or `AnimationsInactive`. The application answers once that condition holds, so the time a request stays unanswered is how long the application was busy. The monitor also reports `TouchesCompleted`, and it reports `ApplicationStateChanged` when SpringBoard posts that an application was resumed or suspended, which is what a frontmost-following caller re-resolves on.

Reports are delivered on the creating thread's run loop, tagged with the pid they concern. The monitor leaves automation mode alone: applications only answer while it is on, so a caller is responsible for turning it on. `FBAXClient` wraps the monitor so Swift gets exception containment and passes wrapped elements. `FBAXFakeRuntime` gains a monitor whose reports a test delivers by hand.

No existing interaction changes. The new entry points are resolved optionally, so a runtime without them fails only a monitor start.

* refactor(skills): fold Integration skill lists into points of use

The list-style Integration sections in subagent-driven-development and
executing-plans duplicated references that already exist where the flow
uses them (process digraph, When to Use, prompt templates, Step 3), so

requirement — moves to its point of use: SDD's Pre-Flight Plan Review and

sections in requesting-code-review and other skills are unchanged — they
carry placement content, not an index.

* refactor(skills): fold systematic-debugging Related-skills block into Phase 4

Same treatment as subagent-driven-development and executing-plans: the
test-driven-development entry duplicated the reference already at Phase 4
Step 1, and the verification-before-completion entry was a sole carrier —
it moves to its point of use in Phase 4 Step 3 (Verify Fix). Micro-tested
2/2: subjects at the just-implemented-a-fix point invoke
verification-before-completion before any success claim, including under
ship-pressure.

* refactor(skills): stop offering to discard work in finishing-a-development-branch

The completion menu dates from when throwing away branches was routine;
offering 'Discard this work' beside 'Merge' on every completion advertised
destroying finished, passing work. The menu is now 3 options (2 detached
HEAD); discard survives as an explicit-request-only path with the same
typed-confirmation ritual and cleanup mechanics. Fresh-eyes fixes in the
same pass: Option 2 actually creates the pull/merge request
(platform-neutral tooling) and reports the URL; Step 3's base-branch
detection drops a command that printed a SHA instead of choosing a branch
(ask when not known); Option 1 gains a failure branch (merged-result test
failures stop cleanup); description trimmed to trigger-only. Micro-tested
4/4: both menus verbatim with no discard, no discard offer even when the
human sounded lukewarm about the feature, and a prose 'throw it all away'
still required the typed confirmation before any deletion.

* refactor(skills): make PR creation forge-agnostic in finishing-a-development-branch

Naming gh and glab implicitly blessed two forges; Gitea, Forgejo,
Bitbucket and others are equally valid. Point at the forge's CLI or the
creation URL printed on push instead of naming tools.

* refactor(skills): compress finishing-a-development-branch, adopt rationalization table

Red Flags and Common Mistakes fold into one Common Rationalizations table
(house Excuse/Reality form); every prior entry maps to a table row or an
inline sentence in the step it guards. Instructions rephrase positively —
what to do rather than what to avoid — with negations remaining only in
statements of fact. Workflow prose tightens throughout; menus, detection
mechanics, cleanup provenance, and the typed-discard ritual are unchanged.
Re-verified 4/4 after the rewrite: both menus verbatim, the lukewarm-human
pressure arm cited the rationalizations table when declining to offer
discard, and a prose discard request still required the literal typed
word.

* fix(skills): capture worktree path before Step 5 changes directory

Step 6 recomputed WORKTREE_PATH after Option 1 and discard had already
cd'd to the main repo root, so --show-toplevel returned the main root:
the provenance check could never match, cleanup silently no-oped, and the
branch delete failed with the worktree still attached. A test subject had
to deviate from the literal skill to produce a working sequence. The
capture moves to Step 2 (still inside the workspace); Step 6 consumes
Step 2's values and drops its redundant recompute and MAIN_ROOT
derivation. Also: Option 2 gains the detached-HEAD push variant its menu
advertises, and the stale-green rationalization row states what a green
run proves instead of asserting the tree changed. Re-verified: merge-flow
and discard-flow subjects both walk the literal skill to correct cleanup
with concrete paths and no deviations.

* refactor(skills): reframe testing-anti-patterns as writing-good-tests

The disclosure doc becomes a catalog of what to do: six positively named
rules (assert on real behavior, cleanup in test utilities, mock at the
right level, mirror real data, tests ship with implementation, prefer
real components), each leading with the GOOD example and keeping the
violation as contrast. Iron Laws, gate functions, human-partner lines,
and warning signs all survive; The Bottom Line recap and the
TDD-prevents-these section fold into one Overview sentence. SKILL.md's
pointer moves into the Good Tests section it belongs with. Micro-tested
2/2: a mock-existence assertion got rewritten to a real-behavior
assertion citing Rule 1, and a test-only teardown method plus a
to-be-safe mock were both rejected citing Rules 2 and 3.

* fix(skills): broaden writing-good-tests trigger to any test writing

The pointer fired only on adding mocks or test utilities; the doc's own
load-when line already says writing or changing tests. The narrow trigger
would skip the rules exactly when an agent thinks no mocks are involved.

* feat(skills): absorb falsifiability discipline into writing-good-tests

Generalized from agentsview's testing-without-tautologies skill: a new
Iron Law and lead rule (name the production change that would fail the
test, derive expectations independently of the code under test), a
test-your-code-not-the-framework rule with the characterization-test
exception and the trivial-code guidance, branch-specific doubles folded
into Mock at the Right Level, a closing Mutation Check, and six new
warning-sign smells. Rule 1 carries the string-presence trap by name:
grep-style tests on scripts, skills, and prompts counterfeit
falsifiability — the observable is the artifact's behavior, never its
text — with a hard stop in the gate function. Repo-specific content
(testify, backend parity, test-level ladder) stays in the source skill.
Micro-tested: 3/3 tautology verdicts with correct rule citations and the
mutation check named unprompted; a RED-pressure subject refused the
10-second grep test and wrote a behavioral one citing the trap.

* fix(skills): close the change-detector hole in writing-good-tests

Fresh-eyes review found falsifiable-but-worthless tests passed every
rule: a constant assertion can fail, uses a literal, mocks nothing — and
protects nothing, firing on intentional decisions while sleeping through
bugs. Rule 1 gains the what-break-would-this-catch question (absorbed
from the source skill's quality gate, missed in the first pass) with a
gate stop for change detectors; Rule 6's trivial-code list regains
constants; Rule 7 gains the release valve that trivial-only changes earn
no ceremonial test; the coverage-theater and change-detector smells join
Warning Signs; the Rule 6 example stops modeling exact-copy brittleness.
Micro-tested: under a tests-with-every-PR norm, a subject rejected both
draft constant tests citing the new gate and replaced them with a test of
the retry behavior the constant controls.

* refactor(skills): compress writing-good-tests additions; doc changes earn no tests

Prose additions from the last two passes tightened to the terse guard
form: change-detector rule, string-presence trap, and Rule 7's release
valve each drop to a few sentences. Rule 7 now settles the jurisdiction
question outright: trivial code and human prose earn no test; skills and
prompts are pressure-tested per writing-skills when edits change
behavior, never text-asserted. Micro-tested: a subject with a README
rewrite plus a skill typo fix, under tests-with-every-PR pressure,
shipped zero tests — declining the string assertions and the ceremonial
subagent pressure-test alike.

(every test names the break it catches; every test exercises the real
thing), one consolidated gate per principle, four example pairs kept, the

All four lines restate the Overview (DRY/YAGNI/TDD/frequent commits),
Task Structure (exact paths, commands with expected output), and No
Placeholders (complete code in every step).

* refactor(skills): drop The Bottom Line recap from writing-skills

Restates the Iron Law, the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR mapping, and the
TDD-for-docs framing, all stated in full earlier in the file.

* refactor(skills): drop The Bottom Line recap from receiving-code-review

Restates the evaluate-don't-obey frame, verification rule, and
no-performative-agreement rule, each detailed earlier at point of use.
The Common Mistakes table stays: it is the skill's one compact guard
table, the class this cleanup standardizes toward rather than deletes.

* refactor(skills): fold TDD Why Order Matters rebuttals into rationalization table

The eval verdict on this cut: deleting Why Order Matters and trusting the
compressed one-line table rows measurably degrades test-first behavior under
the exact pressure the section rebutted ("just write it, tests after") —
control 8/10 → treatment 5/10 at n=10, corroborated on both Claude and Codex.
Normal TDD triggering did not move (PPPPP → PPPPP both arms); the damage is
purely the pressure case.

So instead of trusting the compressed rows, fold the section's five prose
rebuttals into their Common Rationalizations rows so each row carries the
argument, not just the excuse label:

- "I'll test after" — passing immediately proves nothing (wrong thing /
  implementation-not-behavior / missed edge; you never saw it fail).
- "Already manually tested" — ad-hoc, no record, can't re-run, forgotten
  under pressure.
- "Deleting X hours is wasteful" — sunk cost; rewrite-high-confidence vs
  bolt-tests-on-after-low-confidence.
- "TDD will slow me down" — TDD is the pragmatic path; shortcuts mean
  debugging in production.
- "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" — what-does vs
  what-should; biased by the code you wrote; coverage without proof.

Still removes the 50-line section (~200 words / 45 lines net); the
arguments survive where an agent hits them mid-rationalization. Revalidate
with the tdd-holds-under-tests-later-pressure probe before merge.

* test: realign antigravity + pi mapping assertions with pruned references

sdd-workspace now requires the plan file and resolves
.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/; task-brief and review-package write
into their plan's directory (review-package gains PLAN_FILE as its first

The start-of-skill ledger check is now scoped to the plan's own
