commits.message:
Merge pull request #1477 from twmb/kgo-share-fixes

kgo: share consumer fixes (#1474 and an audit)

kgo: treat GROUP_ID_NOT_FOUND on leave as success

Kafka answers a leave heartbeat for a missing group with
GROUP_ID_NOT_FOUND. Leaving is done once the member is out of the group,
so this is success, as UNKNOWN_MEMBER_ID already was. This applies to
share groups and KIP-848 consumer groups.

kgo: fix share loop wakeups and ack sends

ResumeFetchTopics and ResumeFetchPartitions woke each source with
maybeConsume, which starts the classic fetch loop. A share client has no
consumer session, so that loop exits at once, and a share loop that had
stopped with every partition paused never fetched again until something
else woke it. maybeConsume now starts the share loop for a share client.

The share loop could also stop for good in two other ways. A ShareFetch
given up on at its MaxWait+5s deadline returned with nothing left to
restart the loop; we now reset the session, whose connection is gone,
and keep looping. And the ack timer could exit the loop while a fetch
was buffered, so nothing fetched after the poll took it; like the
classic loop, we now exit only through the request path.

Every ack signal restarted the 1s ack timer. MarkAcks signals on every
call, so calling it more often than once a second while no fetch ran
sent nothing. The timer now starts with the first pending ack and later
acks do not push it back. With nothing to fetch, the loop also spun
after sending the acks until the timer fired; it now stops the timer.

A ShareFetch lists a partition we no longer fetch when it carries that
partition's acks. The broker adds every listed partition to the session
before removing the forgotten ones, so it acquired records for that
partition that we discarded. We now forget it in the same request, as
Java does.

Closing a session built ack ranges only when a user ack was live, so gap
acks alone were dropped, and closing the session released those offsets
rather than archiving them.

kgo: send share acks and an empty subscription on a topic purge

Purging a topic failed its queued acks with errShareConsumerLeft and
dropped its gap acks, so records you had processed were redelivered
after their locks expired. Java still sends acks for partitions that
left the subscription. Purged acks now wait on the source and go out
with its next request, under the new cursor if the topic is consumed
again by then; if the consumer is leaving, they fail as before.

With every topic purged, the heartbeat sent a null SubscribedTopicNames,
which the broker reads as unchanged, so the member stayed assigned. If
the member was then fenced, rejoining with a null list failed with
INVALID_REQUEST forever. We now send an empty list, and at epoch 0 with
no topics we wait to join until topics are added.

kgo: keep the share session's connection active

The broker ties a share session to the connection that opened it and
releases every record the member acquired when that connection closes.
ShareAcknowledge went on another connection, so a consumer that held
records and renewed them without polling left the fetch connection idle,
and our ConnIdleTimeout or the broker's connections.max.idle.ms closed
it, releasing records the user was still processing. ShareAcknowledge
now uses the fetch connection, as with Java's single connection per
broker, so acks and renews keep it active. The ShareGroup docs now say
to ack or renew held records within ConnIdleTimeout.

A ShareFetch's read deadline also ignored MaxWait, so a FetchMaxWait
above RequestTimeoutOverhead (10s by default) timed out the long poll
and closed the connection the same way. It now includes MaxWait, as a
Fetch's does.

kgo: send share acks for a partition in offset order

A share fetch acquires transaction markers, and we ack each acquired
offset that has no record as a gap. buildAckRanges sorted user acks and
gaps separately and appended every gap after every user ack, so a marker
between two records gave batches like [0-1 accept] [3 accept] [2 gap].
Kafka requires a partition's batches in ascending offset order and
rejects the whole partition with INVALID_REQUEST otherwise. We now merge
gaps into the user acks by offset, as Java does.

Each offset also now goes out once. A gap could overlap a user ack or
another gap for the same offset (the offset was redelivered, or a
requeued gap was acquired again), which Kafka rejects the same way.

kgo: wrap the share session epoch and track session resets

Kafka wraps the share session epoch from MaxInt32 to 1; we overflowed to
a negative epoch, which the broker rejects. We also marked acks stale by
comparing their stamped epoch to the current one, which misfires at the
wrap and misses stale acks once a new session passes the old epoch.
Acks are now stamped with a counter that increments on every session
reset.

Merge pull request #1473 from twmb/perf-patch

kgo: produce and consume performance, and bugs found along the way

kgo: default MaxBufferedRecords to 50,000

Records stay buffered until their produce response arrives. With 100
byte records, one 1MB batch holds about 10,000 records, so the old
default of 10,000 let the client buffer about one batch, and a
goroutine producing as fast as it can blocked once per request.
Against kfake, 100 byte records:

  limit    one producer    50 clients, acks=0
  10,000   3.38M rec/s     15.5M rec/s
  50,000   3.98M           13.7M

10,000 100 byte records is about 1MB; 50,000 is still only about 5MB.

kgo: surface fetch responses larger than BrokerMaxReadBytes

A broker returns the first record batch of a fetch even when it exceeds
the fetch limits, and a topic's max.message.bytes may allow a batch
larger than BrokerMaxReadBytes. We rejected the response, killed the
connection, and fetched again, forever: the partitions stalled with
only a warning in the logs, and PollFetches returned nothing.

We now also return the error from PollFetches, as a single error on
topic "" partition -1, and keep retrying with backoff. The error wraps
"response exceeds BrokerMaxReadBytes" so it names the option to raise.

kfake: bound synthetic fetch responses by MaxBytes

A synthetic fetch appended at least one batch for every partition, even
once the response had used up the request's MaxBytes, so fetching 200
partitions of one megabyte batches returned a 200MB response. The
client rejects a response that large and retries forever.

Like a broker, we now return nothing more for a partition once the
response has no room for a batch; only the first batch we return may
exceed the limits.

kgo: fail produced records the broker cannot take any version of

When a broker supports no produce version we can issue, the request
fails with errBrokerTooOld before it is written. We treated that like
any other client error and retried the request, and with the default
unlimited retries, records never failed: ProduceSync hung forever. A
client pinned below Kafka 4.0's minimum produce version (v3) hits this
against 4.0+.

We now fail the request's records with the error, as the Java client
fails a batch on UnsupportedVersionException. The request was never
written, so failing its batches keeps sequence numbers consistent; a
batch that an earlier attempt may have produced still goes through the
normal retry path.

kgo: allow five idempotent produce requests in flight

The sink started with a capacity 1 inflight sem and, on the first
response from a produce v4+ broker, stored a new capacity 4 one. A
request holding the old sem could still be in flight while four took
the new one, so we stopped at four to never exceed Kafka's five.

We now create one capacity 5 sem with four slots filled, and
firstRespCheck frees them. Only one request is in flight until then,
so it runs once, and the sem can never admit more than five. Kafka's
broker keeps the last five batches per producer and partition to
deduplicate retries, and we put at most one batch per partition in a
request.

kgo: decode fetched records straight into Records

We decoded each record batch into a slice of kmsg.Records, allocating a
Headers slice for each record with headers, and then copied every one
into a Record, throwing the kmsg.Records away.

We now decode straight into Records, reading the fields as
kmsg.Record's decoder does. PoolKRecords pooled the kmsg.Records, which
no longer exist, so it is deprecated and unused.

Decoding a 1MB batch of 100 byte records went from 75ns to 58ns per
record without headers, 187ns to 126ns with two headers, and 288ns to
203ns with five, allocating about 40% fewer bytes. Consuming from one
broker went from 8.73M to 9.49M records/s using 12% less CPU; with 8
and 32 clients, 9% and 19% more, using 18% less CPU.

kgo: do not panic on an overflowing record length varint

kbin.Varint reports an overflowing varint as a negative count of bytes
read, as binary.Varint does. readRawRecordsInto only rejected a count
of zero, so a record whose length varint overflowed made total
negative and in[:total] panicked in the fetch goroutine. A broker bug
or corruption that CRC validation misses, or with CRC validation
disabled, could crash the consumer.

We now stop decoding the batch there, as for any other truncated
record.

kgo: buffer without partsMu for partitioners without OnNewBatch

doPartition held the topic's partsMu across bufferRecord, so every
goroutine producing to a topic buffered one at a time. Holding it
matters for a partitioner with OnNewBatch (KIP-480): it chooses again
when the record would start a new batch, and that choice must see the
batch it aborted on. A partitioner without OnNewBatch, including the
default UniformBytesPartitioner, is not called again after
bufferRecord, and partsMu guards only its state.

For those, we now release partsMu before buffering. The partitioner
sees and updates its state under the lock as before, so its choices
are unchanged, and a goroutine's records still buffer in the order it
produced them.

With one client and 100 byte records, two goroutines producing went
from 4.65M to 5.08M records/s, four from 3.58M to 4.14M, and eight
from 2.92M to 3.24M.

kgo: stamp produced records before taking any lock

We read the clock for a record without a timestamp in bufferRecord,
while holding the topic's partsMu and the partition's recBuf.mu.
partsMu serializes every goroutine producing to a topic, and time.Now
was about a third of the time spent holding it.

We now stamp and truncate the record at the start of produce, which is
where every record we buffer starts. The timestamp is when
Produce was called rather than when the record was buffered, which for
a topic whose metadata is still loading is earlier, and
OnProduceRecordBuffered hooks now see it.

With one client and 100 byte records, two goroutines producing went
from 3.79M to 4.41M records/s, four from 3.03M to 3.39M, and eight
from 2.70M to 2.99M; one goroutine was unchanged.

kfake: read and write connections inline, buffering reads

Each request started a goroutine to read it and each response started
one to write it, only so the read and write loops could select on the
cluster dying. Reading a request also took two reads, the size and
then the body, each its own syscall.

A goroutine per connection now closes it when the cluster dies, which
returns the loops from a blocked read or write, and the loops do their
I/O inline. Reads go through a 4KiB bufio.Reader, so a small request's
size and body usually arrive in one read.

With one producer sending two records per acks=1 ProduceSync, the
cluster went from 38.7K to 40.4K records/s; with fifty, from 184K to
196K.

kgo: buffer connection reads

We read every response with two reads, the four byte size and then the
body, and each was its own syscall. A 4KiB bufio.Reader per connection
lets a small response's size and body arrive in one read. Once the
buffer is empty, bufio reads a large response directly into the
response slice, so fetches pay no extra copy.

Produce responses are about 33 bytes per partition, so 4KiB covers a
produce request spanning about 120 partitions. One producer with acks=1
sending two records per ProduceSync went from 40.8K to 41.5K records/s
against kfake; consuming was unchanged.

kgo: grow worker stacks before the request path

Our request and response workers exit when their queue drains, so a
producer sending one small request at a time starts new ones for every
request. Each starts with the minimum stack and grew it midway through
serializing and compressing the request, copying and adjusting every
frame above it: 2us of a 3us request serialization.

Each worker now grows its stack first, while it has one frame, with a
4KiB local. 4KiB and 8KiB measured the same; 16KiB was slower. One
producer with acks=1 sending two records per ProduceSync went from 37.1K
to 39.9K records/s against kfake.

kgo: read and write on the calling goroutine

writeConn and readConn each started a goroutine to run the blocking
Write or Read, only so the caller could select on the request and
client contexts. Every request paid two goroutine starts and two
handoffs for it.

We now do the I/O inline. Closing the client sets the connection's
deadline to now through a context.AfterFunc registered once per
connection; die stops it. A cancelable request context, other than the
client context, gets its own AfterFunc per read or write, which we stop
when the I/O returns, waiting out a callback that already fired before
we reset the deadline.

kgo: allocate once for the first fetch in PollRecords

Every PollRecords call that returned records allocated three slices:
the Fetches, the first Fetch's Topics, and that topic's Partitions.
We now take all three from one pollOne allocation, so in the likely
common case of taking one or a few records, the fetch costs only one
alloc.

Polling one record at a time, as xk6-kafka does, went from 3.63M to
3.89M records/s against kfake.

commits.message:
release: prepare V4.5.0

Sets both version fields to 4.5.0 and writes the release notes for the
search, font, settings and iPhone work since 4.3.2.

fix: stop iPhone rewriting notes on open and tidy what it shows

Opening a note rewrote it unchanged: the loaded text reached onChange
after the loading flag had cleared, so an autosave ran 800ms later,
bumping the modified date, reordering Recent and re-uploading to iCloud.
Saving now compares against the text the file holds.

The iCloud catalog skipped none of the folders the disk walk skips, so
the library's Trash leaked into Recent, All Notes, search and wikilinks.
GBK notes loaded forever behind the skeleton; they now decode through
GB18030, and a note that cannot be read shows an error instead.

Several labels bypassed the string catalog and showed English to Chinese
readers; they take localized keys now and the missing zh-Hans entries
are added. Inline and quoted code keep the text face as on macOS, and a
block that loses its closing fence drops the code font in the editor.

Card previews no longer fall back to a full read when the first 900
bytes end mid-character, long frontmatter no longer leaks into cards or
snippets, frontmatter follows the reader's rule, and search snippets
clean only a window around the hit.

fix: tighten letter spacing to one 0.02em figure

The preview's 0.04em, the editor's fixed 0.5pt kern and the interface's
0.6pt were set in 2022 around LXGW WenKai, a tight face, and never
revisited through two default-font changes. On PingFang, and on Latin in
any face, they spread words apart. All three now come from one ratio of
the font size, 0.02em, so the editor, lists and preview track alike and
change together.

fix: make TsangerJinKai02 the default face again without bundling it

4.3.0 stopped bundling TsangerJinKai02 because redistributing it needs
a licence, and moved every saved selection to PingFang. The face stays
unbundled, but it is the default by name again for new installs, with
PingFang rendering until it is installed. Stored font choices are left
exactly as they are: no migration touches a text face any more, and a
face that is missing at read time is no longer overwritten with the
default, which is how a font that activated late came back as PingFang.

When a chosen face is installed while MiaoYan runs, the editor, preview
and interface switch to it without a restart. Picking the not-installed
row keeps the choice, and the button downloads the foundry's own .ttf
directly instead of opening its product page.

fix: move note search matching off the main thread

Search ran on the main thread end to end, compared text before checking
the selected folder, matched every note twice, and lowercased whole
bodies on each keystroke. It now filters by scope first and hands plain
candidates to a detached matcher that reads unloaded bodies from disk,
so the list updates without blocking typing. Titles are matched without
the .md extension, so a lone dot no longer matches every note, and the
preview find bar escapes its query instead of running it as a regex.

fix: tidy the settings window layout

Controls ended on five different right edges, a fixed 164pt label column
pushed short Chinese labels towards the middle and cut Spanish ones,
every page sat in the same 520pt window, and the font page was titled
编辑. The label column now fits the widest label across all pages,
every control ends on one edge, rows are grouped with hairlines, the
window fits each page, and the categories read General, Editor and
Fonts. Always on Top is a switch instead of an unlabeled checkbox, and
the shortcut field uses the segmented controls' fill.

fix: follow the text font for code and restore the preview weight The code font defaulted to Menlo and reached inline code, quoted code and, in the editor, raw HTML tags such as , so a paragraph could switch faces mid-line and typing beside a tag re-highlighted the whole paragraph as code. Code now follows the text font by default, the code font applies to fenced code blocks only, and HTML tags are colored without a font change or the code-block mark. A stored Menlo was written by an earlier migration rather than chosen, so it moves to the new default. The V4.3.1 font batch also thinned the preview: body smoothing went to antialiased and TsangerJinKai02 bold was swapped for its W05 face. Both are back to the 4.3.0 rendering.

refactor: keep project facts in AGENTS.md and drop the skill mirrors

The five project skills restated generic Swift review, lint commands,
and release rules that AGENTS.md already holds, and saw one or two uses
in 28 days. Their few project-only facts (altool validation, the release
notes structure, the signed-ZIP rule, MiaoYanMobile checks) now live in
AGENTS.md, which every runtime reads. With no skills left, the mirror
sync script and its test have nothing to guard.

commits.message:
fix(optix): Allow LLVM to choose the PTX ISA version. (#2166)

LLVM's NVPTX backend selects the minimum PTX ISA version required by the
configured CUDA target architecture. Do not force PTX 5.0, which is invalid
for newer targets such as sm_75.

Assisted-by: OpenAI Codex / GPT-5

Signed-off-by: Tim Grant <tgrant@nvidia.com>

build: sync dependency_utils.cmake with OpenImageIO (#2170)

Brings src/cmake/dependency_utils.cmake up to date with OIIO main, so
the file is now identical except for the license header. From OIIO PRs
5128, 5205, 5314, 5361, 5362, 5394, 5410, and 5423:

* checked_find_package() uses its own "_cfp" argument prefix, and
  saves its parsed arguments per package. So when a local build script
  calls checked_find_package() for its own dependencies, it no longer
  clobbers the outer call's arguments.
* Before re-finding a locally built package, clear the stale cached
  library, include, and _DIR variables left by a rejected system
  install.
* Log the configure, build, and install output of each local build to
  deps/<pkg>-build.log. Fail right away if a step fails. If the re-find
  fails, show the install dir contents and the tail of the log.
* Fix the include path for local deps (dist/include), and fix how git
  clone errors are captured and reported.
* New GIT_SUBMODULES argument for build_dependency_with_cmake().
* Pass CMAKE_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH on to dependency child builds.
* Minor: clearer error message when tag verification fails, quote the
  version in the RECOMMEND_MIN test, and drop a cmake 3.19 check that
  is always true.

Assisted-by: Claude Code / Claude Opus 5.5

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>

build: Fix Makefile wrapper to properly quote test regex (#2168)

Port of OpenImageIO PR 5146. Quote the TEST regex passed to ctest -R,
so that regexes containing shell metacharacters (like `|`) work as
expected with `make test TEST=...`.

Signed-off-by: Larry Gritz <lg@larrygritz.com>
